Property Value Method native-oidc SSO Yes Group Access Group Admin Access Group users_immich Admin Group admin_immich Subdomain photos

Auth Notes

Full OIDC with auto-register and auto-launch; password login is disabled while OIDC is configured. Storage quota and role come from the instance settings as the token claims immich_quota (GiB, -1 = unlimited) and immich_role: members of the admin group are Immich administrators (privileged setting), and Immich re-reads both at every sign-in. Trash days and machine learning are rendered into config.json at every start. Identity: OAuth users are keyed on the OIDC sub. Immich also links a login to an existing user with the same email and cannot be told not to, while LLDAP emails are user-editable; so on every start a one-shot job (immich-lock-local-users) gives local, unlinked users (such as the initial admin@portcullis.local) a placeholder OAuth id, and Immich then refuses the email link. Do not create local users in the Immich UI (they are only locked at the next restart); let users sign in with SSO instead. A user who unlinks OAuth in their settings is locked out of SSO until an admin clears the placeholder. Public exceptions (Hub, off by default): shared links still work for signed-in users; turning them on only matters when the policy requires a client certificate at the TLS handshake, which it then no longer does for any path of photos. (mTLS stays enforced at login via the Keycloak acr). Upgrades: immich-server and immich-machine-learning are pinned to the same release and must always move together; read the upstream release notes for breaking changes and keep immich-db on the image upstream specifies. Shared folders: immich-server runs as root (no compose user:), so External photo library declares runs_as uid 0 / gid 0, read-only; on a shared folder it joins the folder's group through group_add.

items.text:

The app signs users in itself (native OIDC), so these paths are reachable without Portcullis sign-in anyway. When an admin turns them on in the Hub, they are also served without a client certificate on hosts whose policy requires one (see Public exceptions).

items.text:
Free and open-source media server — movies, TV, music, live TV

Category: media Tags: media, movies, tv, music, streaming, opensource Website: https://jellyfin.org/ Source: https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin

items.title: Authentication
items.text:
Property Value Method native-oidc SSO Yes Group Access Group Admin Access Group users_jellyfin Admin Group admin_jellyfin Subdomain media

Auth Notes

SSO-Auth plugin with group enforcement. Users must be in access_group to log in. Members of admin_group get Jellyfin admin. The plugin is pinned (version + SHA-256, jellyfin/plugin.py) and installed by the jellyfin-plugin one-shot before Jellyfin starts (Jellyfin doesn't start if the download doesn't match); the plugin catalog is not used. The jellyfin-setup sidecar configures it at every start. Jellyfin's own login form stays on the ungated router (the Jellyfin apps use it), but no account set up by Portcullis can sign in with a password: SSO-created accounts get a random password and the plugin's authentication provider, and setup moves the local admin it creates to that provider too (setup then authenticates with its own API key, kept in the config volume). Break-glass: admin_jellyfin members are Jellyfin administrators through SSO. Local users an administrator creates by hand do get a password login there; avoid them, or use strong passwords. TV and mobile apps sign in with Quick Connect from a signed-in browser session. Identity: the plugin creates and matches Jellyfin users by preferred_username (the immutable LLDAP username; DefaultUsernameClaim) and never sees the email (no email scope). An SSO login whose username equals an existing local Jellyfin user (e.g. the LLDAP "admin" and the local admin created by setup) is linked to it. Shared folders: the jellyfin image runs as root (no USER, no compose user:), so the library settings declare runs_as uid 0 / gid 0, read-only; on a shared folder Jellyfin joins the folder's group through group_add.

Auth Notes

No public exceptions: Kanboard's router reads ?controller=&action= before the path (app/Core/Http/Router.php), so any public prefix would reach every APP_PUBLIC action, local password login included. Reverse proxy auth: users are matched on X-Forwarded-User, the immutable LLDAP username, honoured only from Traefik (TRUSTED_PROXY_NETWORKS = PORTCULLIS_TRAEFIK_IP). X-Forwarded-Email (user-editable) only fills the profile email and is ignored from other peers too. Auto-creates users on first login. The LLDAP user picked in "Kanboard administrator" (default admin = LLDAP's built-in admin) gets the Kanboard admin role; other roles are set in the Kanboard UI. Access gated by group-gate. Accounts created when the header carried the email are named after it; rename them to the LLDAP username in Kanboard.

items.title: 🌅 LightCraft
items.text:
Non-destructive photo editor and library by ArtCraft, running entirely in the browser (Rust/WebAssembly; files stay on your device). In development.

Category: creative Tags: artcraft, wasm, photo, raw, library Website: https://getartcraft.com/apps/lightcraft Source: https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft

items.title: Authentication
items.text:
Property Value Method forward-auth SSO No Group Access Group Admin Access Group users_lightcraft Admin Group admin_lightcraft Subdomain lightcraft

Auth Notes

In development upstream (https://getartcraft.com/apps): expect missing features and breaking changes between versions. LightCraft (https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft, Apache-2.0 OR MIT) is a static site: the app runs in the visitor's browser and has no user system, no server-side code and no server-side storage. Open uses the browser's file picker, Save/Export download files; preferences live in the browser's storage for this hostname. LightCraft keeps its photo library in the browser's Origin Private File System (or IndexedDB) on the user's device; nothing is uploaded to the server. Portcullis sign-in (forward-auth + group-gate) is the only login; every member of the access group gets the same app (there are no roles). At every start the lightcraft-fetch init container downloads the release's lightcraft-web-.zip from GitHub, checks its SHA-256 against the pin before unpacking, and swaps the unpacked site into the lightcraft-site volume by rename; on any error it exits non-zero and the web server doesn't start (an unchanged pin skips the download). The host needs outbound HTTPS to github.com. The web server (nginx-unprivileged, read-only, no directory listing) answers only Traefik and itself. Version: the Release version / Release SHA-256 settings default to the pin in compose.yml (bumped with the template); set both together, from the release's SHA256SUMS.txt, to pin another release.

items.title: 🤖 LiteLLM
items.text:
Unified LLM proxy — OpenAI-compatible API for 100+ models with auth and rate limits

Category: ai Tags: llm, ai, openai, proxy, api Website: https://www.litellm.ai/ Source: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm

items.title: Authentication
items.text:
Property Value Method native-oidc SSO Yes Group Access Group Admin Access Group users_litellm Admin Group admin_litellm Subdomain llm

Auth Notes

OIDC login for the admin UI. The OpenAI-compatible API (and the management API the UI calls) has no forward-auth, so it is reachable with the master key or virtual API keys. The admin UI and all interactive login paths (/ui, /sso, /login, /v2/login, /fallback/login, /onboarding) sit behind forward-auth + group-gate: only members of users_litellm can sign in. SSO users default to the read-only internal_user_viewer role; LLDAP groups are mapped to roles (admin_litellm -> proxy_admin, users_litellm -> internal_user), but that mapping needs the Keycloak "groups" claim in the LiteLLM client's tokens; until the client has the groups scope, SSO users get internal_user_viewer and an admin (logged in with the master key) promotes them in the UI. Users created before this change keep their existing role; review them under Internal Users. Identity: SSO users are keyed on preferred_username (the immutable LLDAP username). LiteLLM would otherwise attach an SSO login to any existing user with the same email, and LLDAP emails are user-editable, so the template maps the email attribute to a claim that is never sent: SSO users have no email in LiteLLM. Users created before this change that were keyed on their email need their user_id changed to the LLDAP username.

items.title: 💬 Matrix (Synapse + Element)
items.text:
Self-hosted Matrix chat server (Synapse) with the Element web client

Category: communication Tags: chat, matrix, synapse, element, messaging, e2ee Website: https://element-hq.github.io/synapse/ Source: https://github.com/element-hq/synapse

items.title: Authentication
items.text:
Property Value Method native-oidc SSO Yes Group Access Group Admin Access Group users_matrix Admin Group admin_matrix Admin Paths /_synapse/admin (require admin_matrix in addition to access) Subdomain element, matrix

Auth Notes

Two hosts per instance. The homeserver (matrix., Synapse) does its own OIDC login against Keycloak and has no forward-auth, so Element, the Element mobile apps and other Matrix clients and bots reach the client API directly; Synapse only lets in users whose groups claim contains users_matrix (oidc attribute_requirements): outsiders get no account and no session. Element Web (element.) is a static client behind forward-auth + group-gate, so only members even get the page; it is fixed to this homeserver (no server picker) and redirects straight to SSO. Revoking access: Synapse checks the group only at the SSO login, so a user removed from users_matrix (or disabled in LLDAP) keeps the sessions they already have; every session expires after 7 days (session_lifetime) and must sign in again through the group-checked login. To cut a user off at once, deactivate them through the Admin API from inside the synapse container (POST /_synapse/admin/v1/deactivate/ with an admin access token) or log out their devices (DELETE /_synapse/admin/v2/users//devices/). Element Web is the one native-OIDC host router behind forward-auth (validate.py GATED_CLIENT_ROUTERS): it is a static client with no login of its own and no server data. Identity: accounts are keyed on the OIDC sub; the Matrix id is @: (localpart_template preferred_username). allow_existing_users is false, so an SSO login is never attached to an existing account, and the email is not imported. No password login (password_config.enabled false), no open registration, no 3PID changes. A reused LLDAP username (new Keycloak sub) gets a new id with a numeric suffix, never the old account. server_name is the homeserver's hostname, so no .well-known on the apex is needed (Synapse serves /.well-known/matrix/client itself). It is permanent: every user and room id contains it. Synapse refuses to start if the instance's homeserver hostname changes after the first start; pick it when creating the instance (hosts.immutable: the Hub refuses to change it once the instance exists; the Element host can change any time). The default instance's homeserver host is matrix.: changing Portcullis's main domain breaks it. A backup restores into the same instance only, never a new id. Admins: Synapse has no group-to-admin mapping, so admin_matrix grants nothing inside Synapse. Promote the first admin after their first SSO login with UPDATE users SET admin = 1 WHERE name = '@alice:<homeserver host>'; in the matrix-db container (psql -U synapse -d synapse), then restart the synapse container; later admins via the Admin API (PUT /_synapse/admin/v2/users/ {"admin": true}). The Admin API (/_synapse/admin, including shared-secret registration) is additionally behind forward-auth + group-gate and requires admin_matrix (auth.admin_paths), so call it from a browser session of an admin_matrix member or from inside the synapse container (curl http://localhost:8008/_synapse/admin/... with an admin access token, Element: Settings, Help & About). Federation is off: federation_domain_whitelist is [] and the listener serves no federation resource. To federate with specific servers, list their server names in the Federation peers setting: Synapse then serves the federation API and /.well-known/matrix/server on the homeserver host (port 443) and federates with those servers only. Open federation is not offered. Secrets (database, OIDC, registration shared secret, macaroon and form secrets) are generated per instance; the config is rendered at every start into a tmpfs; the server signing key is created once in the synapse-data volume (back it up with the volume: losing it breaks federation and other servers' trust). Synapse trusts X-Forwarded-For from any peer on portcullis-proxy (client IPs in logs and rate limits only). Upgrades: Synapse supports rolling upgrades between releases but read docs/upgrade.md for each step; keep matrix-db on PostgreSQL 16. Element Web is independent of the Synapse version.

items.title: 💬 Mattermost
items.text:
Team chat with channels, threads, file sharing and integrations (Team Edition)

Category: productivity Tags: chat, messaging, team, collaboration, slack-alternative Website: https://mattermost.com/ Source: https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost

items.title: Authentication
items.text:
Property Value Method forward-auth SSO No Group Access Group Admin Access Group users_mattermost Subdomain chat

Auth Notes

Mattermost Team Edition 12.0 has no SSO that works with Portcullis: OpenID Connect (and Google / Entra ID / SAML / LDAP) need a paid license, and the free GitLab SSO provider reads a GitLab user API (numeric "id", "username"), which Keycloak's userinfo doesn't serve (the Hub creates clients without custom mappers, and LLDAP users have no numeric id) and which can't restrict sign-in to a group. So the whole host is behind Portcullis sign-in + group-gate (users_mattermost) and Mattermost keeps its own accounts behind it. Self sign-up is off (no email sign-up, which also closes the first-account and invite-link sign-ups; no open server; locked in the System Console). Team Edition's System Console can't create accounts; an admin creates them with mmctl in local mode, in the container (Hub exec or the server shell): mmctl --local user create --username <LLDAP username> --email <email> --password <random placeholder>, then mmctl --local user change-password <username>, which prompts for the real initial password on stdin (mmctl only takes the create password as an argument, so use a throwaway there), hands that password over out of band, and the user changes it after signing in. Local mode answers anyone who can run a process in the Mattermost container with full system-admin rights (no authentication); Hub exec into that container is admin access. Give each account the person's LLDAP username, since Mattermost doesn't know who passed the gateway. No admin group: Mattermost can't map one (no SSO), so admins are made in Mattermost (by a system admin, e.g. mmctl --local roles system-admin ). The bootstrap system admin is mmadmin- with the generated password MATTERMOST_ADMIN_PASSWORD, created once by the mattermost-init one-shot over the local-mode socket and pinned by its user ID in the data volume: system_admin is granted only to the account that run created, never to an account found by name. If the bootstrap name later belongs to a different account (renamed and taken) or exists without the pinned ID, mattermost-init fails (the Hub reports the failed one-shot) and grants nothing; Mattermost itself keeps running (its image has no shell, so its healthcheck can't read the state file), and the account holding the name stays a plain user. Change the bootstrap password after the first sign-in. Team Edition can't lock usernames (LockProfileFieldsForEmailUsers is Enterprise-only), so users can rename themselves; Mattermost usernames are not an identity Portcullis vouches for. GitLab SSO, personal access tokens and the plugin marketplace are off, and so are plugin uploads (server-side code from any system-admin session). Plugins: a pinned list (plugins.py, each a GitHub release asset checked against its SHA-256): freemium 2.0.0 (dy0gu/mattermost-plugin-freemium, hides Team Edition's upsell UI) and Matterpoll 1.9.2 (/poll). Mattermost requires plugin signatures, and upstream doesn't sign these, so before every compose-managed start (what the Hub runs; a plain Docker restart reuses the last signatures, which is safe) the mattermost-plugins one-shot checks a private copy of each bundle (in its root-only tmpfs; file-store copies are opened without following symlinks, regular files only) against its SHA-256 (a mismatch or a swapped file fails it before anything is signed, and Mattermost doesn't start), signs that private copy with an OpenPGP key it generates in tmpfs for that start only (the private key never reaches a volume), writes bundle + signature into Mattermost's file store (locked to the data volume) and only the public key to a volume Mattermost mounts read-only (SignaturePublicKeyFiles). Mattermost installs from the file store at startup, so any other bundle, unsigned or signed by another key, is refused. The public key is placed before the signatures, so an interrupted job leaves only signatures the new key doesn't verify (those plugins are refused until the next run). Mattermost's built-in key still accepts any Mattermost-signed bundle, old versions included, if something writes one into the file store's plugins/ directory; that needs filesystem access to the data volume or local-mode access (both already full admin). mattermost-init enables the pinned plugins. Bump a plugin by editing its version, URL and SHA-256 in plugins.py (Dependabot doesn't see them). SSO, re-checked: the free GitLab provider can't use Keycloak today. Team Edition switches to the licensed OpenID provider whenever the GitLab scope contains "openid", while Keycloak's userinfo refuses tokens without the openid scope ("Missing openid scope"), and the provider needs a stable numeric "id" that no static Keycloak mapper can derive (LLDAP has no numeric attribute, Keycloak ids are UUIDs). It becomes possible once the Hub allocates a per-person numeric id (a user attribute mapped to "id"), plus mappers for username, which the Hub doesn't create yet. What doesn't work through the gateway: the Mattermost desktop and mobile apps and anything else that talks to the API directly (bots, incoming/outgoing webhooks, slash-command callbacks, personal or bot access tokens), because every request needs a Portcullis browser session first; use the web app. Networking: Mattermost is on the instance's private network only; the gate in front of it (nginx, mattermost-gate, the only container on portcullis-proxy) answers Traefik's address alone, so no other container can reach Mattermost past the gateway. The gate never forwards the Portcullis session (Authorization, access-token headers and the forward-auth cookies are removed) and passes the websocket through. Mattermost takes the client address (logs, rate limits) from X-Real-Ip, which Traefik sets to the peer it accepted (client-sent copies are deleted) and the gate passes on unchanged. Upgrades: follow Mattermost's upgrade path (extended support releases, one major at a time); don't bump the PostgreSQL major.

items.title: 🍽 Mealie
items.text:
Self-hosted recipe manager, meal planner and shopping lists

Category: productivity Tags: recipes, cooking, meal-planning, shopping-list, food Website: https://mealie.io/ Source: https://github.com/mealie-recipes/mealie

items.title: Authentication
items.text:
Property Value Method native-oidc SSO Yes Group Access Group Admin Access Group users_mealie Admin Group admin_mealie Subdomain recipes

Auth Notes

Native OIDC (Mealie v3.30.0). The login page redirects straight to Portcullis (OIDC_AUTO_REDIRECT). Only members of users_mealie or admin_mealie may sign in (OIDC_USER_GROUP / OIDC_ADMIN_GROUP, checked by Mealie on the groups claim); accounts are created on the first SSO login and keyed on the LLDAP username (OIDC_USER_CLAIM preferred_username). admin_mealie members are Mealie admins, re-evaluated at every login; everyone else is a plain user of the default group/household (an admin can move them). No password login at all: Mealie's ALLOW_PASSWORD_LOGIN=false only hides the form and its token API still accepts passwords, so the mealie-init one-shot (guard.py, before the app starts, every start) installs a database trigger that makes every account an OIDC account (Mealie refuses passwords for those), and retires the admin Mealie seeds on an empty database (well-known password) by giving it a username and email no SSO login can match. Self sign-up, invitations and LDAP / reverse-proxy logins are off. Identity: Mealie matches an SSO login to an existing account by the preferred_username claim in the username column, then in the email column, and lets users edit both, so the trigger keeps the username and email of every account fixed (an edit is refused), refuses emails without '@' (LLDAP usernames never contain one) and any account whose email equals another account's username or the reverse: the email lookup can never hand one user's login to another. That is also why OIDC_REQUIRES_EMAIL_VERIFICATION can be off (Keycloak marks LLDAP emails unverified). The name claim is preferred_username (OIDC_NAME_CLAIM; Keycloak omits "name" for users without a first/last name). An admin who creates a user in Mealie pre-provisions it for the LLDAP user of that username (no password). The app's healthcheck fails (Traefik stops routing) if the trigger is missing or an account has a password login. Users need an email in LLDAP (Mealie requires the claim); two LLDAP users with the same email can't both sign in (Mealie's email column is unique), and a member who sets their LLDAP email to someone else's before that person's first login blocks that person's account creation on purpose (an admin has to correct the email in LLDAP). Removing a user from the groups blocks new SSO logins, not sessions (TOKEN_TIME, 48 h) or API tokens already issued; delete or lock the user in Mealie for that. Mobile/desktop apps use the OIDC native flow (register their redirect URI on the Keycloak client). Upgrades: read the Mealie release notes; database migrations run in mealie-init and fail closed if one would change an account's username or email. Keep mealie, mealie-init and mealie-perms on the same image; don't bump the PostgreSQL major.

items.title: 📹 motionEye
items.text:
Video surveillance for network and USB cameras — motion detection, recording, live view

Category: home-automation Tags: home-automation, cameras, surveillance, cctv, motion-detection Website: https://github.com/motioneye-project/motioneye Source: https://github.com/motioneye-project/motioneye

items.title: Authentication
items.text:
Property Value Method forward-auth SSO No Group Access Group Admin Access Group users_motioneye Admin Group admin_motioneye Subdomain cameras

Auth Notes

motionEye 0.44 (motioneye-project, maintained: 0.44.0 in June 2026) has no SSO; its own login has two local accounts, "admin" (full configuration) and "user" (view only), whose passwords are empty after a fresh install. Access is gated by forward-auth + group-gate on the whole host, and motionEye's login stays as a second step: motioneye-init sets each account with an empty password to a generated one before every start (MOTIONEYE_ADMIN_PASSWORD / MOTIONEYE_USER_PASSWORD in this instance's .env, Hub data env/.env; hashed by motionEye, argon2), so motionEye never runs with its well-known empty default, and the healthcheck fails while either is empty. Share the admin password with your camera administrators and the user password with viewers; a password changed in motionEye's settings is kept (clearing one sets the generated value again at the next start). motionEye doesn't read any identity header, so no LLDAP user name maps to these accounts. The admin account can do everything motionEye can, including commands run on motion events inside the container. The UI is on the instance's private network only; the gate in front of it (nginx, the only container on portcullis-proxy) answers Traefik's address alone, never forwards the Portcullis session (Authorization, access-token headers, forward-auth cookies), and is healthy (= routed) only while motionEye refuses an empty password for the admin and user account names. Cameras: network cameras by URL (RTSP, HTTP/MJPEG; added in motionEye, reached outbound from the container) and up to four local V4L2 cameras listed in the Local cameras setting (e.g. /dev/video0; only those are passed in, not privileged, so several instances can each use their own; a path that doesn't exist on the host stops the container from starting). Live view goes through motionEye's own UI; motion's direct streaming ports (8081+, "Video Streaming" in the camera settings) are not published, so direct stream URLs only work inside the instance. Storage: set "Storage folder" to a host path (e.g. /srv/cctv) to record there instead of the instance's media volume; keep an eye on its size (motionEye's own "Preserve" settings delete old media). Not available in a container: shutdown/reboot, and SMB share mounts. Shared folders: motionEye runs as root (uid 0 / gid 0, the image's motion user; no compose user:) and writes the Storage folder, so it declares access write with runs_as uid 0 / gid 0. Root is what lets it write a shared folder: the entrypoint starts motionEye with su -g, which drops supplementary groups, so the folder group the Hub adds through group_add never reaches the process.

items.title: 🐦 NetBird
items.text:
Mesh VPN + zero-trust networking with TURN relay

Category: vpn Tags: vpn, wireguard, mesh, zero-trust Website: https://netbird.io/ Source: https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird

items.title: Authentication
items.text:
Property Value Method native-oidc SSO Yes Group Access Group Admin Access Group users_netbird Admin Group admin_netbird Subdomain netbird

Auth Notes

Dashboard uses OIDC. Management API validates JWT audience. No group-based access restriction — all OIDC users can access dashboard. Identity: management keys users on the token's sub (AuthUserIDClaim; no IdP manager, so nothing is matched by email). The dashboard sends the ID token to the management API (NETBIRD_TOKEN_SOURCE=idToken): its audience is the client id management checks; Keycloak access tokens would carry aud "account". Upgrades: netbird-management and netbird-signal are pinned to the same release and must move together (the dashboard has its own version line); follow the upstream upgrade notes and do not skip releases with migrations. Instances: coturn runs with host networking (a TURN relay advertises its relay ports to peers, so they must be the host's own ports) and binds the STUN/TURN and TURNS ports and the UDP media relay range itself. All three are per-instance port settings; the defaults (3478, 5349, 49152-65535) are taken by the first instance, so the Hub's port collision check refuses to start another instance until it is given free ports and a range that doesn't overlap (e.g. 3479, 5350, 40000-40999). management.json is generated once (it holds NetBird's DataStoreEncryptionKey); a later hostname, STUN port or TURN public IP change is applied to it in place on the next start.

items.title: ☁️ Nextcloud
items.text:
Self-hosted productivity platform — files, calendar, contacts, office

Category: productivity Tags: files, calendar, office, collaboration Website: https://nextcloud.com/ Source: https://github.com/nextcloud/server

items.title: Authentication
items.text:
Property Value Method native-oidc SSO Yes Group Access Group Admin Access Group users_nextcloud Admin Group admin_nextcloud Subdomain cloud

Auth Notes

Native OIDC through Nextcloud's official user_oidc app (pinned v8.11.0, installed and configured by setup.sh at every start; upgrade it there). Sign-in is one Portcullis login: the login page redirects to Keycloak. Accounts are created on the first SSO login and keyed on the LLDAP username (preferred_username, unique-uid off, so the Nextcloud user id is the username); soft auto-provisioning is off, so an SSO login is never attached to an existing local account and nothing is matched by email (the user-editable email only fills the profile). Sign-in is restricted to access_group in Keycloak (keycloak_access_role, contract §8 Access role): only users_nextcloud members can sign in, so a member of admin_nextcloud who is not also in users_nextcloud is denied — put Nextcloud's admins in both groups (user_oidc's group whitelist + login restriction stay as a second check); both groups are synced into Nextcloud at each login, and members of admin_nextcloud become Nextcloud admins within a minute (nextcloud-cron maps them into Nextcloud's "admin" group and removes SSO accounts that left it). No password login at all: Nextcloud can't switch its password form off server-side, so every local account (the nc-breakglass admin the image creates at install, the "admin" of installs made before this template version, accounts created in the Users page) is disabled at every start and within a minute by nextcloud-cron; the login form is hidden. Move a local account's files to its owner's SSO account with occ files:transfer-ownership. An LLDAP user whose name is a local account (e.g. "admin" on older installs) gets "User conflict" until that account is deleted (occ user:delete). Desktop/mobile clients use Login Flow v2 and get app passwords; WebDAV/OCS accept only app passwords or tokens (token_auth_enforced). Break-glass is occ on the server, e.g. docker compose -p portcullis- exec -u www-data nextcloud php occ group:adduser admin (or user_oidc:provider, config:system:set, user:info). Removing a user from the groups blocks new SSO logins and drops the groups at their next login, not sessions or app passwords already issued (occ user:disable for that); single logout is off because the Keycloak client has no post-logout redirect URI. Hostname: setup.sh re-applies trusted_domains, overwrite.cli.url, overwritehost and overwriteprotocol from the instance's hostname at every start, so a hostname change only needs a restart. Public exceptions: the host is not behind forward-auth, so every share link already works without Portcullis sign-in, listed or not (Nextcloud's share token, password, expiry and brute-force protection apply; it sees the client IP via TRUSTED_PROXIES = Traefik). The Hub exception only changes hosts whose policy requires a client certificate: there, the listed share links (mode all: every share) and the static files their page needs are served without one, and logins (Basic auth, remember-me cookies) are refused on those paths. The PDF viewer page (a PHP route) is not in the list, so on such hosts PDFs on a share download instead of opening inline; Markdown renders only in mode all. Apps installed under /custom_apps that hook the share page are not covered. Keycloak must be reachable at a public name and address: Nextcloud's HTTP client refuses hosts with a local TLD (.local, .lan, ...) or a private address (allow_local_remote_servers stays off; user_oidc has no switch scoped to the provider), so with split DNS or a LAN-only domain user_oidc answers "Could not reach the OpenID Connect provider". Never set user_oidc's httpclient.allowselfsigned (it turns TLS verification off). Upgrades: the image is pinned; Nextcloud only upgrades one major version at a time, so step through every major (e.g. 33 -> 34 -> 35) and never skip one. Keep nextcloud and nextcloud-cron on the same image. Database: chosen at setup (PostgreSQL on nextcloud-postgres, the default, MySQL / MariaDB on nextcloud-mariadb, each under its own compose profile, or SQLite in the data volume) and fixed after the first start. Switching means a new instance with the other choice and moving the data across (e.g. with Nextcloud's occ db:convert-type). Never bump the database servers' major versions in place. Settings: the default storage quota and the trash retention are applied live through occ by the apply-settings hook (apply-settings.php, run by the Hub as www-data in the nextcloud container at start and after every save; idempotent, exits non-zero on any occ failure). Quotas set per user in Nextcloud's Users page still win over the default. AI availability: while AI support is on, any container on portcullis-proxy can reach the companion and send wrong credentials; Nextcloud's brute-force protection counts them against the companion's address, which every AI request comes from, so such a container can slow everyone's AI requests down (sign-in itself still holds). Re-used usernames: accounts are keyed on the username, so a deleted person's username given to someone new gets the former person's Nextcloud account, on the web and through AI alike (the AI mint can't tell them apart: user_oidc stores no Keycloak id). Delete or rename the former person's Nextcloud account (occ user:delete) before re-using a username.

items.title: 🗂 OxiCloud
items.text:
Lightweight self-hosted file storage and sync with WebDAV, CalDAV and CardDAV

Category: productivity Tags: files, storage, sync, webdav, caldav, carddav, rust Website: https://atalayalabs.github.io/OxiCloud/ Source: https://github.com/AtalayaLabs/OxiCloud

items.title: Authentication
items.text:
Property Value Method native-oidc SSO Yes Group Access Group Admin Access Group users_oxicloud Admin Group admin_oxicloud Subdomain drive

Auth Notes

Native OpenID Connect (OxiCloud 0.10.0) and nothing else: OXICLOUD_AUTH_METHODS=oidc turns password login, sign-up and the OPAQUE endpoints off, and OIDC hard-disables magic links. The login page redirects straight to Portcullis. OxiCloud has no OIDC group restriction of its own, so the authorize endpoint (/api/auth/oidc/authorize, which mints the login state the callback requires) is behind Portcullis sign-in + group-gate (access_group), and the Hub's Keycloak access role restricts the client to access_group as well. Accounts are created on the first SSO login and keyed on the OIDC issuer + sub; the OxiCloud username is the LLDAP username (preferred_username, lowercased; OxiCloud appends a suffix if it is taken). SSO logins are never linked to existing accounts by email (OXICLOUD_OIDC_AUTO_LINK_EMAIL_MATCH=false); a login whose email matches another account is refused instead, so two LLDAP users with the same email can't both sign in. admin_oxicloud members become OxiCloud admins when their account is created (first login); OxiCloud does not re-evaluate the role later, so promote or demote existing users in its admin panel. Nobody is the instance owner (OxiCloud never derives ownership from an IdP); an operator can name one with oxicloud user promote-to-owner <username> in the container. The first-run setup endpoint (POST /api/setup, a password owner account for whoever calls it first) is closed by the oxicloud-init one-shot before OxiCloud starts (it marks the instance initialized), and the app is routed only while it reports itself initialized. Sessions: Keycloak calls OxiCloud's back-channel logout (/api/auth/oidc/backchannel-logout) whenever a Keycloak session ends; the Hub signs a user out of Keycloak when they leave the group, so their OxiCloud sessions (7 d rotating refresh tokens) are revoked then. What remains until it expires or is revoked in OxiCloud: an access token already issued (at most 1 h) and app passwords (WebDAV/CalDAV/CardDAV, no expiry); deactivate the user in OxiCloud to cut those. Device sign-in (RFC 8628, /api/auth/device) is approved by a signed-in user: a member can be tricked into approving a code an outsider started, which signs the outsider in as that member (approve only codes you started). Public share links (/api/s/{token}, the share page and its assets) are answered by OxiCloud without Portcullis sign-in by design: the host router has no forward-auth (native OIDC). On a host whose policy requires a client certificate they are refused at the TLS layer like everything else; this template declares no auth.public_access, so no exception can be opened for them there. WebDAV, CalDAV and CardDAV clients use app passwords (created by the signed-in user under Settings); the Nextcloud-compatible API for Nextcloud desktop/mobile apps is off (it would add another login flow). Upgrades: read the OxiCloud release notes; don't bump the PostgreSQL major.

items.text:

items.title: Authentication
items.text:
Property Value Method native-oidc SSO Yes Group Access Group Admin Access Group users_paperless Admin Group admin_paperless Admin Paths /admin (require admin_paperless in addition to access) Subdomain paperless

Auth Notes

OpenID Connect only, through Paperless' django-allauth provider (PAPERLESS_APPS openid_connect, provider id portcullis). The regular login form is off (PAPERLESS_DISABLE_REGULAR_LOGIN) and the login page goes straight to Portcullis (PAPERLESS_REDIRECT_LOGIN_TO_SSO). Who can sign in: allauth has no OIDC group restriction, so the SSO start and callback paths (/accounts/oidc/...) sit behind forward-auth + group-gate and only users_paperless members can sign in or get an account; allauth's headless provider-token endpoints (/api/auth/headless/{browser,app}/v1/auth/provider) are gated the same way, so no SSO login skips group-gate. The rest of the API (API tokens, mobile apps) is not gated. Removing a user from users_paperless (or admin_paperless) blocks new SSO logins and takes effect at their next login; browser sessions last 12 hours (PAPERLESS_SESSION_COOKIE_AGE, upstream default 3 weeks), so a removed admin keeps superuser rights for at most that long. API tokens keep working: deactivate the user in Paperless to cut them off at once. No password logins at all: DISABLE_REGULAR_LOGIN only hides the form, while HTTP Basic auth, POST /api/token/ and a password a user sets on their profile would still work, so the one-shot paperless-init job installs a database trigger that replaces every password hash with an unusable one (check_password never succeeds; a password typed on the profile page is discarded). Local accounts created in the Paperless UI therefore cannot sign in. The same job creates an inactive, passwordless placeholder account (paperless-bootstrap), because Paperless opens its signup page and makes the first account a superuser while the database has no user; Paperless only starts once the job succeeded (fail closed). There is no bootstrap superuser password: break-glass is on the server, e.g. docker exec -it python3 manage.py shell (or manage.py document_exporter for backups). Identity: accounts are keyed on the OIDC sub and named after preferred_username (the LLDAP username); allauth never links a login to an existing account by email (EMAIL_AUTHENTICATION off; LLDAP emails are user-editable). If the username is already taken, or the email claim equals another account's, allauth picks a different username or asks the user for one on its signup form; the account is still bound to that person's sub. Roles: groups come from the Keycloak groups claim at every login (PAPERLESS_SOCIAL_ACCOUNT_SYNC_GROUPS): a user's Paperless groups are exactly the Keycloak groups that also exist as Paperless groups. paperless-init creates the users_paperless Paperless group once with a regular-user role (documents, tags, correspondents, document types, storage paths, saved views, notes; read-only custom fields and tasks; own UI settings; no users, groups, mail, workflows, share links or settings), so a member can work with documents they own or that are shared with them (and unowned ones, e.g. from the consume folder). To grant more, create a Paperless group named like an LLDAP group and put users in that LLDAP group; groups assigned by hand in Paperless are replaced at the next login. admin_paperless members become superuser and staff, and lose it at their next login once removed. The Django admin (/admin) is additionally behind forward-auth + group-gate with admin_paperless. Consume folder: a volume (paperless-consume). To use a scanner folder on the host, bind it to /usr/src/paperless/consume in the app's custom override (Hub Expert tab, under /srv, /mnt or /media); it must be writable by uid 1000. Documents consumed from there have no owner, so every user with the regular role can see them; give them an owner with a Paperless workflow. Extra OCR languages beyond the image's eng, deu, fra, ita and spa can't be installed (the container runs rootless). Office documents (Tika / Gotenberg) are not included. Upgrades: paperless and paperless-init use the same image and move together; read the Paperless release notes before major upgrades (paperless-init runs upstream's compatibility check and the migrations with every volume mounted, as Paperless itself would). PostgreSQL stays on 18 and Redis on 8 (no major bumps without a data migration).

Auth Notes

Early alpha upstream (https://getartcraft.com/apps): expect missing features and breaking changes between versions. PdfCraft (https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft, Apache-2.0 OR MIT) is a static site: the app runs in the visitor's browser and has no user system, no server-side code and no server-side storage. The host needs outbound HTTPS to github.com. The web server (nginx-unprivileged, read-only, no directory listing) answers only Traefik and itself. Version: the Release version / Release SHA-256 settings default to the pin in compose.yml (bumped with the template); set both together, from the release's SHA256SUMS.txt, to pin another release.

items.text:
Network-wide ad blocking via DNS sinkhole (every member of the access group is a full Pi-hole admin; Pi-hole has no roles)

Category: networking Tags: dns, adblock, privacy, filtering Website: https://pi-hole.net/ Source: https://github.com/pi-hole/pi-hole

items.title: Authentication
items.text:
Property Value Method forward-auth SSO No Group Access Group Admin Access Group users_pihole Admin Group admin_pihole Subdomain pihole

Auth Notes

No SSO in Pi-hole; Portcullis sign-in (forward-auth + group-gate) is the only login. Pi-hole's own password is off (FTLCONF_webserver_api_password empty), which upstream allows: with no password the API needs no session. Safe here because Pi-hole's web server ACL (FTLCONF_webserver_acl, https://docs.pi-hole.net/ftldns/configfile/#acl) only lets Traefik and the container itself connect: other containers on portcullis-proxy get 403, and Traefik serves the host only through the gateway. The DNS ports (53) are unaffected; Pi-hole serves no DNS-over-HTTPS. Consequences: every member of users_pihole is a full Pi-hole admin (Pi-hole has no roles). Without a password FTL (v6.8, src/api/auth.c check_client_auth) still refuses browser requests sent by other websites, sibling hosts on the same parent domain included (Sec-Fetch-Site / Origin), and requests whose Host is not one of its own names (DNS rebinding); FTLCONF_webserver_domain is therefore set to the instance's hostname at every start. The previous PIHOLE_WEBPASSWORD is no longer used. Upgrades: keep an image with FTL v6.8 or later (these no-password checks).

items.text:

Auth Notes

Plex uses its own plex.tv account system; no SSO is possible. By default the Hub puts Portcullis sign-in (users_plex) in front of Plex's own login; the Hub's Sign-in setting can switch to Plex's own login only (no Portcullis, TLS tier public), which Plex's native apps need. Claim token required for initial setup. Shared folders: pms-docker's first-run script sets the plex user's uid / gid from PLEX_UID / PLEX_GID, and Plex starts through s6-setuidgid plex, which resets the supplementary groups to plex's own in /etc/group (a group_add gid wouldn't reach Plex). So the library settings join a shared folder's group through PLEX_GID (joins_group gid_env): the Hub writes the folder gid there. Keep all three library settings on the same shared folder (subfolders are fine), or all on host paths; a library left empty doesn't count.

items.title: Sign-in
items.text:
The app has its own login. The Hub's per-app Sign-in setting chooses who signs users in (Apps with their own login):

  • Portcullis sign-in, then the app's own login (default): forward-auth and group-gate in front, members of users_plex.
  • App's own login only (no Portcullis): allowed by this template. No forward-auth, TLS tier public@file: anyone on the internet reaches the app's login page.

Plex signs users in with plex.tv accounts. Behind Portcullis sign-in only the web app in a browser works; Plex's TV, mobile and desktop apps can't pass forward-auth and need "App's own login only".

items.title: 📂 Samba
items.text:
File sharing over SMB, a home folder per person and up to 8 shared folders, each person with their own file-share password

Category: storage Tags: files, smb, samba, nas, file-sharing Website: https://github.com/ServerContainers/samba Source: https://github.com/ServerContainers/samba

items.title: Authentication
items.text:
Property Value Method custom SSO No Group Access Group Admin Access Group users_samba

Auth Notes

No web page: file sharing over SMB. Each member of users_samba creates their own file-share password on My apps (people.) after a fresh passkey sign-in, and gets the share Home, their own folder / (owned by their Hub uid, mode 0700). Up to 8 shared folders (slots 1-8): the admin assigns a slot a shared folder (Settings -> Shared folders), a share name and reader and writer groups. Readers can read, writers can also write, nobody else in the instance can open it; files land as <the person's uid>:<the folder's gid> (force group), mode 0660, directories 2770. To share a folder with everyone who has access, pick users_samba as its reader group. The password is shown once; the Hub keeps only its NT hash on the hub_secrets volume, mounted read-only here, never in a backup. Someone who leaves the access group, or whose account is deleted, loses the password at once, and someone who leaves a share's groups loses that share at once: the Hub's hook removes the account or the share and ends their open sessions within seconds (a change made directly in LLDAP within about a minute). Image: ServerContainers samba (smbd-only, Samba 4.23 on Alpine); its /container/scripts/entrypoint.sh never runs, so none of its ACCOUNT_, GROUP_, SAMBA_* or AVAHI_* variables does anything (setting one is ignored; an ACCOUNT_* would only put a password in docker inspect). The container starts with portcullis-sync --boot (shared with the Time Machine template), which writes the whole smb.conf, the passdb (smbpasswd on tmpfs) and the Unix accounts from the Hub's people file and hash files, then runit supervises smbd alone (no nmbd, avahi or wsdd2). The image has no default account. SMB is hardened and verified: SMB3 only (3.1.1), encryption and signing required, NTLMv2 only, no guest or anonymous access, no NetBIOS, port 445 only, hosts allow = the Hub's Local networks (an empty list keeps the instance from starting); testparm must show exactly these values or smbd doesn't start. Publish 445 on the LAN or VPN only (lan_only); Docker's published ports bypass ufw. Capabilities: cap_drop ALL, then CHOWN (a new person's home folder is created and given to their uid), SETUID and SETGID (smbd acts as each person with the folder's group; the Hub's files and each folder's size are read as their owner, a privilege drop with runit's chpst instead of DAC_OVERRIDE / DAC_READ_SEARCH, which this container never has) and NET_BIND_SERVICE (port 445). no-new-privileges. The root filesystem isn't read-only: portcullis-sync writes /etc/passwd, /etc/group and /etc/shadow (each person's Unix account and the pfg group of each shared folder) and the start writes runit's service directory (/run/portcullis-sv); the hashes, the passdb and Samba's state are on tmpfs, and /shares is a small tmpfs, so a slot without a shared folder has nothing to serve. A healthcheck reports unhealthy while smb.conf no longer verifies or smbd isn't running. A home folder that belongs to a former account (an account deleted and created again gets a new uid) is never served; the File sharing tab and the doctor show it. Share names are refused, case-insensitively, when Samba reserves them (global, homes, printers, print$, ipc$, home) or another slot has the same name; the doctor shows it. Bonjour is off by default: people connect with the smb:// address shown on My apps (Finder → Go → Connect to Server). Bonjour opt-in mounts the host's Avahi services directory at /portcullis/avahi and writes portcullis-.service there, not the image's fixed samba.service (two instances would overwrite each other). Upstream tags name the Alpine and Samba versions (smbd-only-a-s-r): Dependabot follows them.

items.title: 🕰 Time Machine
items.text:
Mac backups over SMB, one backup share per person with their own file-share password

Category: storage Tags: backup, time-machine, macos, smb, samba Website: https://github.com/mbentley/docker-timemachine Source: https://github.com/mbentley/docker-timemachine

items.title: Authentication
items.text:
Property Value Method custom SSO No Group Access Group Admin Access Group users_timemachine

Auth Notes

No web page: file sharing over SMB. Each member of users_timemachine creates their own file-share password on My apps (people.) after a fresh passkey sign-in, and gets one Time Machine share, -, in their own folder / (owned by their Hub uid, mode 0700). The password is shown once; the Hub keeps only its NT hash on the hub_secrets volume, mounted read-only here, never in a backup. Someone who leaves the access group, or whose account is deleted, loses the password at once: the Hub's credential_change hook removes the account and ends their open sessions within seconds (a removal made directly in LLDAP within about a minute). Image: mbentley/timemachine (smb variant, Samba 4.23 on Alpine); its /entrypoint.sh never runs. The container starts with portcullis-sync --boot (shared with the Samba template), which writes the whole smb.conf, the passdb (smbpasswd on tmpfs) and the Unix accounts from the Hub's people file and hash files, then s6 supervises smbd alone (no nmbd, avahi or dbus). The image's default timemachine account is never created. SMB is hardened and verified: SMB3 only (3.1.1), encryption and signing required, NTLMv2 only, no guest or anonymous access, no NetBIOS, port 445 only, hosts allow = the Hub's Local networks (an empty list keeps the instance from starting); testparm must show exactly these values or smbd doesn't start. Publish 445 on the LAN or VPN only (lan_only); Docker's published ports bypass ufw. Capabilities: cap_drop ALL, then CHOWN (a new person's folder is created and given to their uid), SETUID and SETGID (smbd acts as each person; the Hub's files and each folder's size are read as their owner, a privilege drop instead of DAC_OVERRIDE / DAC_READ_SEARCH, which this container never has) and NET_BIND_SERVICE (port 445). no-new-privileges. The root filesystem isn't read-only: portcullis-sync writes /etc/passwd, /etc/group and /etc/shadow (each person's Unix account) and the start writes its copy of /etc/s6 (/run/portcullis-s6); the hashes, the passdb and Samba's state are on tmpfs. A healthcheck reports unhealthy while smb.conf no longer verifies or smbd isn't running. Backup size limit: Time Machine keeps backups within it (Samba's fruit:time machine max size, cooperative, not a hard quota). A folder that belongs to a former account (an account deleted and created again gets a new uid) is never served; the File sharing tab and the doctor show it. Bonjour is off by default: people connect with the smb:// address shown on My apps (Finder → Go → Connect to Server, then System Settings → Time Machine → Add Backup Disk). Upstream tags are dated (smb-YYYYMMDD): Dependabot follows the digest.

items.title: 🔐 Vaultwarden
items.text:
Lightweight Bitwarden-compatible password manager

Category: security Tags: passwords, bitwarden, vault, secrets Website: https://github.com/dani-garcia/vaultwarden Source: https://github.com/dani-garcia/vaultwarden

items.title: Authentication
items.text:
Property Value Method native-oidc SSO Yes Group Access Group Admin Access Group users_vaultwarden Admin Group admin_vaultwarden Admin Paths /admin (require admin_vaultwarden in addition to access) Subdomain passwords

Auth Notes

No public exceptions: Bitwarden Send (1.37.4, web vault v2026.7.0) needs the web vault at / with root-level hashed assets and the password-login token endpoint /identity/connect/token (grant_type=send_access), which no narrow path list can express. Native SSO via OpenID Connect, and SSO only (SSO_ONLY): the email + master password login is disabled in the web vault and for the clients, so every sign-in goes through Keycloak. The master password never signs anyone in; it only decrypts the vault after the SSO login (Bitwarden's end-to-end encryption), so users still set one. The SSO start and callback paths (/identity/connect/authorize, /identity/connect/oidc-signin) sit behind forward-auth + group-gate, so only members of users_vaultwarden can sign in or get an account by SSO (Vaultwarden has no OIDC group restriction); the API, the token exchange and the Bitwarden clients are not gated. Removing a user from users_vaultwarden blocks new SSO logins, not sessions or devices already signed in (deactivate the user in /admin for that). The admin panel (/admin) is also behind forward-auth + group-gate and, through auth.admin_paths, requires admin_vaultwarden on top of users_vaultwarden; Vaultwarden's ADMIN_TOKEN (VAULTWARDEN_ADMIN_TOKEN) is still required, keep it secret. Identity: SSO accounts are keyed on the OIDC subject (issuer + sub); SSO_SIGNUPS_MATCH_EMAIL stays false, so an SSO login is never attached to an existing registered account by email (LLDAP emails are user-editable). The Keycloak client uses email_verified_claim: false (scope email-unverified: email claim, no email_verified), which Vaultwarden accepts with SSO_ALLOW_UNKNOWN_EMAIL_VERIFICATION, so new users sign up with SSO on their first login and then set the master password that encrypts their vault. SIGNUPS_ALLOWED is false (accounts only via SSO) and INVITATIONS_ALLOWED is false: an email invitation would create a placeholder account that Vaultwarden hands to the first SSO user presenting that email. Organisations can therefore only add users who have already signed in; check the member's name (their LLDAP username) before confirming them, since the email they were found by is user-editable. Don't use the /admin "Invite user" button (it ignores INVITATIONS_ALLOWED and creates such a placeholder). A user whose email collides with an existing account is refused, never merged.

items.text:

Category: productivity Tags: tasks, todo, kanban, projects, caldav Website: https://vikunja.io/ Source: https://github.com/go-vikunja/vikunja

items.title: Authentication
items.text:
Property Value Method native-oidc SSO Yes Group Access Group Admin Access Group users_vikunja Subdomain tasks

Auth Notes

Native OIDC (Vikunja v2.7.1). The login page redirects straight to Portcullis: local accounts are off (auth.local.enabled false), so Vikunja registers no password login, sign-up, password reset or invite link route at all, and LDAP is off. Who may sign in: Vikunja has no OIDC group restriction of its own, so the Hub enforces users_vikunja in Keycloak (keycloak_access_role: the client's access role and browser flow; direct grants and the other non-browser grants are off on the client). Accounts are created on the first SSO login, keyed on the OIDC issuer + sub and named after preferred_username (the LLDAP username; Vikunja picks a random one if that name is taken); they are never linked to an existing account by email or username (emailfallback / usernamefallback false). Users need an email in LLDAP (Vikunja requires the claim; it is display/notification only). Every SSO user is a regular user: Vikunja's instance admin is a paid feature (admin panel license) set only with the CLI, so admin_vikunja is not used. Team sync: Vikunja reads teams only from a custom vikunja_groups claim (objects with name and oidcID), which the Hub's Keycloak clients don't send; teams are managed in Vikunja. CalDAV and the API take Vikunja's own CalDAV / API tokens (created by a signed-in user), never a password. Public project links are off unless "Link sharing" is turned on. Outgoing requests to URLs users enter (webhooks, imports, avatars) may not reach private addresses. Removing a user from the group blocks new sign-ins (and the Hub signs them out of Keycloak), not Vikunja sessions or API / CalDAV tokens already issued: refresh sessions end after 24 h without use (VIKUNJA_SERVICE_JWTTTL, upstream 72 h / 30 days), an active one keeps refreshing; disable the user in Vikunja to end it, effective within 10 min (vikunja user change-status). Mobile and desktop apps sign in through Vikunja's own OAuth flow in the browser, i.e. through Portcullis. Upgrades: database migrations run when Vikunja starts; don't bump the PostgreSQL major.

items.title: 📖 Wiki.js
items.text:
Modern wiki with Portcullis sign-in (OpenID Connect) and group-based rights

Category: productivity Tags: wiki, docs, knowledge-base Website: https://js.wiki/ Source: https://github.com/requarks/wiki

items.title: Authentication
items.text:
Property Value Method native-oidc SSO Yes Group Access Group Admin Access Group users_wiki Admin Group admin_wiki Subdomain wiki

Auth Notes

Native OIDC through Wiki.js' generic OpenID Connect strategy (key "portcullis"), configured by the wiki-setup sidecar at every start over the internal network (GraphQL, with its own API key kept in the wiki-setup-data volume). One Portcullis login: the login page offers only "Portcullis". No password login: the sidecar disables the local strategy (and its self-registration), so the internet-facing GraphQL login and register mutations refuse local accounts. Traefik only routes the wiki while its healthcheck passes, which needs the Portcullis strategy enabled and the local one disabled: the setup wizard of a fresh install, and a re-enabled local login, get 404 from Traefik. Identity: Wiki.js keys accounts on the OIDC subject (the Keycloak id of the LLDAP user, never the email; Wiki.js has no username-claim option). It requires an email claim and keeps emails unique per strategy, so an account's email is only profile data, but: it would link a login to a user an admin pre-created for this strategy with the same email (never pre-create users for the Portcullis strategy), and a user who sets their LLDAP email to another user's address makes the later login of whichever of them is second fail (denial of service, no takeover; fix the email in LLDAP). Rights come only from groups: new accounts get no group, and at each login Wiki.js sets the user's membership of the Wiki.js groups users_wiki (editors, created once; adjust its rights in Wiki.js) and admin_wiki (manage:system, re-applied every start) from the groups claim. A realm user outside access_group can't sign in (Keycloak denies it, see below) and would have no rights anyway. The Guests group has no permissions (re-applied before every boot by wiki-init and by the sidecar), so nothing is readable anonymously. Removing a user from the groups takes effect at their next login (Wiki.js sessions last up to 14 days). Break-glass, on the server only: docker compose -p portcullis- exec wiki-db psql -U wiki -d wiki -c "UPDATE authentication SET \"isEnabled\" = true WHERE key = 'local'", restart the wiki container, open Wiki.js directly on its container address (e.g. an SSH tunnel to :3000; Traefik serves 404 meanwhile) and sign in as admin@wiki.invalid with WIKI_ADMIN_PASSWORD; the next start of the app (Hub) disables the local login again. Existing installs: local accounts can no longer sign in; reset or remove them in Administration > Users (as an SSO admin) since their passwords stay valid if the local login is ever re-enabled. If the sidecar has neither its API key nor the local admin admin@wiki.invalid / WIKI_ADMIN_PASSWORD (installs whose first admin had another email), it can't configure anything and the wiki stays unrouted: create that local admin through the break-glass steps and restart. Hostname: wiki-init writes the site URL from the instance's hostname before Wiki.js boots, so a hostname change only needs a restart. Sign-in is restricted to access_group in Keycloak (keycloak_access_role, contract §8 Access role): only access_group members can sign in, so a member of admin_group who is not also in access_group is denied — put the wiki's admins in both groups.

items.text:
Word processor by ArtCraft, running entirely in the browser (Rust/WebAssembly; files stay on your device). In development.

Category: productivity Tags: artcraft, wasm, word-processor, documents, office Website: https://getartcraft.com/apps/wordcraft Source: https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft

items.title: Authentication
items.text:
Property Value Method forward-auth SSO No Group Access Group Admin Access Group users_wordcraft Admin Group admin_wordcraft Subdomain wordcraft

Auth Notes

In development upstream (https://getartcraft.com/apps): expect missing features and breaking changes between versions. WordCraft (https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft, Apache-2.0 OR MIT) is a static site: the app runs in the visitor's browser and has no user system, no server-side code and no server-side storage. Open uses the browser's file picker, Save/Export download files; preferences live in the browser's storage for this hostname. Portcullis sign-in (forward-auth + group-gate) is the only login; every member of the access group gets the same app (there are no roles). At every start the wordcraft-fetch init container downloads the release's wordcraft-web-.zip from GitHub, checks its SHA-256 against the pin before unpacking, and swaps the unpacked site into the wordcraft-site volume by rename; on any error it exits non-zero and the web server doesn't start (an unchanged pin skips the download). The host needs outbound HTTPS to github.com. The web server (nginx-unprivileged, read-only, no directory listing) answers only Traefik and itself. Version: the Release version / Release SHA-256 settings default to the pin in compose.yml (bumped with the template); set both together, from the release's SHA256SUMS.txt, to pin another release.

items.title: 🐝 Zigbee2MQTT
items.text:
Zigbee to MQTT bridge with its web frontend and a bundled, password-protected Mosquitto broker

Category: home-automation Tags: home-automation, zigbee, mqtt, iot, smart-home Website: https://www.zigbee2mqtt.io/ Source: https://github.com/Koenkk/zigbee2mqtt

items.title: Authentication
items.text:
Property Value Method forward-auth SSO No Group Access Group Admin Access Group users_zigbee2mqtt Admin Group admin_zigbee2mqtt Subdomain zigbee

Auth Notes

Zigbee2MQTT 2.14 has no user system: its frontend's only protection is an optional shared auth_token. It runs without one here: forward-auth + group-gate on the whole host is the sign-in, and every member of the access group has full control (pairing, device settings, OTA, the network key in Settings). The frontend is on the instance's private network only; the gate in front of it (nginx, the only container on portcullis-proxy) answers Traefik's address alone, so no other container reaches it unauthenticated. Zigbee2MQTT's onboarding wizard and failure page never open (Z2M_ONBOARD_NO_SERVER): they would configure the instance for whoever reaches them first; the instance settings are applied at every start instead (they override edits made in the frontend's Settings for the same keys). Coordinator: set either "Serial device" (the host path of a USB coordinator, best a stable /dev/serial/by-id/... path; only that device is passed into the container, not privileged, so several instances can each drive their own coordinator; a path that doesn't exist on the host stops the container from starting) or "Network coordinator" (tcp://host:port of an Ethernet/Wi-Fi coordinator such as an SLZB-06 or a ser2net bridge, reached outbound, with its Adapter type); with neither, Zigbee2MQTT is not started and its log says what to set. No host networking is needed: mDNS discovery of network coordinators isn't available, give their address. MQTT: by default the bundled Mosquitto 2.1 on the instance's private network, anonymous clients refused, two accounts with generated passwords (zigbee2mqtt for the bridge, homeassistant for Home Assistant), ACL limited to zigbee2mqtt/# and homeassistant/# (the base topic is fixed to zigbee2mqtt). The homeassistant account has an allowlist only (Zigbee2MQTT matches bridge requests case-insensitively, so writes are never denylisted): discovery (read homeassistant/#, write homeassistant/status), device and group state, endpoint state, availability and device-trigger actions, the bridge's state, info (its configuration without the network key, MQTT password and frontend token), devices, groups and event topics (never bridge/logging, where Zigbee2MQTT logs every MQTT publish with its payload, the extension / converter JavaScript source, definitions or health), [/]/set|get commands and the permit_join request; never other bridge requests (extensions, converters, options, backup, restart, OTA updates, ...) nor bridge responses. So in Home Assistant the bridge's log level select and restart button and the firmware update entities (Zigbee2MQTT OTA update requests) are refused, and Home Assistant can't clear retained discovery messages (deleting a device in Home Assistant leaves its discovery config; remove the device in Zigbee2MQTT, which clears it). Use friendly names without "/" (availability and two-level names aren't covered), or your own broker via "MQTT server". External JavaScript (extensions and converters, arbitrary code) is off unless the instance setting turns it on. The gate never forwards the Portcullis session (Authorization, access-token headers, forward-auth cookies) to the frontend. Passwords are written hashed by mosquitto-init at every start; Zigbee2MQTT stores its own MQTT password in configuration.yaml in its data volume (upstream behaviour). Or set "MQTT server" (+ user and password) to use an existing broker, e.g. the one Home Assistant uses (the bundled broker then idles). Home Assistant: with "Home Assistant discovery" on, Zigbee2MQTT publishes discovery messages; in Home Assistant add the MQTT integration with the broker address host:, user homeassistant and the password Z2M_BROKER_HA_PASSWORD from this instance's .env (Hub data env/.env). The MQTT port (default 1883) is bound to 127.0.0.1 by default; set its bind address to the host's LAN address (or 0.0.0.0) for a Home Assistant on another machine or in a container, or clear the port to keep the broker private. It is plain MQTT without TLS, protected by the password: use it on a trusted network only. Each instance needs its own MQTT port (the Hub's port collision check). The frontend's "Open in Home Assistant" links and device pages link to this instance's hostname.

items.title: Adding an App
items.text:
This guide walks through creating a new app template. Templates live in porelli/portcullis-templates, one directory per app at the repo root. The repo accepts outside contributions, including pull requests from forks.

Start with CONTRIBUTING.md

The templates repo's CONTRIBUTING.md is the authoritative checklist: auth method choice, compose and security rules, image pinning, and what CI runs. This page explains the same steps with examples.

items.title: Overview
items.text:
A template is:

<app-id>/
  manifest.yaml   # what the Hub shows and how auth is wired
  compose.yml     # how the app runs behind Traefik
  ...             # optional support files (config templates, setup scripts)
tests/apps/<app-id>.sh   # its CI test

A template can run as several instances (template contract v2, contracts §3.1): the default instance, whose id is the app ID, and any number of others an admin creates in the Hub, each with its own id, hostnames, data volumes, Keycloak clients and groups. When an admin enables an instance, the Hub:

  1. generates the instance's .env from the manifest (option values, generate: random secrets, referenced core variables) plus the instance variables: PORTCULLIS_INSTANCE, one PORTCULLIS_HOST_<ROUTER> per host router (the full hostname), PORTCULLIS_OIDC_CLIENT_ID(_<KEY>), PORTCULLIS_ACCESS_GROUP, PORTCULLIS_ADMIN_GROUP
  2. copies the directory to <core>/templates/<app-id>/ (every instance shares it)
  3. registers the instance's Keycloak clients (client id = the instance id)
  4. starts the compose file with the Hub's override as its own project, portcullis-<instance-id>
  5. publishes the instance's hostnames, group, admin paths and policy to group-gate (policy file keyed by full hostname)
  6. delivers the rest of its settings: data files (written before the start), hooks, token claims and request headers (see Declaring settings)

items.title: Step 1: Pick an app ID and a default subdomain
items.text:
The app ID is lowercase and matches ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$, e.g. uptime-kuma. It is the directory name and the default instance's id (other instances get ids an admin chooses). Pick a default subdomain <sub> no other template uses: the default instance runs on <sub>.<main domain>, a new instance is pre-filled with <sub>-<suffix>.<domain> on the domain the admin picks, and every hostname can be edited in the Hub. Core subdomains (auth, traefik, hub, directory, enroll, people, metrics, mcp) are off limits. A hostname belongs to at most one instance: the Hub refuses a second one.

git clone https://github.com/porelli/portcullis-templates.git
cd portcullis-templates
mkdir myapp

items.title: Step 2: Choose the auth method
items.text:
The app... auth.method Router middlewares speaks OpenID Connect and can be pointed at Keycloak native-oidc (+ keycloak_clients) no portcullis-auth; the app logs users in itself can create/log in users from a trusted header (X-Forwarded-User) header-auth portcullis-auth@docker,portcullis-groups@docker has its own login (or none) and no SSO forward-auth portcullis-auth@docker,portcullis-groups@docker is protected by a YubiKey certificate at the TLS handshake only (browser certificates are refused there) mtls tls.options: protected@file, no forward-auth uses a vendor account system (e.g. plex.tv) custom (+ auth.native_login if it has its own login) none: the Hub adds Portcullis sign-in through its override is meant to be public public none

Prefer native-oidc when the app supports it well: mobile apps, API tokens and CLI clients keep working. Then check who can log in:

  • The app can restrict OIDC logins to a group. Configure it with access_group (users_<app-id>) and set group_access: true.
  • It cannot. Then any Keycloak realm user could sign in. Put only the interactive login paths behind forward-auth + group-gate, on a higher-priority PathPrefix router. Keep the API on the host-wide router without forward-auth. See gitlab/, litellm/ and vaultwarden/.
  • It has an admin panel on a path (e.g. Vaultwarden's /admin). Route the path through a gated PathPrefix router and list it in auth.admin_paths. group-gate then also requires admin_group there.

Give SSO-created users the least-privileged role the app has.

If the app has share links for people without an account (public file shares, shared dashboards), declare them in auth.public_access instead of adding an ungated router: the Hub generates the public router when an admin turns the exception on. Read the app's routes at the pinned version and keep the list narrow: {token} paths for per-share listing, static-only supporting paths, exact routes with a justification, and the app's login headers, cookies and query parameters in credential_*.

items.title: Step 3: Write manifest.yaml
items.text:
Copy a template with the same auth method and adapt it: grafana/ for header-auth, scrutiny/ for forward-auth, vaultwarden/ for native OIDC. All fields are documented in the Manifest Reference.

# yaml-language-server: $schema=../schema/manifest.schema.json
name: My App
description: A brief description of what the app does
icon: "\U0001F4E6"
category: productivity
tags: [example, demo]
links:
  website: https://myapp.example.org/
  source: https://github.com/example/myapp
instances: multi   # contract v2: one or many instances

auth:
  method: forward-auth
  sso: false
  group_access: true
  group_admin: false
  access_group: users_myapp
  admin_group: admin_myapp
  notes: Access gated by group-gate. No SSO -- uses its own login.

env:
  - key: MYAPP_SECRET
    description: Secret key for My App
    generate: random

keycloak_clients: []
config_files: []

urls:
  - label: My App
    url: "https://{{HOST_MYAPP}}"   # the instance's hostname of router myapp

ai:
  unsupported: "No official MCP server; community servers are small and not vetted by Portcullis"

items.title: Declaring AI support
items.text:
Every manifest has an ai: block (reference, contracts §3.2), in exactly one of two forms:

  • unsupported: one sentence saying why the AI can't act in the app (no MCP server, no per-person identity, a password vault, a public site, …). Optionally an alternative {name, source, note}: a community server an admin may evaluate on their own. The Hub shows it labelled "not vetted by Portcullis" and never installs it.
  • mcp: the app's companions. A companion is the app's built-in MCP server (kind: builtin) or a service running the upstream project's, or a vetted community project's, published image (kind: companion), pinned by digest. Never MCP server, adapter or proxy code written for Portcullis. Vet a community project first: maintained, an open licence, a multi-user identity that fits an identity mode, no shared admin identity running tool calls, a pinned release; record why in the template's notes.

Choose the identity mode by what the app offers:

The app has Mode You write per-person API tokens or app passwords an admin CLI can create app_token mint and revoke hooks (when: [ai]) that create a portcullis-ai-<random> credential for the given user (exit 3 when the person has no account yet; never create accounts) and delete credentials by id, or every portcullis-ai-* one for revoke_all a server that trusts identity headers from one caller identity_headers a caller_secret (a generate: random env entry) the companion requires, and a trust network so the app trusts the headers only from the companion its own OAuth-protected MCP route that signs in through Keycloak app_oauth a revoke hook that ends a person's AI tokens by their Keycloak id (sub), or everyone's for revoke_all

Then classify the tools: writes (hidden in read-only mode), confirm (deletes and anything that sends data out: the person approves with a passkey) and never (tools that would put a secret in front of the model, or open access). The gate also confirms tools the companion marks destructive. Hooks get one JSON document on stdin, and their stdout is never stored (§15.5).

The companion's alias and router are the Hub's: portcullis-mcp- appears nowhere in compose.yml, the companion service has no Traefik labels, no host ports and isn't on portcullis-proxy, and it reads ${PORTCULLIS_AI_READONLY_<NAME>:-true} to start read-only. See gitea/ (app_token), grafana/ (identity_headers), nextcloud/ (app_token with HTTP Basic) and homeassistant/ (app_oauth).

items.title: Declaring settings
items.text:
Anything an admin should be able to change (a library folder, a quota, a role, an API key) is an option under settings:. The template declares what the option is and how the app reads it; the Hub validates the value, works out who gets what and delivers it. Copy the closest pilot: immich/ (per-person claims), grafana/ (per-person header), nextcloud/ (a live hook), firefox-sync/ (values each person enters, in a data file).

settings:
  sections: [Library]
  options:
    - key: trash_days              # an identifier, not an env name
      label: Keep deleted items for
      type: int
      unit: days
      min: 0
      max: 3650
      default: 30
      section: Library
      applies: restart             # the app reads it at start
      delivery: [{env: IMMICH_TRASH_DAYS}]

Decide three things for each option:

  1. Its type: string, int, size, duration, bool, enum, multi_enum, list, table, path, secret, group(s) or user(s), with the type's constraints (pattern, min / max, options, …). Sizes are bytes and durations seconds; write them with units (10GiB, 30d). Credentials the admin enters are type: secret, never an env entry.
  2. Its scope: instance (the default: one value), person (a default plus values per group, resolved per person with resolve), group (records per group, delivered as a whole) or person_entered (each person enters their own, see below).
  3. How the app reads it (delivery) and when a change takes effect (applies):
The app reads it… Delivery applies from an environment variable at start {env: NAME}; compose uses ${NAME…} restart as a bind-mounted host folder type: path with target: {service, mount} (no delivery) restart from a token claim at sign-in (native OIDC) {claim: {client, name, json_type, render}} next_sign_in from a request header (forward-auth / header-auth) {header: {name: X-Forwarded-Attr-<Name>}} next_request from a JSON file at start {file: {name}} + a files: entry restart (or reload) through its own API or CLI, while running {hook: <name>} + a hooks: entry live

A person option needs a per-person delivery (claim, header, file or hook); one environment variable can't carry a value per person. Values are rendered per delivery with render (unit: GiB, unlimited: "-1", join: ",", format: json), so the Hub stores one canonical value and each app gets the form it understands.

Per-person roles and admin flags are privileged: true: their default is the lowest value, and group_values may preset only the instance's admin group ("{{ADMIN_GROUP}}": Admin). The Hub then accepts rows only from groups delegates can't steer.

The complete list of fields and rules is in the Manifest Reference; tests/validate.py refuses exactly what the Hub refuses, with the same messages.

items.title: Host folders, doctor checks and LAN-only ports
items.text:
If the app reads or writes a host folder (media libraries, photos, a recordings folder), give the path option a folder block instead of mode, needs and writes_as. It tells the Hub what the app does there and as which ids, so an admin can point the setting at a shared folder that several apps use with consistent ownership:

    - key: movies_path
      label: Movies folder
      type: path
      target: {service: jellyfin, mount: /data/movies}
      folder:
        access: read                  # read is always mounted read-only
        runs_as: {uid: 0, gid: 0}     # the ids the process has: here root, no compose user:
      applies: restart

Check what the image really does before you choose runs_as and joins_group:

  • Which uid and gid the app's process has (docker exec … id). With a compose user:, the numbers must match it; with user: "${PUID:-1000}:${PGID:-1000}", use uid_env: PUID / gid_env: PGID (both instance int options).
  • Whether it keeps supplementary groups. The default group_add adds the folder's gid as a supplementary group. Images that start the app through s6-setuidgid, su -g or a similar switch drop it.
