      • create_instance takes label (required), groups ({mode: new} or {mode: existing, users, admins}) and setup (setup option key → value), exactly the create body of §11.9; its class is decided per call as above (binding an existing group with people is D).
      • set_instance_label (class W, idempotentHint) twins PUT /api/instances/{id}/label: arguments id, label; it answers the instance.
      • save_env is gone. set_env_override (class D; arguments id, name, value) and clear_env_override (class D; arguments id, name) twin PUT / DELETE /api/instances/{id}/env/{name} and answer {row, effect}; get_env answers {rows} (§11.9), masked like its twin. A reset can switch an app's behaviour back as much as an override can, so both are D.
      • get_logs keeps its optional service argument (one container's logs, §11.9).

    • New tools and arguments (NEW (DNS hardening), §12):

      • get_domain_dns (class R; arguments name, optional refresh) answers the domain's DNS plan (§12.2); get_main_dns (class R; optional refresh) the main domain's read-only plan (can_write: false).
      • apply_domain_dns (class W; arguments name, sets) applies those record sets and answers the domain object; audited domain.dns_apply (detail sets=<a,b>).
      • enable_domain_dnssec (class D; argument name) turns on DNSSEC signing: the confirmation says it is zone-wide (the whole zone <zone>, the user's other names included) and can't be undone from Portcullis. It answers the domain object, or isError 409: "can't sign"; audited domain.dnssec_enable. No tool turns signing off.
      • domain_op (class R; argument name) answers the op record of the domain's last doctor DNS fix (op key _domain.<name>, §14.6), like folder_op. The DNS fixes themselves go through doctor_preview_fix / doctor_apply_fix (dns_apply, dnssec_sign: touches_data false; doctor_apply_fix is W for dns_apply and D for dnssec_sign, which signs the whole zone).

    • New tool (NEW (rootless), §11.10): get_runtime (class R; no arguments) answers GET /api/runtime's JSON.

    • VPN routes without a tool (NEW, VPN). PUT /api/vpn/settings and POST /api/instances/{id}/vpn-dns/ack are admin UI only. No tool creates a VPN device or a config, so no key lands in a transcript; the people resource has no VPN tool.

    • Never tools. The confirmation routes (GET /confirm/{id}, POST /api/me/confirmations/{id}: an AI must never approve its own confirmation), credential create and revoke (/api/me/apps/{instance}/credentials/{key}: my_file_share_password only returns the People-page link), the multipart CSV import/review (import_review takes JSON and calls what the route's JSON branch calls; its twin is import/apply's), and the page, /static/ and /healthz. NEW (sign-in part 2): the YubiKey renewal (POST /api/me/signin/yubikey-certificate/renew: it needs the certificate the browser presents) and both history routes (GET /api/me/signin/history, GET /api/directory/users/{u}/signin/history; my_sign_in carries the last 20 entries) have no twin; DELETE /api/me/signin/password has no tool either (removing your password is done on the Sign-in page, where my_password hands off); mcp_parity_test.go lists them with that reason. GET /signin is a page. There is no my_certificates: my_sign_in lists the certificates. NEW (sign-in part 3): the impersonation start (POST /api/directory/users/{u}/impersonation: "needs the admin's fresh YubiKey touch and a typed reason; never by an AI"), switching it on (PUT /api/signin/impersonation: "switched on in Hub Settings only"; listed once, turn_off_impersonation covers allowed: false) and every /api/me/impersonation* route ("the impersonating browser only") have no tool; mcp_parity_test.go lists each with that reason. GET /impersonation/stop is a page. A browser signed in as someone else can't reach the Portcullis MCP at all (§15.2). NEW (polish 1): PUT /api/me/signin/passkeys/{credentialId}/label has no tool, with the reason "naming your passkeys: on the Sign-in page, where you can see which key is which (my_sign_in lists names and models)"; mcp_parity_test.go lists it.
    • Answers. Tool errors are isError results prefixed <status>: (an OpError as its JSON record, redacted and clipped); a people tool refused for a missing permission is 403: not allowed: needs <perm> and, like every W, D and U refusal before Run, audited refused under the twin's action; a non-admin on /mcp/admin gets empty lists and the JSON-RPC error "admins only" for reads and prompts; while the caller can't be resolved (the directory is down) a tools/call still gets a tool result (isError), never a protocol error; a request without an identity on the MCP listener is 403 (§15.7). wait_for_op answers {done, record} and get_op the record, both with the record's steps and created (NEW (operation progress)); stop_op the record (stopping: true); get_instance mirrors the last-operation route; audit_recent {entries, offset, next_offset} (limit 1–200, default 50, offset ≤ 10000, optional via=ai, NEW (people & groups): optional group and user filters); create_person / send_invite state {created, expires_at, note} (never the link); invite_person {exists, created_by, last_invite, expires_at, pending} (the caller's own invite; pending is evidence, not proof); my_file_share_password {link, note}; revoke_ai_access {status, instance, companion, user}; ai_activity {lines} (default 50); add_domain / replace_domain_token answer {name, added, domain, note} (added: whether the Hub lists the domain now), and replace_domain_token also reports last_replaced from the audit log; preview_settings carries the plan_hash save_settings needs; doctor_preview_fix the FixPlan with touches_data always present; check_folder_path creates nothing. A Hub method an AI actor reaches without a confirmation where one is required answers 409 (defence in depth: a data fix, a widening assignment, an undo, a folder delete, a re-check of a different directory).
    • Refused arguments. set_env_override (NEW (apps), formerly save_env) refuses secret-looking and Hub-owned names (a client secret_env, a generated variable, [set]) on the tool path, as its twin does (§11.9); add_source refuses URLs with credentials; save_hub_settings refuses turning the admin MCP on (403, checked and audited refused before its class is judged, so no confirmation is created for it). The global redactor never hides PORTCULLIS_HOST_* and the other Hub-set public instance variables for their name.
    • U tools. The first call answers the form's URL (a URL elicitation, or the text "secrets are never passed through the AI; use "); the tool runs only on a 2026-07-28 retry whose input reply is accept. Text-only clients never reach it: they get the link, and an R tool reports the result. Input keys: portcullis_confirmation (D) and portcullis_secret_form (U). Deep links: #app/<id>/settings[/<option>], #app/<id>/ai, #settings/domains?add=<name>[&provider=<p>], #settings/domains?token=<name>, #settings/ai?provider=<name>&field=<field> (Hub); #users/<name>[?password|?invite] (the person's page, then the prompt), #invite?username=&email=&display_name=[&groups=] (the invite form; groups= — admin forms only — carries only plain groups — known and guarding nothing, none while the directory can't be read — and the form never ticks an administrator or permission group from a link) and #myapps (people page). NEW (people & groups): the person forms (create_person, send_invite, set_password, the invite note) link to https://people.<d>/, no longer to the Hub, whose old #users… links redirect there (#users/<name> → #people/<name>, #users?create&… → #invite?…).
    • Resources and prompts. portcullis://docs/<name> (both scopes), portcullis://templates and portcullis://templates/{id}, portcullis://doctor/checks and the prompts are admin-only. Long operations send no progress notifications (stateless: the twin's 202 body at once, then wait_for_op).
    • Canonical JSON. The Hub's internal/mcpsdk/canon.go is a copy of the gate's internal/canon (one can't import the other across repos); both keep the same vectors.

items.title: 15.11 Hub API, switches and audit
items.text:
Admin routes on the Hub listener only (adminOnly: no X-Forwarded-User 401, delegates 403), proxy-secret and CSRF guards, strict JSON bodies ≤ 64 KiB. Every answer shows secrets as {set, updated_at} only.

Route Body Does GET /api/ai/settings — Settings → AI (gate_present: the Hub has a parseable gate recipient; without the gate secret file the MCP listener doesn't start either, §15.7; no field reports a client's health: an unhealthy client is left out of the gate file and the People cards without the UI saying so): {enabled, gate_present, clients: {claude: {offered, admin}, claude_code: {offered, admin}, generic: {offered, admin}}, portcullis_admin, portcullis_people, offline_idle_days, offline_max_days, limits: {resource_rpm, resource_burst, person_rpm, tool_calls_rpm, confirmations_per_hour, mints_per_minute, fanout}, allowed_origins} PUT /api/ai/settings the same fields but gate_present (only what changed) Save; audited settings.ai with the changed keys. Defaults on a new install: enabled false, all three clients offered with admin off (§8: the admin enables it client by client), both Portcullis MCPs on, 7 / 30 days, the limits of §15.9, no origins. Idle 1–30, max 1–90 days, idle ≤ max; origins https://<host>[:port]; else 400 GET /api/ai/providers · POST /api/ai/providers provider (§15.12), no secret fields List {providers} (secrets per field {set, updated_at}, used_by [{instance, group, people, restarts}]) · add: 201 {provider} (ai.provider.add) PUT · DELETE /api/ai/providers/{name} provider · — Update: {provider, restarts} (ai.provider.update; restarts the enabled AI page instances re-delivered and restarted) · delete (ai.provider.delete; 409 naming the instances while any selects it; its secrets removed) PUT /api/ai/providers/{name}/secrets/{field} {"value": "…"} or {"clear": true} Set or clear one secret field; answers {set, updated_at, restarts}; audited ai.provider.secret (<field> replaced / cleared) GET /api/instances/{id}/ai — The instance's AI tab: {unsupported, alternative, master_off, refused, companions: [{name, label, url, kind, identity_mode, upstream, source, modes, mode, enabled, status, last_error, population, credentials, revoking, connections, confirm, never, own_rules, unmatched}], providers, provider_kinds} (refused the reason a switch-on would be refused, e.g. a rule that needs a certificate; own_rules for app_oauth; unmatched the app_oauth leavers to dismiss, §15.5; providers and provider_kinds (kind → one/many) only for ai.chat; connections is always 0: Keycloak has no per-scope count, and the UI hides it) PUT /api/instances/{id}/ai {"companions": {"<name>": {"enabled": true, "mode": "read_write"}}, "providers": ["…"]} (one part per request: both is 400) Switch companions on / off, change modes (ai.enable, ai.disable, ai.mode before → after) or, for ai.chat templates, set the provider selection (ai.providers, detail <before> -> <after>); (NEW (operation progress)) a companion switch or mode change on an enabled instance (it restarts the app and runs its hooks) runs in the background: 202 {op_id, op: "ai", instance, poll} (§11.7; steps revoke, scopes, restart, hooks; the warnings in the record's warnings); on a disabled instance (state, scopes and gate file only) and for the provider selection it answers 200 with the tab plus restarts (true when an enabled instance's project is recreated, §3.2) and warnings POST /api/instances/{id}/ai/revoke {"companion": "…", "user": "…"} (user omitted = everyone) Revoke one person's or everyone's AI credentials for a companion now (revoke / revoke_all); answers {status: "revoked", instance, companion, user} (user everyone for all); audited ai.credential.revoke. 409 for identity_headers (nothing to revoke), and for an app_oauth person with no recorded or an unverifiable record POST /api/instances/{id}/ai/dismiss {"user": "…", "companion": "…"} (companion omitted = every companion) Dismiss an unmatched app_oauth leaver (§15.5) once the admin has deactivated the account in the app; answers {status: "dismissed", instance, user}; audited ai.credential.revoke dismissed GET /api/ai/activity?instance=&user=&n= — {lines}: access-log lines (§15.8), newest first, filtered by instance and user (lowercased) when given; n 1–200 when given (else 400), default 50 GET /api/directory/audit?via=ai[&include=access] — via=ai: the last 100 audit entries with via: ai ([AuditEntry]); with include=access, merged with the last 100 access-log lines as [{source: "audit"\|"access", time, entry\|line}], newest first. include without via=ai, or another value, is 400
  • Switching on (PUT …/ai, a companion enabled: true): refused 409 while the master switch is off, the instance is deleting / restoring, the template has ai.unsupported, the instance's sign-in rule needs a certificate on every alternative (signin.NeedsCertificate: "needs a YubiKey or browser certificate on every sign-in"; AI clients can't present one), or another container answers the alias (§3.2); 404 unknown companion; 400 a mode outside modes. Steps: revoke_all (§15.5; failure 502, nothing changed) → state saved → scope ensured and attached (§8) → gate files → override + compose up on an enabled instance (the app restarts) → on_change; in the op record they are the steps revoke, scopes, restart and hooks. NEW (operation progress): on an enabled instance the 202 comes once the request's refusals (above) are checked and the lock is held, so a revoke_all failure is the operation's failure (status: 502, nothing changed). A failure after the state save is an OpError (op ai); the same request re-applies every step. Stop (§11.7) puts the companion's previous {enabled, mode} back through the same path; credentials the stopped switch revoked are minted again lazily. Switching off reverses it: router, alias and scope removed, scale: 0, revoke_all, entries removed, on_change enabled: false.
  • Sign-in saves (NEW, sign-in). A sign-in change (§8.1: a method switch, a template edit, the default or an instance's pick) that makes an instance's rule need a certificate on every alternative first switches AI support off on those instances (audited ai.disable, detail sign-in needs a YubiKey or browser certificate); the instance settings preview and the template preview list them.
  • Signing in as someone else (NEW, sign-in part 3). Its switch is in Settings → Sign-in (PUT /api/signin/impersonation, §8.1 "Impersonation"), not in Settings → AI. An AI may only turn it off (turn_off_impersonation, W), list impersonations (impersonations, R) and stop one (stop_impersonation, W); it can never start one or switch the feature on. AI support never mixes with an impersonation: mcp-gate refuses impersonated tokens (§15.2), and Keycloak refuses AI clients in an impersonated browser (§8.1).
  • Master switch. On: the offered AI clients exist and follow Settings → AI (§8). Off: the gate refuses everything (enabled: false), per-app switches are greyed out, People cards are hidden; clients and scopes are kept.
  • State: state.yaml ai (the Settings → AI values and provider definitions; never a secret) and ai_instances (per instance id {companions: {<name>: {enabled, mode}}, providers}); per-instance AI state is in backups (§11.5).

items.title: 15.12 Model providers and the AI page
items.text:
An AI page is an instance of a template with ai.chat (the ai-chat template, LibreChat): an MCP client whose one MCP server is "all my apps" through its ai_client (§8, scope mcp:all). Its models come from the providers in Settings → AI.

  • Provider: {name, label, kind, instance, base_url, region, instance_name, api_version, deployments, models: {fetch, list}, credentials}. name ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,30}$, unique; label single line ≤ 64 (shown to people with the data-egress note "What people send on the AI page, and what their apps return to it, goes to ."); credentials admin (default) or per_person; azure_openai can't use per_person (the AI page can't take each person's own Azure key), so the Hub answers 400 to an add or an update that sets it. Per kind: kind Fields Secret fields litellm instance (an installed LiteLLM instance; the Hub fills base_url from it) key openai_compatible base_url (required) key (optional: Ollama needs none) anthropic, openai, google base_url (optional) key bedrock region access_key_id, secret_access_key azure_openai instance_name or base_url, api_version, deployments key

    The litellm kind is tied to the LiteLLM template by name, an exception to "no template id in Hub code" (ruling T9): its instance must be an instance of the template litellm, and base_url is https:// + the host of that instance's router litellm.

    models.fetch only for litellm, openai_compatible, openai. A kind is offered only while an installed ai.chat template declares it (400 "no installed AI page supports kind " otherwise).

  • Secrets are write-only. Entered in type=password inputs, cleared on submit, never rendered back. Stored only in <data>/ai/provider-secrets.json (0600, atomic; the Hub's secret store for providers) and in the .env of each AI page instance that selected the provider, single-quoted, as PORTCULLIS_AI_PROVIDER_<NAME>_<FIELD> (<NAME> and <FIELD> upper-cased, - → _). Never in state.yaml, ai-providers.json, logs, the audit, op records, errors, answers or tool results. A provider whose variable for any field would equal another provider's (x + secret_access_key vs x-secret-access + key) is a 409.

    • Delivery to the app. The Hub's override adds environment: {<VAR>: ${<VAR>}} for each selected provider variable to the ai.chat.env.service only (§3.2); templates never reference the variables.
    • Masked and blanked. Expert Env shows a set provider variable as [set] and SaveEnv treats them as Hub-set (a changed value is 400); backups blank them by name; a restore and a restore-as rewrite them from the store for that instance's own selection only; every provider secret value is in the redaction set (§15.10).
  • Selection per AI page instance: PUT /api/instances/{id}/ai providers (§15.11). An instance with no selection yet gets the default at create and at its first enable: every provider whose kind the template supports, and for a one kind the first by name; from then on the selection is the admin's (it never follows new providers, and an emptied one stays empty); two providers of a one kind, or a kind the template doesn't declare, is a 400. A change re-delivers ai-providers.json (§3.2) and the env and restarts that instance only. A provider update, a secret change and a hostname change of the LiteLLM instance a provider points at restart every enabled AI page that renders it (named in restarts); every affected page's .env is rewritten at once, disabled ones included. Deleting a LiteLLM instance a provider points at is 409. Everyone who can open an instance can use every provider selected for it; to give a group other providers, the admin adds another ai-chat instance with its own access group.
  • Hub Settings → AI shows, per provider, the instances using it with their access groups and population counts, and the reachability note "Claude desktop and claude.ai connect from Anthropic's servers (160.79.104.0/21): auth.<domain> and every app host must be reachable from the internet."

items.title: 16. VPN and the wg service — NEW (VPN)
items.text:
Core's wg service is one Go binary (wg/ in core) running WireGuard on a userspace network stack (wireguard-go and the gVisor netstack): no capabilities, no TUN device, no kernel module. It has two roles, edge and people. The VPN is always an extra condition after the normal sign-in, never a sign-in method or factor. wg never touches the engine socket, and the Hub reads its state from wg_data/status.json, never through the engine.

  • Roles:
    • edge: the only PROXY v2 client of Traefik's vpnsecure, which it reaches over portcullis-vpn-edge. On wg's portcullis-vpn address it has exactly one TCP listener per wired provider (9001 + slot) and nothing else. It also takes the people role's TCP 443 connections in-process, as provider builtin. It checks every claimed client address against the provider's ranges and its fresh device map, then re-originates the connection to vpnsecure with PROXY v2. No UDP, no WireGuard key.
    • people (the built-in provider, on when PORTCULLIS_VPN_BUILTIN=on and the key file isn't empty): one WireGuard device with key secrets/wg/people.key, UDP ${PORTCULLIS_VPN_PORT:-51820}, tunnel ${PORTCULLIS_VPN_SUBNET:-10.213.0.0/22} with the server at .1, MTU 1280. Clients get AllowedIPs = 10.213.0.1/32 and DNS = 10.213.0.1 (a split tunnel). Its peers come from vpn.json builtin.peers (§4). Its netstack listeners, at 10.213.0.1 on the tunnel only: TCP 443 (handed to the edge), TCP 80 (308 to https), UDP and TCP 53 (the resolver, below).
    • The link role (multi-server). Server-to-server tunnels are not part of this service yet. Reserved for them: secrets/wg/link.key, ${PORTCULLIS_LINK_PORT:-51821}/udp and ${PORTCULLIS_LINK_SUBNET:-10.214.0.0/24}. The multi-server design reuses this section for the link role.
  • Separation. The roles share code, nothing else: each tunnel has its own WireGuard device, gVisor stack, private key, UDP port and subnet, and the subnets are disjoint. There is no forwarding code between stacks: the people stack's only outbound path is the edge to vpnsecure. One role failing to load (for instance a non-empty builtin.server_public_key that doesn't match its key) sets that role's ok: false in status.json, and the other keeps running.
  • Networks and addresses:
    • portcullis-vpn (internal, ${PORTCULLIS_VPN_NET:-172.31.254.0/26}, dynamic range ${PORTCULLIS_VPN_IP_RANGE:-172.31.254.8/29} so no dynamic address takes a pinned one): wg at ${PORTCULLIS_VPN_WG_IP:-172.31.254.3}, where the edge listens, and the wired gateways at .16–.62 (slot 0 → .16, slot 46 → .62). Nothing else joins it; Traefik isn't on it.
    • portcullis-vpn-edge (internal, ${PORTCULLIS_VPN_EDGE_SUBNET:-172.31.254.64/28}, dynamic range ${PORTCULLIS_VPN_EDGE_IP_RANGE:-172.31.254.72/29}): exactly Traefik at ${PORTCULLIS_VPN_EDGE_TRAEFIK_IP:-172.31.254.66} and wg at ${PORTCULLIS_VPN_EDGE_WG_IP:-172.31.254.67}. Traefik's vpnsecure (.66:8443) listens there and trusts PROXY v2 only from .67. Only the edge opens connections to vpnsecure.
    • wg-egress: publishes the people UDP port and carries the resolver's upstream queries.
    • portcullis-metrics-wg (internal): wg and Prometheus only; wg's metrics listen on wg-metrics:9100 there (Prometheus job wg).

  • Edge ports and accept rules. Provider p (slot n) has the edge port 9001 + n (9001–9047) and the gateway address .16 + n, both in vpn.json (edge_port, gateway_ip) and in the gateway's PORTCULLIS_VPN_EDGE (§3.3). A connection on p's port is admitted only when all of these hold:

    1. the port is p's edge_port (else wrong_port);
    2. its TCP peer address is p's gateway_ip (else wrong_gateway);
    3. it starts with a PROXY v2 header, TCP over IPv4, within 5 s (else no_header or slow_header; an IPv6 source is outside_ranges);
    4. the header's source address lies in p's ranges (else outside_ranges): a gateway claiming another provider's address is closed here;
    5. p is fresh by the edge's own clock (else stale);
    6. the address is a device of p, unexpired, and for builtin with its unexpired peer (else not_in_map).

    With no valid vpn.json every connection is refused (no_doc). Refusals are counted in wg_edge_rejected_total{provider,reason}, admissions in wg_edge_accepted_total{provider}. A built-in connection skips steps 1–3: the people tunnel hands it over in-process with its tunnel source address.

  • Edge connection limits. The edge caps open connections, each counted from accept (connections still waiting for their PROXY header included):

    • per provider: 1024;
    • per person: 128, across all of that person's devices and providers (keyed by the device's user in vpn.json);
    • per client address: 32.

    A connection over any cap is closed and counted as wg_edge_rejected_total{reason="busy"}.

  • Pressure eviction. Above 90% of a provider's cap, a new connection on it first closes the heaviest person's sessions on that provider that have been idle for at least 2 min (on a tie, the alphabetically smallest username), counted as wg_edge_closed_total{reason="pressure"}. Active sessions, and other people's sessions, are never closed this way. With the per-person cap, filling a provider takes at least 8 different people.

  • Limit settings. Core's .env keys PORTCULLIS_VPN_EDGE_MAX_PER_PROVIDER (default 1024), PORTCULLIS_VPN_EDGE_MAX_PER_USER (128), PORTCULLIS_VPN_EDGE_MAX_PER_CLIENT (32), PORTCULLIS_VPN_EDGE_PRESSURE_PERCENT (90) and PORTCULLIS_VPN_EDGE_PRESSURE_IDLE (2m), passed to wg as WG_EDGE_MAX_PER_PROVIDER, WG_EDGE_MAX_PER_USER, WG_EDGE_MAX_PER_CLIENT, WG_EDGE_PRESSURE_PERCENT and WG_EDGE_PRESSURE_IDLE. wg refuses to start unless per client ≤ per person ≤ per provider, the percentage is 1–100 and the idle time is at least 1 s.

  • Admitted connections are re-checked. The edge keeps every admitted (spliced) connection with the facts it was admitted on: provider, client address, device id and owner. On every vpn.json reload, and every 2 s, it re-runs the admission check against the current file and its own clock, and closes the connection when:

    • the file is missing or invalid, a past valid_until included (this closes every connection: no_doc);
    • the provider is gone or no longer owns the address (outside_ranges), or is stale (stale);
    • the device is gone, has expired, or now has another id or owner (revoked).

    It also closes every connection 12 h after admission (lifetime) and after 1 h with no byte in either direction (idle). Closes are counted in wg_edge_closed_total{provider,reason}. So a revocation, an expiry or a stale map ends open connections within 2 s, not only new ones. The people role also removes a revoked or expired peer from its tunnel.

  • Forwarding. The edge re-originates each admitted connection to vpnsecure with a new PROXY v2 header carrying the same client address. Traefik honours PROXY v2 only from wg's address (§5), so a gateway's own PROXY header sent straight to vpnsecure is never honoured.

  • Resolver (people role). A forwarding resolver at 10.213.0.1:53, upstream ${PORTCULLIS_VPN_DNS_UPSTREAM:-1.1.1.1,9.9.9.9}. For names under the domains of builtin.domains (the main domain and the added ones) it rewrites only answers that point at this server: A → 10.213.0.1, AAAA → NODATA. Foreign records pass untouched, CNAME chains included. It never sets AD on a rewritten answer and strips its RRSIGs. A client that validates DNSSEC itself fails on rewritten names; browser DNS-over-HTTPS bypasses the resolver, and VPN-only apps then show /vpn-required (§5).

  • Files:

    • secrets/wg/people.key: the people role's private key, 0640 group 10006, written by ./portcullis vpn init in place inside the wg container. An empty file means the people role is off; core always creates the empty placeholder, so the bind never makes a directory.
    • vpn_doc volume, vpn.json: the Hub's file (§4; volume 10001:10007, 2750, file 0640), mounted read-only in wg at /vpn-doc. wg is in group 10007 only: it has no hub_data mount and isn't in group 10001.

    • wg_data/status.json (0640, group 10001; the wg_data directory is owned 10006:10001, mode 2750): written by wg every 10 s, read by the Hub (which mounts wg_data read-only):

      {"version": 1, "written": "2026-11-13T14:30:00Z", "mode": "apps", "edge": {"ok": true, "error": ""},
 "people": {"ok": true, "error": "", "public_key": "<base64 public key>", "port": 51820, "subnet": "10.213.0.0/22", "mtu": 1280,
            "peers": [{"public_key": "<base64 public key>", "last_handshake": "2026-11-13T14:29:45Z"}]}}
      • version: exactly 1. written: RFC 3339 UTC. mode: PORTCULLIS_VPN_MODE.
      • people is null when the role is off. last_handshake is RFC 3339 UTC or null.
      • The Hub treats a file whose written is more than 30 s old, or more than 30 s in the future, as "wg down", and so does wg healthcheck.
      • The service (compose profile wg, off by default; ./portcullis vpn init adds wg to COMPOSE_PROFILES): built locally (build: ./wg), user: "10006:10006", group_add: ["10007"], read_only: true, cap_drop: ALL, no-new-privileges. No cap_add, devices, sysctls, /dev/net/tun, privileged, network_mode or engine socket. Volumes vpn_doc (read-only), wg_data:/data and the key bind. The engine publishes ${PORTCULLIS_VPN_PORT:-51820}/udp. It is the same on rootful Docker and rootless Podman: restart: always comes from docker-compose.podman.yml, and the key bind's Z from docker-compose.podman-selinux.yml. Rootless host preparation checks the operator's containers.conf default_subnet_pools (§3.3 "Reserved ranges"): a mismatch is a warning without the wg profile and a refusal with it.
      • Subcommands of the wg binary: run (the default), genkey <path> (writes a key, 0640; never prints it), keypair ({"private_key", "public_key"} on stdout, for the host CLI only), qr (stdin text → a terminal QR code), healthcheck, status (prints status.json), providers (an internal status view of vpn.json: per provider its id, label, ranges, device count, refreshed_at and freshness; no keys and no names). Usage errors exit 2.
      • The CLI (./portcullis vpn …):
        • vpn init [--builtin on|off] [--port N] [--subnet CIDR]: refuses a subnet that overlaps a Docker network, portcullis-vpn, the reserved link subnet or (from hub vpn host-info) a Local network or provider range, and suggests the next free /22 in 10.213.0.0/16. With --builtin on (the default) it generates the key. It writes PORTCULLIS_VPN_BUILTIN, PORTCULLIS_VPN_PORT and PORTCULLIS_VPN_SUBNET, adds wg to COMPOSE_PROFILES once, refreshes the Hub's core.env and starts wg, Traefik and the Hub.
        • vpn mode apps|admin|server [--force] [--public-enrol true|false]: writes PORTCULLIS_VPN_MODE, PORTCULLIS_VPN_PUBLIC_ENROL and the three PORTCULLIS_EP_* (§5), then recreates core. For admin and server it refuses unless hub vpn host-info says admin_device_seen (an lldap_admin member's device seen in the last 10 minutes on the built-in or a source: hook provider); --force overrides. vpn mode apps is the break-glass: it works with wg, every provider and the Hub down, because group-gate takes the mode from its own environment, not from the Hub's policy (§4).
        • vpn builtin on|off: off empties the key file and sets PORTCULLIS_VPN_BUILTIN=off; the edge keeps running. Either way wg is recreated.
        • vpn add-device <user> <name>:
      • wg keypair runs in the wg container, and the key pair stays in shell variables;
      • only the public key is piped to hub vpn add-device, and the Hub allocates the address and publishes vpn.json;
      • the config is assembled from environment variables and printed with a terminal QR (wg qr).

      The private key is never on a command line and never in a file.

    • vpn devices [--user U] [--json] and vpn revoke <device-id>, through hub vpn.

    • ./portcullis status shows the mode, each role's health, the built-in port and subnet, and per provider its label, ranges, devices and map age; with a mode other than apps, wg down is a Problem.
    • Host control socket. The Hub serves HTTP on the Unix socket /tmp/hub-host.sock (mode 0600, the Hub's tmpfs), and on no TCP listener: the /host/ routes are 404 on all three listeners. Its routes:
    • POST /host/vpn/devices (the public key in, VPNDeviceConfig out; any enabled person in the VPN users group);
    • GET /host/vpn/devices[?user=];
    • DELETE /host/vpn/devices/{id};
    • GET /host/vpn/info → {"local_networks", "provider_ranges", "admin_device_seen"}.

    Its only clients are the hub vpn add-device --user U --name N (public key on stdin, config JSON on stdout), hub vpn devices [--user U], hub vpn revoke <id> and hub vpn host-info subcommands, which ./portcullis vpn … runs inside the Hub container. The audit actor is host. A missing socket exits 1 with "the Hub isn't running".

  • The forwarder image ghcr.io/porelli/portcullis-forwarder. For VPN apps whose node can't send PROXY v2 itself because it has a real tunnel interface (NetBird, plain WireGuard). The forwarder runs with network_mode: service:<ingress.service> (§3.3), so it sees the clients' tunnel addresses.

    • It listens on ${FORWARDER_LISTEN:-:443} and forwards each connection to $PORTCULLIS_VPN_EDGE with a PROXY v2 header whose source is the address of the peer that connected to it (the client's tunnel address).
    • It exits 2 without a valid PORTCULLIS_VPN_EDGE. It runs as uid 65534.
    • A template that uses it adds cap_add: [NET_BIND_SERVICE] to bind :443.
    • Core publishes it from main as :edge and from each release vX.Y.Z as :X.Y.Z (signed with cosign, keyless); there is no latest. Templates pin it by digest.

items.title: Manifest Reference
items.text:
Every app template has a manifest.yaml that describes the app to the Hub. This page documents every field of the schema.

The authoritative definition is the JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) schema/manifest.schema.json in the templates repo. The Hub enforces the same rules and skips templates that fail them (see Integration Contracts §3). Rules that need the compose file, the filesystem or several templates at once are checked by tests/validate.py (see Validation).

For editor completion, start the manifest with:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=../schema/manifest.schema.json

items.title: Conventions
items.text:
Several types recur throughout the schema:

Type Rule single line A string without control characters (U+0000–U+001F, U+007F) env key ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,127}$. It becomes a key in the per-app .env group An LLDAP group name: ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,63}$ service A service name from the template's compose.yml: ^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9_.-]*$ {{DOMAIN}} In urls and redirect URIs, replaced with PORTCULLIS_DOMAIN (the main domain) {{HOST_<ROUTER>}} NEW (contract v2). In urls and redirect URIs, replaced with the instance's full hostname for host router <router> (<ROUTER> as in instances)

No other keys are allowed. Every object in the schema sets additionalProperties: false, so a typo is an error, not a silently ignored field.

items.title: Top-level fields
items.text:
Field Type Required Description name single line, 1–64 chars Yes Display name shown in the Hub description single line, 1–200 chars Yes One-line description of what the app does icon single line, 1–16 chars Yes Unicode emoji for the Marketplace card and Apps list, e.g. "\U0001F4CA" category ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$ Yes Catalog category tags list of unique strings ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.+-]{0,31}$ Yes Searchable tags (lowercase) links object Yes The app's own website and source repository. See links auth object Yes See auth settings object {sections, options} No Options set in the Hub (template contract v3). See settings files list No Data files for file deliveries. See files hooks list No Commands the Hub runs with the settings on stdin. See hooks reload object No The app's reload action. See reload ports list No See ports env list No See env keycloak_clients list No; required (at least one) for native-oidc See keycloak_clients config_files list No See config_files urls list No See urls tests object Yes, for templates in the default catalog (tests.signin; validate.py) CI only, the Hub ignores it. See tests.signin instances multi or single No (default single) NEW (contract v2). Whether the Hub may run more than the default instance. See instances hosts object No Per-host properties by host router name; today only immutable. See hosts.immutable jobs list of compose service names No NEW (apps). One-off setup services that exit when done. See jobs ai object Yes NEW (AI support). mcp (companions) or unsupported (the reason). See ai vpn object No NEW (VPN). The app is a VPN the Hub can wire as a VPN provider. See vpn

Categories in use: monitoring, media, productivity, security, networking, ai, devops, finance, vpn, remote-access, public.

items.title: links
items.text:
Where the app itself comes from. The docs site shows both on the app's page.

Field Type Required Description website https:// URL (≤ 512 chars, no credentials or placeholders) Yes The project's own homepage (not a mirror, store page or Docker Hub). If it has none, its repository or documentation site source https:// URL or null Yes The canonical upstream code repository (GitHub, GitLab, Codeberg, Gitea, SourceHut, …), or the repository the template's image is built from when that differs (name the upstream in auth.notes). null only for closed-source apps source_note single line, 10–200 chars Only with source: null Why there is no source repository, e.g. "Plex Media Server is proprietary"

tests/validate.py refuses registry and package pages, this templates repository, and non-repository URLs on known code hosts.

links:
  website: https://jellyfin.org/
  source: https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin

items.title: auth
items.text:
Field Type Required Description method enum Yes native-oidc, forward-auth, header-auth, mtls, custom or public (see below) sso true, false or "partial" Yes Whether single sign-on is supported group_access boolean Yes group-gate restricts the instance's hostnames to its access group (access_group for the default instance). For custom apps only while Portcullis sign-in is in front of them (native_login), or on a router-less custom template (no Traefik router), where the access group decides only who may create file-share passwords group_admin boolean Yes The app maps admin_group to its admin role access_group group If group_access: true LLDAP group required for access, by convention users_<app>. It is the default instance's group; every other instance uses users_<instance-id> (instances) admin_group group If group_admin: true or admin_paths is non-empty LLDAP group for admin privileges, by convention admin_<app>. The default instance's; other instances use admin_<instance-id> admin_paths list of path prefixes No Paths that additionally require admin_group (see below) public_access object No Public path exceptions: share-link paths the Hub can open without forward-auth (see auth.public_access) native_login object No The app has its own login and no SSO (method: custom only); enables the Hub's Sign-in setting (see auth.native_login) keycloak_access_role boolean No native-oidc only, needs access_group. Keycloak itself refuses sign-in to anyone outside the instance's access group (see below) identity_headers list of header names If method: header-auth and public_access is set Headers the app reads the user from (e.g. X-Forwarded-User); the Hub strips them on public paths notes string No Free-text notes about the auth integration. Shown on the app's docs page, the portal (for an app without a web page), the policy view and the app detail. Upgrade constraints go here too

Constraints the schema enforces:

  • group_access: true requires access_group.
  • group_admin: true requires admin_group.
  • A non-empty admin_paths requires admin_group.
  • method: public requires group_access: false and an empty (or missing) admin_paths.
  • public_access is only allowed with method forward-auth, header-auth or native-oidc; with header-auth it requires a non-empty identity_headers (each ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9-]{0,63}$, unique).
  • native_login requires method: custom and sso: false.
  • Every method except custom needs at least one Traefik HTTP router. A custom template may have none (router-less: no web page), and may then set group_access: true without native_login.
  • keycloak_access_role: true requires method: native-oidc and access_group; so does method: native-oidc with group_access: false.

access_group is only enforced by group-gate when group_access: true. Otherwise it is informational, unless the Keycloak access role applies.

keycloak_access_role. The Hub restricts sign-in to the instance's access group in Keycloak (contract §8, "Access role"): every client of the instance gets a client role access, the access group gets that role, and the client's browser flow denies sign-in without it (also when the user already has a Keycloak session). The Hub does the same for every native-oidc template with group_access: false. Set it for apps that can't restrict sign-in to a group themselves or that let outsiders create accounts without rights (Immich, Headscale, NetBird, DokuWiki, Wiki.js, Actual), and as defence in depth on apps whose login paths are gated by group-gate or that check groups themselves (Paperless, Vaultwarden, GitLab, Nextcloud). It fails closed: without the group or the role nobody signs in. Only access-group members sign in — admin-group members too only if they are also in the access group. Every client of such an app has direct access grants, implicit flow, service accounts, device and CIBA grants and standard token exchange switched off (only the browser flow signs in): don't use it for an app whose client needs one of them. CI has no Hub, so the sign-in test runs without the access role (see tests.signin expected_fail).

items.title: Auth methods
items.text:
method Meaning Router middlewares native-oidc The app talks OIDC to Keycloak itself. Needs keycloak_clients No portcullis-auth on the host-wide router. Login or admin paths may use a separate PathPrefix router with forward-auth forward-auth oauth2-proxy + group-gate in front. The app has its own login, or none portcullis-auth@docker,portcullis-groups@docker header-auth Forward-auth, and the app also trusts X-Forwarded-User from Traefik (and only from Traefik) portcullis-auth@docker,portcullis-groups@docker mtls A YubiKey certificate at the TLS layer (Traefik's protected option trusts only the YubiKey certificate authority: a browser certificate is refused at the handshake) tls.options: protected@file, no forward-auth custom The app handles its own sign-in (app-specific account system, e.g. plex.tv). With native_login, the Hub can put Portcullis sign-in in front of it None: the Hub's override adds the gateway pair for Portcullis sign-in public No authentication None

See Choosing an auth method in the templates repo's contributing guide.

items.title: SSO values
items.text:
• true: the user authenticates once in Keycloak and is logged into the app automatically.
  • false: the app has its own login form. Forward-auth only gates access, and the user logs in again.
  • "partial": the app auto-creates users from the identity, but needs extra setup, e.g. role assignment.

items.title: auth.native_login
items.text:
For a custom app that has its own login and no SSO. The Hub then shows a per-app Sign-in setting and implements it with compose-override labels; the template itself never changes.

auth:
  method: custom
  sso: false
  group_access: true          # enforced only behind Portcullis sign-in
  access_group: users_plex
  group_admin: false
  native_login:
    supported: true
    allow_without_gateway: true
    note: Plex signs users in with plex.tv accounts; its TV and mobile apps need "App's own login only".
Field Type Required Description supported true Yes The app's own login protects it on its own allow_without_gateway boolean No (default false) Admins may choose App's own login only (no Portcullis) note string (≤ 500) No Shown next to the Sign-in setting: what the app's login is, what breaks behind forward-auth

The two modes (Apps with their own login):

  • Portcullis sign-in, then the app's own login (default): every router gets portcullis-auth@docker,portcullis-groups@docker in front of its own middlewares, the TLS tier from the policy, and group-gate requires access_group if group_access: true. The access policy applies as for forward-auth.
  • App's own login only (only with allow_without_gateway: true): the template's middlewares without the gateway pair, public@file, no group.

Rules (schema and tests/validate.py; the Hub checks the first two too):

  • only with method: custom and sso: false: an app with SSO is signed in through Portcullis and never gets a way around it;
  • supported must be true (omit the block otherwise);
  • a custom app with group_access: true needs native_login (group-gate only runs behind Portcullis sign-in);
  • the compose file of a custom app never uses portcullis-auth@docker or portcullis-groups@docker: the Hub adds them.

items.title: admin_paths
items.text:
admin_paths lists path prefixes on the app's hostnames that need the admin group in addition to the hostname's group. The Hub publishes them as group-gate path_groups (see Groups → Path rules).

Each item must:

  • match ^/[A-Za-z0-9._~%!$&'()*+,;=:@/-]*$, be at most 256 characters, and be unique in the list
  • not contain .. or //, and have no . segment (/./, a trailing /.)

Matching is a segment-boundary prefix match: /admin matches /admin and /admin/x, but not /administrator.

Path rules only take effect on routers that use portcullis-groups@docker. validate.py therefore fails if no router with portcullis-auth@docker,portcullis-groups@docker serves each listed path.

auth:
  method: native-oidc
  sso: true
  group_access: true
  group_admin: false
  access_group: users_vaultwarden
  admin_group: admin_vaultwarden
  admin_paths: ["/admin"]

items.title: auth.public_access
items.text:
Public path exceptions let anonymous visitors use an app's share links (Nextcloud /s/<token>, Grafana shared dashboards) while the rest of the host stays behind Portcullis. The template only declares the paths. When an admin turns the exception on in the Hub, the Hub adds one Traefik router for them without forward-auth and group-gate (contracts §3). A template must never ship such a router in compose.yml. The app's own auth (share token, share password, expiry) is all that protects these paths; see Sign-in methods → Public exceptions.

Field Type Required Description enabled_by_default boolean No (default false) State of the Hub toggle until an admin chooses description string, one line, ≤ 500 No Shown in the Hub above the warning default_mode listed or all No listed: only shares an admin lists in the Hub; all: every share. Default listed if a path has {token}, else all. listed needs a {token} path token_pattern anchored regex ^...$, ≤ 200 If a path has {token} (and only then) Every listed share token must match it credential_headers list of header names No Headers besides Authorization / Proxy-Authorization (always refused) the app logs a user in with, e.g. Immich x-api-key credential_cookies list of cookie names No Cookies the app logs a user in with (session, remember-me, render keys) credential_query list of parameter names No Query parameters the app logs a user in with (e.g. Immich apiKey, Grafana auth_token) static_extensions list of [a-z0-9]{1,8} No Extra file extensions supporting paths may serve (default: avif css eot gif ico jpeg jpg js map mjs otf png svg ttf webp woff woff2). Script extensions (php, phtml, cgi, py, jsp, …) are refused service compose service No Service the public router targets. Default: the only service with HTTP routers paths list, 1–20 Yes See below

Each paths item:

Field Type Required Description prefix path Yes Segment-boundary prefix: /s matches /s and /s/..., not /sx. Letters, digits and . _ ~ - per segment, optional trailing /; one whole segment may be {token}. Not / itself; no wildcards, .., //, %, ?, #, $, quotes or backticks description string, one line, ≤ 200 Yes What the path is for (shown in the Hub and on the app page) supporting boolean No Token-free path the share page needs. Opened in both modes, and only for static files below it unless exact. Can't have {token} exact boolean No Opens only this path itself (Path, no subpaths): a single app route or file the page needs. Requires justification; can't have {token}. A path on the broad list (an exact /index.php is still the whole front controller) also needs broad: true broad boolean No Acknowledges a prefix on the broad list; requires justification justification string If broad: true or exact: true Why the broad prefix / exact route is needed

What each mode opens:

Path kind Mode listed Mode all {token} path, e.g. /s/{token} /s/<t> for each listed token <t> /s (up to the segment before {token}) supporting: true static files under the prefix (see below) same supporting: true + exact: true the exact path same other token-free paths no segment-boundary prefix (or the exact path with exact: true)

Static files means Traefik's PathRegexp of the prefix, dot-free directory segments and a file name ending in a static extension, e.g. /dist/core-common.js or /core/img/actions/a.svg, but not /dist/, /dist/a, /dist/a.php or /dist/x.php/a.js. An app route that only accepts extension-less paths is therefore never reached through a supporting path.

Logins never ride the public router: core's public guard (contracts §5) answers 403 to requests carrying Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, a credential_headers header, a credential_cookies cookie or a credential_query parameter. Cookie and query names are compared case-insensitively after PHP's name mangling (leading spaces dropped, and . become _, name[…] is name), raw and percent-decoded. List every way the app authenticates a request at the pinned version.

In mode listed with no listed share, nothing is opened and no router is generated.

Rules (schema, tests/validate.py and the Hub):

  • Broad prefixes need broad: true and a justification: /api, /apps, /index.php, /ocs, /ocs/v1.php, /ocs/v2.php, /remote.php, /remote.php/dav, /remote.php/webdav, /public.php, /dav, /webdav, /graphql, /rest, /v1, /v2, /v3, /auth, /login, /user, /users, /account, /settings, /identity, /sso, /oidc, and any bare /<name>.php. A {token} path is checked on its mode-all extent (/api/{token} is broad).
  • Never public: anything overlapping /oauth2, /admin or /.well-known, or the app's admin_paths.
  • No overlap with other routers: a prefix (mode-all extent) may not overlap a Path/PathPrefix of another router on the app's hosts (login gates, admin routers, API splits). Traefik's PathPrefix is a plain string prefix, so PathPrefix(/login) overlaps /logins.
  • Analysable routing only: routers on the app's hosts may use only Host, Path, PathPrefix, Method, Header, HeaderRegexp, Query, QueryRegexp and ClientIP, without negation. PathRegexp, negated matchers or unknown matchers make the Hub refuse the template's public plan (it can't prove there is no overlap).
  • token_pattern must be anchored and compile, and must reject "", ., .., a/b, /, backticks, spaces, %2F, ${X}, ) and newlines. The Hub additionally requires tokens of [A-Za-z0-9._~-]{1,128}.
  • Routing names: routers and middlewares named portcullis-public-* are reserved for the Hub.

  • Service: with several routed services, set service. If it defines several Traefik services, exactly one host-wide router on it must name one.

  • Supporting prefixes are directories: a supporting prefix whose last segment looks like a file (/custom.css) must be exact.

Set enabled_by_default: true only when turning the exception on opens nothing by itself (mode listed) and can't weaken the host. Example (Nextcloud, abridged):

auth:
  method: forward-auth
  public_access:
    enabled_by_default: true
    default_mode: listed
    description: Public share links for people without a Portcullis account.
    token_pattern: '^[A-Za-z0-9-]{1,32}$'
    credential_cookies: [nc_username, nc_token, nc_session_id]
    paths:
      - prefix: "/s/{token}"          # quote: { } in flow style is YAML syntax
        description: Share page, password form, download and direct preview
      - prefix: "/public.php/dav/files/{token}"
        description: Public WebDAV of the share
      - prefix: /dist
        description: Compiled JS/CSS
        supporting: true                # static files only
      - prefix: /core/mimeicon
        description: File-type icon for files without a preview
        supporting: true
        exact: true
        justification: "#[PublicPage] route that only redirects to a static icon"
      - prefix: /apps/text/public
        description: Markdown viewer sessions (token in the body, so only in mode all)

items.title: settings
items.text:
Options an admin (or each person) sets in the Hub: template contract v3, Integration Contracts §13. Each option has a type, a scope, constraints and one or more deliveries (how the value reaches the app). The Hub validates, stores, resolves and delivers the values; the template only declares them. Decoding is strict: an unknown key anywhere under settings, files, hooks or reload is refused.

settings:
  sections: [Storage, Accounts, Library]   # panel sections, in order
  options: [...]                           # the options below
Field Type Description sections list of ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9 ]{0,31}$, unique Panel sections, in display order options list of options The options, in display order

A list directly under settings: (contract v2) is refused.

Immich example (abridged):

settings:
  sections: [Storage, Accounts, Library]
  options:
    - key: trash_days
      label: Keep deleted items for
      type: int
      unit: days
      min: 0
      max: 3650
      default: 30
      section: Library
      applies: restart
      delivery: [{env: IMMICH_TRASH_DAYS}]
    - key: storage_quota
      label: Storage quota
      type: size
      step: 1GiB
      allow_unlimited: true
      scope: person
      default: 100GiB
      resolve: max
      resolve_choices: [max, min, priority]
      section: Storage
      applies: next_sign_in
      delivery:
        - claim: {client: immich, name: immich_quota, json_type: int,
                  render: {unit: GiB, unlimited: "-1"}}
    - key: role
      label: Role
      type: enum
      options: [{value: user, label: User}, {value: admin, label: Administrator}]
      scope: person
      privileged: true
      default: user
      group_values: {"{{ADMIN_GROUP}}": admin}
      resolve: max
      section: Accounts
      applies: next_sign_in
      delivery: [{claim: {client: immich, name: immich_role, json_type: string}}]
    - key: external_library
      label: External photo library
      type: path
      mode: ro
      needs: read
      writes_as: {uid: 0, gid: 0}
      target: {service: immich-server, mount: /usr/src/app/external}
      applies: restart

items.title: Option fields
items.text:
Field Type Required Description key ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,39}$, unique Yes Identifier (not an env name) label single line, 1–64 chars Yes Panel label description text, ≤ 500 chars, no control characters No Help text in the panel and on My apps section one of settings.sections No Panel section type see Types Yes scope instance, person, group, person_entered No (default instance) See Scopes. Refused on person_secret and person_id (always per person, set by the Hub) required boolean No The value must be non-empty. A set secret counts as non-empty. On person scope the default must be non-empty; not for group scope default a value of the option's type person: yes; refused for group, person_entered and secrets The template's default (for person: everyone else with access) applies live, reload, next_request, next_sign_in, restart, account_creation No When a change takes effect. Default: next_sign_in with a claim delivery, next_request with a header delivery, otherwise restart. See Applies requires list of option keys No Instance options only: other instance options that must be non-empty when this one is (not itself) requires_any list of option keys No Instance options only: when this one is non-empty, at least one of the listed instance options must be non-empty (not itself). The Samba share slots use it: a slot's folder needs a reader or writer group delivery list of deliveries See Deliveries How the value reaches the app resolve max, min, priority, union, intersection, any, all person only, and required there How one value is picked for a person in several groups. See Scopes resolve_choices list of the above person only Other rules the admin may switch to; each must fit the type group_values map {{ACCESS_GROUP}} / {{ADMIN_GROUP}} → value person only Preset rows for the instance's own groups (the manifest needs access_group / admin_group). Other group names are refused: the admin picks them privileged boolean person only The option grants a privilege. Only enum and bool; the default must be the lowest value (the first options entry, or false); no {{ACCESS_GROUP}} preset self_visible boolean (default true) person (and person_id, which requires false); on an instance option only true false hides the person's value from My apps. An instance option with self_visible: true may be shown in a person_secret info line ({value:<key>}) unique boolean list, or person_entered string / int No two items (list) or no two people (person-entered) hold the same value admin_override boolean person_entered only Admins may enter a value for someone (they can always clear one) setup boolean instance scope, not secret NEW (apps). A setup choice: asked in the setup form before the first start. See Setup options fixed_after_start boolean with setup only NEW (apps). The value can't change after the instance's first successful start profiles map: option value → list of compose profiles setup enum options only NEW (apps). The compose profiles each value starts ([] for none); every value has an entry

Type constraints (pattern, min, options, …) are in Types. A constraint the type doesn't take (min on an enum) is refused.

items.title: Types
items.text:
Values are stored canonically: sizes in bytes, durations in seconds. Write sizes with binary units only (10GiB, 512MiB; 10GB and 10G are refused) and durations with a unit (30d, 90m, 60s). default, min / max / step and group_values must be valid values of the option.

Type Holds Constraints string Text (one line) pattern (anchored ^…$, Go RE2 syntax: no lookarounds or backreferences, matches the whole value), min_len / max_len (0–65535), format: hostname (lowercase, at least two labels; a dotted IPv4 address such as 192.168.1.10 matches too, an IPv6 address or a single label doesn't), ip, cidr (no host bits), url (http/https), email, iana_tz, locale, cron, semver, hex int 64-bit integer min, max, step (values are min + k × step), unit (a label, e.g. days) size Bytes min, max, step (values are k × step), allow_unlimited (the value unlimited; every delivery must then set render.unlimited) duration Seconds min, max bool true / false — enum One choice options: [{value, label}] (at least one; value ≤ 128 chars, label one line ≤ 64). The order is the rank for max / min multi_enum A set of choices options as for enum, min_items / max_items; stored in option order list Ordered items items: {type, …} (string, int, bool or enum, with that type's constraints), min_items / max_items (0–1000), unique table Records min_items / max_items, columns: [{name, label, type, required, …}] (name ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}$, unique; type string, int, bool or enum with its constraints), key_column (that column's values are unique; records are delivered keyed by it) path A host directory, bind-mounted target: {service, mount} (an absolute, clean container path), mode (ro / rw), needs (read / write; write with ro is refused), writes_as: {uid, gid} (numbers, or keys of instance int / string options; shown in the panel), or instead of those three a folder block, and checks (Shared folders). Instance scope only, no delivery: the target is the delivery. The value is a host path or folder:<id>[/<subpath>] secret A write-only value min_len / max_len, generate: {length, charset} (length 8–128; charset hex, alphanumeric or ascii_printable: printable ASCII without space, ' and \). No default. Values can't contain ' or control characters group / groups One / a set of LLDAP groups groups: min_items / max_items. Instance values are bound to the groups' LLDAP ids: a deleted or re-created group grants nothing and is purged. A file delivery may render the members instead (render.expand_members) person_secret A per-person file-share password; the Hub keeps only its hash See Per-person credentials and ids person_id A Hub-allocated per-person number (a Unix uid) See Per-person credentials and ids user / users One / a set of LLDAP usernames (lowercased; never an email) users: min_items / max_items

Refused: the contract v2 types text, boolean, select and paths (use string, bool, enum with options: [{value, label}], and one path per directory), and the reserved type folder (a shared folder is a type: path option with a folder block). env[].generate: none is gone: a value the admin enters is a setting.

items.title: Shared folders (folder, checks, lan_only)
items.text:
Integration Contracts §13.15 and §14.

folder (a path option; replaces mode, needs and writes_as):

Field Type Required Description access read / write Yes read always mounts read-only runs_as {uid, gid} numbers, or {uid_env, gid_env} env names of instance int options, or {uid_from, gid_from} keys of a person_id option (each person's own id); one source per id Yes The uid and gid the app uses on this mount; numbers must match the service's compose user: when the service sets one. uid_from alone (no gid source) needs joins_group: template; gid_from needs uid_from and joins_group: template (a per-person tree) joins_group group_add / gid_env / template No (default group_add) How the app joins the folder's group; gid_env needs runs_as.gid_env must_own boolean No The Hub also sets the owner to the app's uid. Writers only

checks (option level, next to folder): a list of {kind, reason, …}; reason is required (one line, ≤ 200 characters).

kind On Parameters filesystem a path option with folder needs: from [xattr, acl]; not: from [nfs, cifs, fuse] exclusive a path option with folder.access: write — free_space a path option min: a size in binary units (500GiB) requires_group_value a scope: person option —

ports[].lan_only: see ports.

Choosing runs_as and joins_group. Give the ids the app's process really has on the mount:

  • the image runs as root and the compose service sets no user: (Jellyfin, Immich): runs_as: {uid: 0, gid: 0} with the default group_add;
  • the service sets user: "1000:1000": the same numbers;
  • the service sets user: "${PUID:-1000}:${PGID:-1000}": runs_as: {uid_env: PUID, gid_env: PGID}, both instance int options;
  • the image drops supplementary groups before starting the app (s6 s6-setuidgid, su -g, many PUID/PGID images): a group_add gid never reaches the process. Use joins_group: gid_env so the Hub writes the folder's gid into the app's primary group variable instead (Plex: PLEX_GID), or, for a root process that keeps its own rights, say so in the notes (motionEye).

One primary group per process. With joins_group: gid_env every folder option of the service shares that one variable, so they must all use the same shared folder (subfolders are fine) or all use host paths; the Hub refuses an assignment that would need two gids ("point both settings at the same shared folder"). Plex's three libraries follow this rule; say it in the template's notes so admins know. The variable may not be read by another service's user: or group_add.

Hardware transcoding next to a folder block. Next to a folder block, every group_add entry of the target service must be a number or exactly one ${NAME} of an instance int option; group names (video, render) are refused. The render group's gid differs from host to host, so declare an int option (for example render_gid, env RENDER_GID, default 109) and write group_add: ["${RENDER_GID:-109}"]. A variable that isn't a declared int option is refused on every service.

Jellyfin example:

settings:
  sections: [Libraries]
  options:
    - key: movies_path
      label: Movies folder
      description: Host path to your movies library
      section: Libraries
      type: path
      target: {service: jellyfin, mount: /data/movies}
      folder:
        access: read
        runs_as: {uid: 0, gid: 0}
        joins_group: group_add
      applies: restart

items.title: Scopes
items.text:
Scope Values Rules instance One value for the instance Without delivery: env: <UPPER(key)> person A default plus per-group rows the admin adds; resolved to one value per person with access Needs default and a per-person delivery (claim, header, file or hook); env is refused group One record per group the admin adds; not resolved per person No default. Env needs render.format: json. Records are delivered only for groups that still exist with the same LLDAP id person_entered Each person enters their own value on My apps See Person-entered options

resolve picks one value for a person in several groups with a row:

Rule Types max, min int, size, duration, enum (by option order); unlimited beats any number under max and loses under min priority Any: the first row (in the admin's order) the person is in union, intersection list, multi_enum, groups any, all bool

The default is a fallback for people in none of the rows' groups and never takes part in max / union. Nobody outside the population (the access group's members, minus expired memberships) gets a value.

Group values must only grant. A group-scope record, and a group row, is left out when its group was deleted or re-created, and records aren't delivered at all while Users & Groups is unavailable. The app must treat a missing record as "nothing granted", never as "no restriction".

items.title: Person-entered options
items.text:
scope: person_entered: each person with access enters their own value (Firefox Sync's Mozilla account ID). See Adding an App for the full example.

  • Types string, int, bool or enum only (not secret). A string needs max_len (at most 256), a pattern or a format.
  • unique: true (string / int): no two people of one instance hold the same value. admin_override: true: admins may enter one for someone.
  • Refused: default, required, resolve, resolve_choices, group_values, privileged, requires (in either direction), self_visible: false, applies: account_creation.
  • applies must match the delivery:
    • file: the file's on_membership_change (restart → restart, reload → reload, hook → live; a file without one is refused);
    • hook: live, and the hook's when lists membership_change;
    • claim: next_sign_in; header: next_request;
    • env: restart, and render.join or render.format: json (the variable is the list of everyone's values).
  • A template whose routes can run without Portcullis identity (method public or custom, or native_login.allow_without_gateway) needs auth.access_group: its members may enter a value.

items.title: Per-person credentials and ids (person_secret, person_id)
items.text:
Integration Contracts §13.16 and §13.17. Both types are allowed only on a router-less custom template (no Traefik router) with group_access: true and an access_group: its population is the access group's members. Neither takes scope, default, required, resolve, resolve_choices, group_values, privileged, requires or requires_any; neither can be set by an admin.

person_secret: each person with access creates their own file-share password on My apps after a fresh sign-in (a method the app's template accepts). It is shown once; the Hub keeps only its NT hash, outside every backup, and destroys it when the person loses access.

Field Type Required Description hash nt Yes The NT hash (MD4 of the UTF-16LE password), the one form Samba imports length integer ≥ 24, a multiple of 4 Yes Password length, shown in groups of 4 joined by - (24 → 29 characters with the dashes) delivery exactly file (a scalar, not a list) Yes The hashes are files in a read-only directory (below); no other delivery mount {service, path} Yes The compose service and the absolute, clean container directory where the Hub mounts the directory of <username>.nt files (32 hex characters each), read-only. Not colliding with a path target or data-file mount on that service revoke_on_leave true Yes The credential is destroyed when the person leaves the population, is deleted or is re-created on_restore void Yes Any restore voids every credential of the instance username {pattern, reserved, reason} No Usernames the app can serve. pattern: anchored ^…$, only literals, bracket classes and {m,n} (what Go RE2 and busybox ERE read alike); reserved: lowercase names the image already has; reason: one line ≤ 200 characters shown to people whose name fails. If compose passes it to the container, it is PORTCULLIS_USERNAME_PATTERN in environment: with every $ written $$, and must equal pattern info list of {label, value} No Lines on the person's credential card. value placeholders: {user}, {value:<key>} (an instance string / int / enum / bool option with self_visible: true; never a secret or path), {port:<PORT KEY>} (the instance's host port), {port_suffix:<PORT KEY>:<default>} (empty when the host port is <default>, else :<port>). Any other {…} is refused applies live No Credential changes reach the app through hooks with credential_change

label, description and section work as for every option; self_visible and checks are refused. The template must declare at least one hook on mount.service whose when includes credential_change: it applies revocations live (within 8 s, else the Hub stops and restarts the instance).

person_id: a stable number per person, allocated by the Hub.

Field Type Required Description pool posix_uid Yes The Hub-wide uid pool, 20000–59999 (never 0–999, 1000, 10000–10099, 65534 or 60000–60999). Every option with the pool, in every instance, gives a person the same id; ids are never reused, and a deleted and re-created account gets a new one self_visible false Yes Never shown on My apps delivery file deliveries only Yes {file: {name, field}}: the person's id in the people section of the data file

A folder block's runs_as.uid_from / gid_from name a person_id option (Shared folders): {uid_from: uid} with joins_group: template for a shared folder every person writes (files land as <person's uid>:<folder gid>; the template reads ${PORTCULLIS_FOLDER_GID_<KEY>} in compose environment:, the one allowed form), {uid_from: uid, gid_from: uid} with joins_group: template for a per-person tree (each <username> directory <uid>:<uid> 0700; such an option never takes a shared folder).

Time Machine example (abridged):

instances: multi
auth:
  method: custom                  # no Traefik router: no web page
  sso: false
  group_access: true
  group_admin: false
  access_group: users_timemachine
  notes: "No web page: file sharing over SMB with per-person file-share passwords; LAN/VPN only."
ports:
  - {key: TM_SMB, label: SMB, container: 445, default: 445, protocol: tcp,
     service: timemachine, lan_only: true}
files:
  - {name: people, service: timemachine, mount: /portcullis/data, format: tsv,
     on_membership_change: hook}        # the sync hook applies changes live
hooks:
  - name: sync
    service: timemachine
    command: [/portcullis/portcullis-sync]
    when: [start, settings_change, membership_change, credential_change]
    timeout: 60s
settings:
  sections: [Access, Backups, Network]
  options:
    - key: share_password
      label: File-share password
      type: person_secret
      hash: nt
      length: 24
      delivery: file                          # <username>.nt files, read-only at mount.path
      mount: {service: timemachine, path: /portcullis/secrets}
      revoke_on_leave: true
      on_restore: void
      username:
        pattern: "^[a-z_][a-z0-9_.-]{0,31}$"
        reserved: [root, nobody, timemachine]   # every account of the image
        reason: "isn't a valid Samba and Unix name"
      info:
        - {label: Connect, value: "smb://{value:connect_address}{port_suffix:TM_SMB:445}/{value:share_prefix}-{user}"}
        - {label: Username, value: "{user}"}
      applies: live
      section: Access
    - key: uid
      label: File owner id
      type: person_id
      pool: posix_uid
      self_visible: false
      delivery: [{file: {name: people, field: uid}}]
    - key: size_limit
      label: Backup size limit
      type: size
      step: 1GiB
      allow_unlimited: true
      scope: person
      default: 500GiB
      resolve: max
      section: Backups
      applies: live
      delivery:
        - file: {name: people, field: size_limit,
                 render: {unit: MiB, integer: true, unlimited: ""}}
      checks: [{kind: requires_group_value, reason: Most people should get a deliberate limit}]
    - key: storage
      label: Backup storage
      type: path
      target: {service: timemachine, mount: /opt}
      folder:
        access: write
        runs_as: {uid_from: uid, gid_from: uid}   # a per-person tree
        joins_group: template
      checks:                                     # option level, next to folder
        - {kind: filesystem, needs: [xattr], not: [nfs, cifs, fuse],
           reason: Time Machine stores metadata in extended attributes}
        - {kind: exclusive, reason: Backup bundles must not be written by other apps}
      applies: restart
      section: Backups
    - key: share_prefix
      label: Share name prefix
      type: string
      pattern: "^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,31}$"
      default: TimeMachine
      self_visible: true                          # shown in the info line
      applies: live
      delivery: [{file: {name: people}}]
    - key: connect_address
      label: Address people connect to
      type: string
      format: hostname                            # an IPv4 address matches too
      required: true
      self_visible: true
      section: Network
      applies: live
      delivery: [{file: {name: people}}]
    - key: avahi_dir
      label: Host Avahi services directory
      description: Bonjour advertising. Advertising shows every share name, which contains usernames, to everyone on the local network.
      type: path
      target: {service: timemachine, mount: /portcullis/avahi}
      mode: rw
      needs: write
      writes_as: {uid: 0, gid: 0}
      section: Network
      applies: restart
    - key: advertise
      label: Advertise with Bonjour
      description: Turn this off before clearing the Avahi directory.
      type: bool
      default: false
      section: Network
      applies: live
      delivery: [{file: {name: people}}]

The data file people.tsv then holds lines such as person alice uid 20000, person alice size_limit 10240 and value share_prefix TimeMachine.

items.title: Setup options (setup, fixed_after_start, profiles)
items.text:
NEW (apps). The Hub asks for an instance's setup choices before its first start (Install… / + Add instance), with their defaults (contracts §13.18). After the first start they are ordinary settings, except those with fixed_after_start: true: changing one would mean moving the data, so a save that changes it is refused (409); the way to another choice is a new instance and a restore of a backup.

A setup enum may switch which compose services run: profiles maps each value to the compose profiles it starts, and the Hub writes the instance's COMPOSE_PROFILES from the current values.

settings:
  options:
    - key: database
      label: Database
      type: enum
      options:
        - {value: mysql, label: MySQL / MariaDB}
        - {value: postgres, label: PostgreSQL}
      default: mysql
      setup: true
      fixed_after_start: true
      profiles:
        mysql: [db-mysql]
        postgres: [db-postgres]

# compose.yml
services:
  db-mysql:
    profiles: [db-mysql]
    # …
  db-postgres:
    profiles: [db-postgres]
    # …

Rules (the Hub and tests/validate.py refuse anything else, naming the option):

  • setup only on scope: instance options that aren't secret; fixed_after_start only with setup.
  • profiles only on setup enum options of scope instance, with a default; its keys are exactly the option's values (write value: [] for a value that starts no profile); each profile matches ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$ and is listed by at least one compose service.
  • A compose service's profiles: is a list of literal names of that form, and every service with profiles: is started by some value of some option's profiles — otherwise the Hub would never start it.
  • A service without profiles: may not name a profiled service in depends_on, network_mode: service:<x> or volumes_from: compose couldn't start it for a choice that leaves that service off.
  • COMPOSE_PROFILES is the Hub's: a manifest may not declare it.

items.title: Deliveries
items.text:
Each entry of delivery is exactly one of:

Delivery Form For env {env: NAME} instance, group (render.format: json), person_entered (the list). The name must match the env-key rule, not be PORTCULLIS_*, not be used by another option, env:, ports: or a client's secret_env, and be interpolated in compose.yml as ${NAME…} (not hard-coded in a service's environment) indexed env {env: NAME_{n}} An instance list with max_items (at most 64): writes NAME_1 … NAME_<max_items>, one item each, unused ones empty. Every NAME_<n> compose references must be within max_items claim {claim: {client, name, json_type, render}} person, person_entered on native-oidc templates. client is a keycloak_clients[] client_id; name matches ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$ and isn't a standard OIDC / JWT, Keycloak, attr_* or portcullis_* claim; one option per claim and client header {header: {name, render}} person, person_entered. name matches ^X-Forwarded-Attr-[A-Za-z0-9]+(-[A-Za-z0-9]+){0,30}$; one option per header. See the header rules below file {file: {name, field, render}} Any scope. name is a files[] entry. field (person, person_entered and person_id only; default the option key, ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,39}$) names the value in the file's people / entries; one option per field hook {hook: <name>, render} Any scope. name is a hooks[] entry

render goes inside the claim, header or file; on an env or hook delivery it is the entry's own render key.

json_type (claims): string, int, bool or json. int is a 32-bit integer (Keycloak's conversion): a size must be rendered in a unit (render.unit: GiB) and render.unlimited must be a 32-bit integer ("-1"). bool needs a bool option whose render.true / render.false are exactly true / false. json takes render.format: json, a table, or numbers. Statically visible mismatches are refused; a value that doesn't fit at delivery time is not delivered (the person's claim is cleared).

Headers are per-person values group-gate adds on the instance's hosts. They need routers with portcullis-groups@docker, and every router that reaches the delivering backend (its network namespace, network_mode: service: followed) must run Portcullis forward-auth, so no client can send the header itself. Refused: method public or custom without Portcullis sign-in, native_login.allow_without_gateway, and Traefik-labelled services on network_mode: host. The Hub's public-exception router strips every declared header name (and its _ spelling).

items.title: Render
items.text:
Field For Meaning unit size: B, KiB, MiB, GiB, TiB (binary) or KB, MB, GB, TB (decimal, strictly 10ⁿ); duration: s, m, h, d; int: its own unit The value divided by the unit integer size, duration Refuse values that aren't whole in the unit (the save names the app and the unit) unlimited size with allow_unlimited (required there) What unlimited renders as for this app, e.g. "-1", "0", "none".
