Stored values are never numbers for unlimited true / false bool The strings for true and false (default true / false) join lists, sets, person-entered env lists Separator (default ,) format structured values json, yaml or csv expand_members file deliveries of group / groups options true: the file holds the members of the groups who have access to the instance (sorted usernames), not the group names

Env, header and claim values are one line; headers are at most 1 KiB and claims 4 KiB. Env values are single-quoted, so a value with ', \ or a newline is refused at save.

items.title: Applies
items.text:
applies Effect of a change live A hook applied it; no restart. Needs a hook delivery (or a file with on_membership_change: hook) reload The template's reload action. Needs reload next_request Headers: each request reads the attributes file next_sign_in Claims: Keycloak reads them at sign-in restart The Hub restarts the instance account_creation Only new accounts get it; the panel warns "existing accounts keep their value"

A save does the strongest effect of the changed options once (restart over reload over nothing).

items.title: files
items.text:
Data files the Hub writes for file deliveries (contracts §13.7).

Field Type Required Description name ^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}$, unique Yes The file is <mount>/<name>.json (and <name>.secrets.json when it holds a secret option), or <mount>/<name>.tsv with format: tsv service service Yes The compose service that reads it mount absolute, clean container directory (no :) Yes The Hub bind-mounts the file's directory here read-only (a directory, not a file: atomic renames give a new inode). It may not collide with another file's or a path option's target on the same service format json (default) or tsv No tsv: one tab-separated record per line, for apps that read the file with a shell (contracts §13.7). No secret and no table option may be delivered into a tsv file on_membership_change restart, reload, hook, none (default) No What happens when people joining or leaving change the file. reload needs reload; hook a hook with membership_change

The data file is mode 0640 and the secrets file 0600, both owned by the Hub's uid 10001: the reading service runs as root, or with group_add: ["10001"] for the data file and user: "10001" for a secrets file.

items.title: hooks
items.text:
Commands the Hub runs in the app's running containers with the desired settings on standard input (contracts §13.8).

Field Type Required Description name ^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}$, unique Yes Referenced by {hook: <name>} service service Yes Where it runs (a running container of this instance) command non-empty list of non-empty strings, no control characters Yes argv, run directly (never through sh -c) user string No User to run as (default: the container's) when list of start, settings_change, membership_change, credential_change (at least one), or exactly [ai], or exactly [vpn] Yes start: after every successful start; settings_change: after a save that changed its input; membership_change: after people joining or leaving changed its input; credential_change: right after a file-share password was created, regenerated, revoked or voided (also how a revocation is applied live: within 8 s). A hook whose last run failed runs again at its next trigger. NEW (AI support) ai: run only by AI support (mint, revoke, on_change of the ai block), never by settings deliveries or a retry; it gets the AI stdin instead of the settings and its stdout is never stored (contracts §15.5). ai can't be combined with another trigger, and no delivery {hook} or reload: {hook} may name such a hook. NEW (VPN) vpn: run only by the VPN machinery, as the vpn block's identity or DNS hook, with the VPN stdin; the same rules as ai (alone, named by the block, never a delivery or reload hook) timeout Go duration, e.g. 60s No (default 30s) At most 10m

A hook of a template with person_secret options also gets credentials on stdin (who has an active password: id and version, never a hash). A hook may print one line PORTCULLIS-REPORT <json> (findings and per-person folders for the doctor and the File sharing tab; shape and limits in contracts §13.8); all other output is log only.

items.title: reload
items.text: The template's reload action, at most one: {service, signal} (signal HUP, USR1 or USR2, sent to the service's running containers; applied when the container still runs, and isn't unhealthy, 10 s later) or {hook: <name>} (a declared hook). Not both. applies: reload and on_membership_change: reload need it.

items.title: ports
items.text:
Host port bindings the app needs (for non-HTTP protocols such as DNS or TURN; HTTP always goes through Traefik). The Hub:

  1. Refuses to enable the app if one of its ports is already claimed by another enabled app.
  2. Shows each port as an editable field, so users can rebind it or (if not required) disable it.
  3. Writes the effective bindings into the per-app compose override. compose.yml must not publish these ports itself.
Field Type Required Description key env key Yes Variable holding the user-overridable host port label single line, non-empty Yes UI label, e.g. DNS (TCP) protocol tcp or udp Yes service service Yes Compose service the port belongs to container integer 1–65535 Yes, unless range is set Container-side port default integer 1–65535 Yes, unless range is set Default host port range "low-high" No Inclusive port range, e.g. "49152-65535". Mutually exclusive with container and default; can't be rebound bind IPv4 or IPv6 address No Default bind address (default 0.0.0.0) required boolean No If not true, the user can clear the host port to disable the binding description string No Help text network_mode_host boolean No The service uses network_mode: host. Ports are claimed globally and can't be rebound lan_only boolean No The port should be reachable only from the local networks; the Hub's doctor warns when it is bound to all interfaces or a public address (§14.7) 
ports:
  - key: ADGUARD_DNS_TCP_HOST
    label: DNS (TCP)
    container: 53
    protocol: tcp
    default: 53
    required: true
    service: adguard
  - key: COTURN_MEDIA_RANGE
    label: TURN media relays
    protocol: udp
    range: "49152-65535"
    required: true
    service: coturn
    network_mode_host: true

items.title: env
items.text:
Per-app environment variables. Contract v3: env entries with generate: none are refused. An admin-entered variable is a settings option (see above).

Field Type Required Description key env key Yes Variable name description non-empty string Yes What it is for generate random or "" No random: the Hub generates 32 hex characters on first enable and writes them to the per-app .env required boolean No The variable must have a value

Secrets (passwords, OIDC client secrets, app keys) must be generate: random entries. Never hard-code a secret in compose.yml. A variable that compose.yml references as required (${VAR:?...}) must be an env entry with generate: random, because that is all the Hub writes.

env:
  - key: VAULTWARDEN_ADMIN_TOKEN
    description: Vaultwarden admin panel token
    generate: random
  - key: VAULTWARDEN_OIDC_SECRET
    description: Vaultwarden OIDC client secret
    generate: random

items.title: keycloak_clients
items.text:
OIDC clients the Hub registers in Keycloak when the app is enabled. Required (at least one) for native-oidc.

Field Type Required Description client_id ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,63}$ Yes Keycloak client ID of the default instance. Other instances get <instance-id> (first entry) and <instance-id>-<client_id> (further entries); compose reads the id from PORTCULLIS_OIDC_CLIENT_ID / PORTCULLIS_OIDC_CLIENT_ID_<KEY>. Core clients such as portcullis-forward-auth are reserved, and so is the prefix portcullis-ai- secret_env env key Yes The env entry (with generate: random) holding the client secret name single line, non-empty Yes Display name in Keycloak redirect_uri URI Exactly one of the two A single redirect URI redirect_uris list of URIs (at least one) Exactly one of the two Several redirect URIs backchannel_logout_url https://{{HOST_<ROUTER>}}/<path> No The app's OIDC back-channel logout endpoint on one of its own hosts (single templates may use https://<sub>.{{DOMAIN}}/<path>). The Hub sets it as the client's back-channel logout URL with "session required" (logout tokens carry sid), so a Keycloak sign-out — the Hub signs users out when they leave a group — ends the app's session too. It follows hostname changes. The path must be routed without forward-auth (Keycloak posts to it server-to-server). Nextcloud uses it ai_client boolean No (default false) NEW (AI support). Only in an ai.chat template (exactly one such entry): the AI page's MCP client. The Hub registers it as an AI client — confidential, consent required, no default ACR (mcp-gate checks the resource's sign-in rule), default scopes basic + acr only, optional scope mcp:all only — keeping the instance's access role (contracts §8) email_verified_claim boolean No (default true) false: the client gets the email-unverified scope instead of email, so tokens carry email but no email_verified claim. For apps that refuse email_verified=false but accept the claim being absent (Vaultwarden). The app must then not request the email scope

Redirect URIs must match ^[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*://\S+$, so custom schemes such as app.immich:///oauth-callback work. {{DOMAIN}} and {{HOST_<ROUTER>}} are replaced; a multi template names its own hosts only as {{HOST_<ROUTER>}} (e.g. https://{{HOST_IMMICH}}/auth/login).

The Hub tags each client with the instance id that owns it (the template id for the default instance), and attaches the acr and groups scopes (see Hub → Keycloak clients).

email_verified_claim. Keycloak never trusts the LLDAP email (users can edit it), so the built-in email scope always sends email_verified: false. Some apps refuse that value. With email_verified_claim: false the Hub attaches core's email-unverified scope instead (the email claim only) and removes email from the client. Keycloak rejects a request for a scope the client doesn't have (invalid_scope), so drop email from the scopes the app requests; tests/validate.py checks *SCOPE* environment variables. The email is still unverified: identity stays sub / preferred_username, and the app must never link accounts by email (contract §8).

keycloak_clients:
  - client_id: vaultwarden
    secret_env: VAULTWARDEN_OIDC_SECRET
    redirect_uri: "https://{{HOST_VAULTWARDEN}}/identity/connect/oidc-signin"
    name: Vaultwarden
    email_verified_claim: false

keycloak_clients:
  - client_id: immich
    secret_env: IMMICH_OIDC_SECRET
    redirect_uris:
      - "https://{{HOST_IMMICH}}/auth/login"
      - "https://{{HOST_IMMICH}}/user-settings"
      - "app.immich:///oauth-callback"
    name: Immich

items.title: ai
items.text:
NEW (AI support), required in every template. Whether the AI can act in the app through MCP, and how (contracts §3.2, §15). Exactly one of mcp and unsupported.

Field Type Required Description mcp non-empty list of companions (below) One of the two The app has AI support through these MCP servers: the app's built-in one or an upstream / vetted community image, pinned by digest. Never code written for Portcullis unsupported single line, 1–200 chars One of the two Why there is no AI support, shown to the admin, e.g. "No official MCP server; community servers are small and not vetted by Portcullis" alternative {name, source, note} No; only with unsupported A community server the admin may evaluate on their own (displayed only, labelled "not vetted by Portcullis"). name single line ≤ 64, source https:// URL, note single line ≤ 200 on_change hook name No; only with mcp Hook run when a companion is switched on or off or its mode changes (stdin in §15.5) chat {provider_kinds, file, env} No; only with unsupported The template is an AI page (an MCP client), see below

Companion (ai.mcp[]):

Field Type Required Description name ^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*$, ≤ 31 chars, unique Yes Companion name: scope mcp:<instance>.<name>, router and alias portcullis-mcp-<instance>--<name>, variable PORTCULLIS_AI_READONLY_<NAME> label single line, 1–64 chars Yes Shown to people and the admin kind companion or builtin Yes companion: a compose service only for AI (the Hub scales it to 0 while AI is off); builtin: the app's own service serves MCP service service whose name matches ^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$ Yes The service that serves MCP. A companion service has no Traefik labels, doesn't join portcullis-proxy (the Hub adds it with the alias), has no network_mode, container_name, hostname or host ports (the gate is its only way in), and backs one companion only. No other service may use network_mode: service:<it> (or pid: service:<it>) port integer 1–65535 Yes Its container port (unused for app_oauth) path absolute clean path No (default /mcp) The upstream MCP path router host router name Yes The endpoint is https://<that router's host><public_path> public_path absolute clean path No (default /mcp) Not /, never at or under /.well-known/ or /oauth2/, never at, under or above a public-access path, and never at, under or above another companion's endpoint path on the same router (its public_path, or an app_oauth companion's path). Not for app_oauth identity object (below) Yes How the person's identity reaches the companion modes list of read_only, read_write Yes What the admin may choose; app_oauth: exactly [read_write] default_mode one of modes When modes has two tools {writes, confirm, never} lists of patterns No Tool names with * globs, or tool:method for consolidated tools (^[A-Za-z0-9_.*-]{1,128}(:[A-Za-z0-9_.*-]{1,128})?$, case-insensitive): writes are hidden in read-only mode, confirm need the person's passkey in their browser, never are hidden and refused aggregate boolean No (default true; app_oauth: false, true refused) Whether its tools are in "all my apps" upstream official or community Yes builtin companions are official source https:// URL Yes The companion project protocol list of 2025-06-18, 2025-11-25, 2026-07-28 Yes The MCP versions it speaks

identity, by mode (only that mode's fields):

mode Fields app_token header (default Authorization); exactly one of format ("<Scheme> {credential}", e.g. "token {credential}") and basic: {user, password} (user {username} or a literal without :, {, }; password exactly {credential}); mint, revoke (hook names, required); scopes: {read_only: [...], read_write: [...]} (optional, passed to mint) identity_headers caller_secret: {env, header, format} (required; env a generate: random entry, header default Authorization, format default "Bearer {secret}") app_oauth revoke (hook name, required); only with kind: builtin

A header is ^[A-Za-z0-9-]{1,64}$, never Host, Cookie, Content-Type, Accept, Proxy-Authorization, the hop-by-hop and framing headers (Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding, Connection, Keep-Alive, TE, Trailer, Upgrade, Proxy-Connection), Mcp-*, MCP-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Session-Id, X-Forwarded-*, X-Auth-Request-*, Remote-* or X-Portcullis-* (case-insensitive).

An identity_headers companion of kind companion needs a trust network: it joins exactly one network, declared at the top level as exactly {internal: true}, whose only members are the companion and the service(s) of its router (the app that trusts the headers). No other service joins it or shares a member's network or pid namespace, no service of the template uses network_mode: host or pid: host, and the caller secret's variable is interpolated only in the companion's service. The app trusts identity headers only from that network's addresses (Grafana's trust.sh reads the prefix at start) and the companion reaches the app by a name ending in -internal on it (contracts §3.2).

chat (AI page templates):

Field Type Description provider_kinds map of kind → one or many Model provider kinds the template renders: litellm, openai_compatible, anthropic, openai, google, bedrock, azure_openai file {service, mount} The service that reads ai-providers.json and the directory it is mounted at (read-only; a files mount's rules) env {service} The service that receives the selected providers' PORTCULLIS_AI_PROVIDER_* variables (the Hub adds them; the template never references them)

A chat template has exactly one keycloak_clients entry with ai_client: true, and that entry needs secret_env (the AI page's client is confidential). chat.file.mount may not collide with a files mount on the same service.

Hooks named by ai (mint, revoke, on_change) must have exactly when: [ai] and never run on a kind: companion service (it is scaled to 0 while off). Templates may read ${PORTCULLIS_AI_ENABLED:-false}, ${PORTCULLIS_AI_READONLY_<NAME>:-true} and ${PORTCULLIS_MCP_GATE_IP:-172.31.250.3} (only in these forms), and never set or reference a PORTCULLIS_AI_PROVIDER_* variable (the Hub adds them to the chat.env service).

A companion is never code written for Portcullis: vet the project before adding it (maintained, an open licence, a multi-user identity that fits an identity mode, no shared admin identity, a pinned release) and write down why in the template's notes; the AI support page keeps the reasons for the shipped templates.

ai:
  mcp:
    - name: gitea
      label: Gitea
      kind: companion
      service: gitea-mcp
      port: 8080
      router: gitea
      upstream: official
      source: https://gitea.com/gitea/gitea-mcp
      protocol: ["2026-07-28", "2025-11-25"]
      modes: [read_only, read_write]
      default_mode: read_write
      identity:
        mode: app_token
        format: "token {credential}"
        mint: mcp-mint
        revoke: mcp-revoke
      tools:
        writes: ["*_write", "create_*", "update_*", "delete_*"]
        confirm: ["delete_*", "repo_write:delete"]

ai:
  unsupported: "No official MCP server; community servers are small and not vetted by Portcullis"
  alternative:
    name: paperless-mcp
    source: https://github.com/nloui/paperless-mcp
    note: "community, 248★, last change Nov 2025, API token per person"

items.title: vpn
items.text:
NEW (VPN), optional. The template is a VPN (a mesh, a WireGuard server) that the admin may wire as a VPN provider for VPN-only access (contracts §3.3). Installing the template doesn't make it a provider: the admin turns that on per instance on its VPN tab. Without the block an instance can't be a provider, but any instance can still be made VPN-only.

Field Type Required Description label single line, 1–64 chars Yes Shown on Settings → VPN, the instance and the device lists ranges list of 1–8 IPv4 prefixes Yes The addresses the app hands to its clients, each /8–/30, no overlaps. Each entry is a literal prefix or exactly {{setting:<key>}}, naming a string option with format: cidr and scope: instance; the Hub resolves it per instance, and an unset or invalid value refuses the wiring ingress {service, proxy_protocol} Yes service: the compose service the Hub joins to portcullis-vpn (the gateway); proxy_protocol: exactly v2 identity {source, hook, owner, refresh} Yes How the device list is built: source: hook (with hook and owner) or source: static (no hook, no owner; the admin assigns addresses on the VPN tab). refresh: a Go duration, 15s–10m, default 60s dns {hook} or {manual: true} Yes Exactly one: a hook that receives the A records to apply, or the VPN tab shows them for the admin to configure (doctor vpn_dns_manual until acknowledged) control_routers list of host router names No (default []) Routers clients need to connect (coordination, signal, relay). They stay on websecure,vpnsecure with no allowlist whatever the instance's access or the mode. Never a router of an admin UI (auth.admin_paths, or any router of a group_admin template)

identity.hook names a hook with exactly when: [vpn]; owner is oidc_sub (the hook reports Keycloak user ids, resolved to LLDAP usernames through Keycloak's LDAP link, never an email) or username (LLDAP usernames, exact lowercase). The hook gets {"version": 1, "trigger": "vpn", "instance": "<id>", "op": "devices", "ranges": [...]} on stdin and prints one JSON document (at most 4 MiB and 10 000 devices, unknown keys refused):

{"version": 1, "gateway": "100.64.0.1",
 "devices": [{"id": "12", "name": "laptop", "address": "100.64.0.7", "owner": "<sub or username>",
              "online": true, "last_seen": "2026-11-12T10:00:00Z", "expires": null}]}

gateway (required, inside the ranges) is the gateway node's tunnel address, the DNS target, never a device. A refused document keeps the last good list until it is stale (max(3 × refresh, 3 min)). Single devices are left out (IPv6, outside the ranges, the gateway's address, expired, a shared address, an owner who isn't a Portcullis person), each shown on the VPN tab.

dns.hook names a hook with exactly when: [vpn] that gets {"version": 1, "trigger": "vpn", "instance": "<id>", "op": "dns", "records": [{"name": "<fqdn>", "type": "A", "value": "<gateway>"}, ...]} (one record per Portcullis hostname served from this server) after a devices run that changed gateway and after any hostname change. It exits 0 once they are applied; its output is ignored.

The ingress namespace. ingress.service has no network_mode, isn't a job or a kind: companion AI service, and has no Traefik router or traefik.* label: the gateway is reached only over portcullis-vpn. The only other service allowed in its network namespace (network_mode: service:<ingress.service>) is core's forwarder image ghcr.io/porelli/portcullis-forwarder, pinned by digest (for clients with a real tunnel interface, which can't send PROXY v2 themselves; it needs cap_add: [NET_BIND_SERVICE] for :443). Every service in the namespace follows the same rules and publishes no ports. With a vpn: block no service uses pid: host, and network_mode: host is allowed only outside the ingress namespace on a service with no Traefik router or label.

PORTCULLIS_VPN_EDGE. The Hub sets it (<wg ip>:<9001 + slot>) on the ingress service and every service sharing its namespace. Read it only as $$PORTCULLIS_VPN_EDGE in a container shell: ${PORTCULLIS_VPN_*} is reserved (core's and the Hub's) and refused anywhere in a template.

# manifest.yaml (excerpt, headscale)
vpn:
  label: Headscale tailnet
  ranges: ["100.64.0.0/10"]
  ingress: {service: gateway, proxy_protocol: v2}
  identity: {source: hook, hook: vpn-devices, owner: oidc_sub, refresh: 60s}
  dns: {hook: vpn-dns}
  control_routers: [headscale]

items.title: config_files
items.text:
Files the Hub copies from the template directory into the core checkout when the app is enabled.

Field Type Required Description src relative path, no .. segment, no whitespace Yes Path relative to the template directory. Must exist (validate.py) dest non-empty, no .. segment Yes Destination relative to the core checkout. Must stay inside it and not at its top level

The Hub already copies the whole template directory to <core>/templates/<app-id>/ before every compose up. Mounting ./templates/<app-id>/<file> is usually all you need, and every built-in template uses config_files: [].

items.title: urls
items.text:
Links shown in the Hub.

Field Type Required Description label single line, non-empty Yes Link text url ^https?://\S+$ Yes URL, with {{DOMAIN}} and {{HOST_<ROUTER>}} replaced. A multi template uses {{HOST_<ROUTER>}} for its own hosts 
urls:
  - label: Vault
    url: "https://passwords.{{DOMAIN}}"

items.title: tests.signin
items.text:
How CI signs real users in to the app (tests/e2e/app_signin.py in the templates repo, run by test-apps.yml after the app's shell test). The Hub ignores tests. The test creates e2eadmin (access + admin group), e2emember (access group) and e2eoutsider (no group), registers the template's Keycloak clients and writes the group-gate policy as the Hub would, and signs each in through a setup link with a virtual security key. It passes when the member is signed in (and not admin), the admin has admin rights and the outsider is refused; a visible password field fails it unless password explains it. CI runs without the Hub: the clients are plain Keycloak clients, so the Hub's Keycloak access role (keycloak_access_role) is not applied there.

Field Type Description skip string Why the app can't be signed into in CI. Only for public, custom and mtls apps; then nothing else is set path ^/ Required otherwise. Page opened on the host; the setup link lands there host {{HOST_<ROUTER>}} Host to sign in on (default: the host of the first urls entry) login list of Playwright selectors The app's own SSO buttons, clicked when visible fill list of {selector, value} Inputs filled before clicking signed_in check Required otherwise. How to recognise the signed-in user admin check Required when auth.group_admin is true. How to recognise admin rights password string Why a password field on the app's pages is expected (a documented own login or break-glass) setup list of {service, command, save_env, user} or {restart: true} Post-start steps an admin would do: run command in service (as user); with save_env, save the last output line as that env/setting and restart the app; restart: true restarts the app (a documented restart after the first start) expected_fail {member, admin, outsider}: {reason, match, not_match} Known failures: reported, not fatal, only if the failure matches match and not not_match (regexes, case-insensitive), searched in that check's own evidence only: its detail, the pages its flow saw, and the app's container logs / log_files since its flow started. A flow the test broke (password field, Keycloak/enroll or browser error, never on the app) or an exception always fails; a marked check that passes fails the run. A native-oidc app that can't restrict sign-in by group itself (group_access: false, or keycloak_access_role: true) and lets outsiders in marks outsider: with the Hub its access role refuses them at Keycloak, but CI has no Hub and doesn't apply the role. forward-auth / header-auth apps never may. Never widen an app's access (e.g. auto-provisioning) to make a check pass: mark it refused_users list of usernames Extra users in access_group and admin_group that must be refused with HTTP 403 (names the app reserves, e.g. CloudBeaver's cbadmin-*) log_files list of {service, path} Files inside the app's containers, searched by expected_fail.match and kept as artifacts pause_between_users seconds Wait between the users' sign-ins, for apps whose per-client rate limits CI's single client address would trip (Actual: 500 requests a minute) max_clicks integer How often each login selector may be clicked per user (default 5; lower for apps that rate-limit logins, e.g. Actual) boot_timeout, timeout, refused_after seconds Container readiness (600), per-user sign-in (240), how long the outsider is watched once on the app (45)

A check is one of:

Form Passes when text: "{username}" (+ url: /path) the visible text contains it (case-insensitive) html: "{username}" the page source contains it json: {url, field, equals, contains, headers} GET url with the session's cookies answers JSON whose dotted field equals equals (default {username}) or is a list containing contains js: "<expression>" (+ equals, url) the expression, evaluated in the app's page (after opening url, if set; may return a promise), equals equals (default {username}) reach: /path (+ text) the path answers 2xx on the app host (and shows text)

Plus wait (seconds to poll, default 10), url_contains and absent (text that must not be on the page: the app's own denial, e.g. DokuWiki's "Permission Denied" for a session without rights). Strings may use {username}, {email}, {access_group} and {admin_group}.

tests:
  signin:
    path: /
    signed_in:
      json: {url: /api/user, field: login}     # Grafana (group_admin: false: no admin check)

With admin rights mapped from admin_group (DokuWiki):

tests:
  signin:
    path: /doku.php?do=login
    login: ["a:has-text('Portcullis')"]
    signed_in: {text: "{username}", absent: "Permission Denied"}
    admin: {reach: /doku.php?do=admin, text: "Access Control List"}

A known failure (Immich: native OIDC with no group restriction of its own; with the Hub its Keycloak access role keeps outsiders out, but CI runs without the Hub, so every test user gets in there):

tests:
  signin:
    path: /auth/login
    signed_in:
      json: {url: /api/users/me, field: storageLabel}
    expected_fail:
      outsider:
        reason: "Immich has no OIDC group restriction of its own: only the Hub's Keycloak access role (keycloak_access_role) keeps outsiders out, and CI runs without the Hub (app_signin.py registers plain clients)"
        match: "e2eoutsider signed in"

items.title: jobs
items.text:
NEW (apps). Compose services that run once and exit (a setup or migration container). The Hub counts a job's container as done when it exited 0 and as failed when it exited non-zero, whatever its restart: policy, so a finished job never makes the app "not all running" (contracts §11.9). A service another service waits for with depends_on: {<job>: {condition: service_completed_successfully}} is a job without being listed; list the others here.

jobs: [migrate]

Each entry is a service of compose.yml, listed once. No job — listed or found through depends_on — may have a Traefik router (a job serves nothing).

items.title: instances
items.text:
NEW (contract v2). instances: multi lets the Hub run several fully separate instances of the template, each with its own project, volumes, settings, secrets, Keycloak clients, groups and hostnames (Integration Contracts §3.1 and §11). single (the default) means only the default instance, whose id is the template id. Keep a template single only when it needs host-level uniqueness (e.g. fixed host devices), and say why in auth.notes. Host ports are no reason: they are per-instance settings.

instances: multi

Hostname variables. Each hostname the template serves has one host router (a rule with Host() alone; path-scoped routers on the same host reuse its variable). The Hub sets PORTCULLIS_HOST_<ROUTER> to the instance's full hostname for it; <ROUTER> is the template's original router name upper-cased, with - and . turned into _. The default subdomain <sub> is one DNS label (^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$), and a template uses one rule form for all its routers. Router rules use it with the default subdomain:

traefik.http.routers.grafana.rule: Host(`${PORTCULLIS_HOST_GRAFANA:-grafana.portcullis.local}`)
traefik.http.routers.vaultwarden-admin.rule: Host(`${PORTCULLIS_HOST_VAULTWARDEN:-passwords.portcullis.local}`) && PathPrefix(`/admin`)

Instance variables the Hub sets for every instance (never declare them in env, settings or ports; always use the default form with the default instance's value):

Variable Value PORTCULLIS_INSTANCE Instance id (the template id for the default instance) PORTCULLIS_HOST_<ROUTER> Full hostname for host router <router> PORTCULLIS_OIDC_CLIENT_ID Keycloak client id of the first keycloak_clients entry PORTCULLIS_OIDC_CLIENT_ID_<KEY> Keycloak client id of each entry; <KEY> = its client_id upper-cased, -/. → _ (two entries mapping to the same <KEY> are an error) PORTCULLIS_ACCESS_GROUP The instance's access group (access_group for the default instance, else users_<id>) PORTCULLIS_ADMIN_GROUP The instance's admin group (admin_group for the default instance, else admin_<id>)

A multi template has no ${PORTCULLIS_DOMAIN} in router rules (it may still use it for core hosts such as auth.${PORTCULLIS_DOMAIN:-portcullis.local}), no volume name: (the Hub sets portcullis_<key> for the default instance and portcullis_<instance-id>-<key> for the others), and no hard-coded Keycloak client id or group name in compose.yml. Routers that may serve extra-domain hostnames list portcullis-auth@docker on the router itself, never inside a chain middleware (the Hub swaps it for the extra-domain sign-in there, and refuses extra-domain hostnames for a router whose own chain reaches it).

items.title: hosts.immutable
items.text:
Host routers whose hostname is fixed once the instance exists, for apps that bind their data to their own hostname (Synapse's server_name is part of every user and room id):

hosts:
  immutable: [matrix]   # host router names

The admin chooses the hostname when creating the instance; the Hub refuses every later change (409), the default instance's too, and moving it means a new instance. The default instance's immutable hosts start as <sub>.<main domain> and are pinned on its first enable: a later main-domain change never moves them (the instance shows as error until the old domain is added as an extra domain). A restore into a new id keeps the archive's hostname for such routers (contract §11.3, §11.6). tests/validate.py requires the list where it knows the app needs it (IMMUTABLE_HOSTS: matrix).

items.title: Validation
items.text:
Run the validator from the templates repo:

python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r tests/requirements.txt
.venv/bin/python tests/validate.py            # all templates
.venv/bin/python tests/validate.py my-app     # one template (cross-template checks still run)
.venv/bin/python tests/validate.py --strict   # warnings fail too

It prints one line per problem with a hint. Exit codes: 0 OK, 1 rule violations, 2 usage or setup error. Besides the schema, it checks:

Layout

  • the directory name is a valid app ID (^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$)
  • the files are named exactly manifest.yaml and compose.yml
  • tests/apps/<app-id>.sh exists
  • the directory is listed in .github/dependabot.yml
  • .core-ref holds exactly one ref

Manifest

  • no variable is written twice across env, ports and the settings' env deliveries, and none shadows a core variable
  • links (see links)
  • every secret_env is an env entry with generate: random
  • port bind values are IPs and range values are valid
  • config_files sources exist
  • auth.native_login only with method: custom and sso: false, and a custom app with group_access: true declares it

Networks and volumes

  • Traefik-routed services use networks: [default, portcullis-proxy], and internal services stay off portcullis-proxy
  • portcullis-proxy is declared external: true, and no other networks are used
  • volumes of single templates declare name: portcullis_<volume>, unique across templates and never external; volumes of multi templates declare no name: (NEW, contract v2)

Variables

  • core variables use their default form, e.g. ${PORTCULLIS_TRAEFIK_IP:-172.31.250.2}
  • instance variables (PORTCULLIS_INSTANCE, PORTCULLIS_HOST_*, PORTCULLIS_OIDC_CLIENT_ID*, PORTCULLIS_ACCESS_GROUP, PORTCULLIS_ADMIN_GROUP) use their default form with the default instance's value, the same default at every use, and are never declared in the manifest (NEW, contract v2)
  • every other variable is declared in the manifest
  • required ${VAR:?} variables are generate: random env entries

Services

  • no ports:, build:, container_name: or env_file:
  • every image is pinned tag@sha256:digest, and floating tags (latest, 16-alpine, ...) are rejected

Bind mounts

  • only ./templates/<app-id>/<file> (the file must exist) and ./certs/ca-bundle.crt:<path>:ro
  • never ./scripts/ or another template's files

Routers

  • every router has a rule of the form Host(`${PORTCULLIS_HOST_<ROUTER>:-<sub>.portcullis.local}`) (NEW, contract v2), optionally && <path matchers>, where <ROUTER> is the host router of that hostname; single templates may still use Host(`<sub>.${PORTCULLIS_DOMAIN:-portcullis.local}`). No core subdomain
  • each hostname has exactly one host router, no two host routers map to the same variable, and the template doesn't mix the two rule forms
  • no router, service or middleware name contains _ (NEW, contract v2)
  • entrypoints: websecure, and tls.options one of authaware@file, public@file, protected@file (mtls apps need protected@file)
  • security-headers@file is in the middlewares
  • portcullis-auth@docker and portcullis-groups@docker always appear together, in that order
  • forward-auth and header-auth routers use them; native-OIDC host-wide routers don't
  • public, custom and mtls routers use neither (for custom apps the Hub adds them, see auth.native_login)
  • each admin_paths entry is served by a gated router

Public exceptions (auth.public_access)

  • only for forward-auth, header-auth and native-oidc; header-auth apps list identity_headers, and every identity-like X-…/Remote-… header in compose.yml must be among them
  • the prefix, broad, never-public, overlap, matcher and token_pattern rules of auth.public_access
  • exact paths have a justification and no {token}; supporting prefixes don't name a file
  • no router or middleware named portcullis-public-*

Header trust

  • header-auth apps restrict identity headers to Traefik's IP
  • nothing trusts **, 0.0.0.0/0, ::/0 or the proxy subnet

Instances (NEW, contract v2; instances: multi)

  • no ${PORTCULLIS_DOMAIN} in any router rule
  • every env value, hostname: or label that names one of the template's own hosts uses its PORTCULLIS_HOST_<ROUTER> variable (no https://<sub>.${PORTCULLIS_DOMAIN…} for its own subdomains)
  • urls and redirect URIs name the template's own hosts only as {{HOST_<ROUTER>}}
  • no hard-coded Keycloak client id or group name in compose.yml (use PORTCULLIS_OIDC_CLIENT_ID*, PORTCULLIS_ACCESS_GROUP, PORTCULLIS_ADMIN_GROUP)
  • no router, service or middleware name starting with portcullis-, and no own paths under /oauth2/
  • bind mounts of support files are read-only (:ro)

AI support (check_ai, the Hub's ValidateAI rule for rule; NEW)

  • an ai: block with exactly one of mcp and unsupported (non-empty, ≤ 200 characters); alternative and chat only with unsupported, on_change only with mcp
  • the alias portcullis-mcp-<id>--<companion> is one DNS label: 15 + len(<id>) + 2 + len(<companion>) ≤ 63, checked with the template id (the default instance; the Hub also checks it for every other instance at create and at AI switch-on)
  • companions: the field rules of ai; source set; service in compose.yml with a name matching ^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$; a companion service without Traefik labels, off portcullis-proxy, without network_mode / container_name / hostname, used by one companion; router a host router; public_path rules; builtin with upstream: official; app_oauth only builtin, with revoke and modes: [read_write]; app_token with mint and revoke; identity_headers with a caller_secret whose env is a generate: random entry; default_mode in modes
  • every hook the block names exists with exactly when: [ai]; no ai hook the block doesn't name; ai never next to another trigger
  • no ai.mcp with auth.admin_paths, auth.method public or mtls, or without an HTTP router
  • ai_client only in an ai.chat template, which has exactly one
  • the prefix portcullis-mcp- nowhere in compose.yml (any key or value, case-insensitive: router, service or middleware names, compose services, container_name, hostname, network aliases included); no keycloak_clients[].client_id starting portcullis-ai-; mcp isn't a default subdomain; the core names mcp-gate (service), mcp_gate_data (volume) and the Traefik names mcp, hub-mcp, people-mcp, mcp-gate are reserved
  • a companion service publishes no host ports; no service uses network_mode: service:<a companion service>; an identity_headers companion has its trust network (above)
  • PORTCULLIS_AI_* and PORTCULLIS_MCP_GATE_IP never declared; PORTCULLIS_AI_ENABLED / PORTCULLIS_AI_READONLY_<NAME> only as ${…:-false} / ${…:-true}, PORTCULLIS_MCP_GATE_IP only as ${PORTCULLIS_MCP_GATE_IP:-172.31.250.3}; PORTCULLIS_AI_PROVIDER_* never referenced, and no service sets one (an environment key or list item, any case); no environment variable name built by interpolation; no PORTCULLIS_AI_ in a ${…} default or alternate value; ai-providers not a files[] name
  • an ai_client entry has secret_env; ai.chat.file.mount doesn't collide with a files[] mount on that service; AI hooks don't run on a kind: companion service
  • companion images pinned tag@sha256:digest like every image

VPN (check_vpn, the Hub's ValidateVPN rule for rule, with the same refusal texts in the same order through the shared vectors tests/vpn_vectors.json; NEW)

  • the field rules of vpn: vpn.label: a single line of 1–64 characters, vpn.ranges: 1–8 IPv4 prefixes, vpn.ranges[<i>]: <v> is not an IPv4 prefix between /8 and /30, vpn.ranges: <a> overlaps <b>, vpn.ranges[<i>]: {{setting:<k>}} must name a cidr setting, vpn.ingress.proxy_protocol: only v2, vpn.identity.source: hook or static, vpn.identity.owner: oidc_sub or username, vpn.identity: source static takes no hook or owner, vpn.identity.refresh: between 15s and 10m, vpn.dns: exactly one of hook and manual: true
  • the ingress service and its namespace: vpn.ingress.service: <s> is not a service of compose.yml, … has network_mode, … is a job, … is an AI companion, … has a Traefik router, … publishes ports, … shares <s>'s network namespace: only the pinned ghcr.io/porelli/portcullis-forwarder image may; vpn: service <n> uses network_mode: host, vpn: service <n> uses pid: host
  • hooks: vpn.identity.hook / vpn.dns.hook: <h> is not a hook with exactly when: [vpn], hooks[<n>]: when: [vpn] needs a vpn: block that names it, hooks[<n>]: vpn can't be combined with other triggers
  • vpn.control_routers: <r> is not a host router of the template, vpn.control_routers: <r> serves an admin UI
  • every template router, with or without a vpn: block: router <r>: entrypoints must be 'websecure' (the Hub adds vpnsecure per instance)
  • reserved: ${PORTCULLIS_VPN_*} anywhere ($$PORTCULLIS_VPN_EDGE in a shell is fine) and as a settings/env key; the prefix portcullis-vpn anywhere in compose.yml; the core names wg (service), wg_data and vpn_doc (volumes), portcullis-vpn, portcullis-vpn-edge, portcullis-metrics-wg and wg-egress (networks). strip-client-forwarded@file may be listed in a router's middlewares (core runs it first anyway)

Cross-template

  • no default subdomain or volume name is used by two templates

items.title: Settings, files, hooks and reload
items.text:
check_settings in tests/validate.py refuses what the Hub refuses when it discovers the template, with the same messages (setting <key>: …). A green Lint means the Hub lists the template. Besides the field rules above:

  • Options: keys unique; section listed in sections; label, description, scope and applies valid; the type known (contract v2 types and the reserved folder type refused); only the constraints the type takes; default, bounds, step and group_values valid values of the option.
  • Scope fields: privileged, self_visible, resolve, resolve_choices and group_values only with scope: person, which needs a default; admin_override only with person_entered; no default for group; unique only for lists and person-entered string / int; generate only for secrets; writes_as only for paths; paths instance only.
  • Privileged: enum or bool only, the default its lowest value, no {{ACCESS_GROUP}} preset.
  • resolve fits the type; group_values keys are only {{ACCESS_GROUP}} / {{ADMIN_GROUP}} and the manifest declares that group.
  • requires: instance options only, naming existing instance options, not itself.
  • Deliveries: each one exactly one kind; at least one for every scope but instance; a per-person delivery for person; no per-person env; group env with render.format: json; applies: live with a hook (or a file with on_membership_change: hook); applies: reload and on_membership_change: reload with reload.
  • Env: the name rules of Deliveries; compose interpolates it and doesn't hard-code it; indexed env only for instance lists with max_items (≤ 64), covering every index compose references.
  • Claims: native-oidc, a declared client, a name that isn't reserved, a json_type that fits the render, one option per claim and client.
  • Headers: the name form, gated routers, every router to the backend's network namespace behind forward-auth, no identity-less method, no Traefik-labelled network_mode: host service, one option per header.
  • Files: declared, field only for per-person scopes, one option per field; names unique, services in compose.yml, mounts absolute and clean, not colliding with another file or a path target on the same service.
  • Hooks: names unique, services in compose.yml, a non-empty argv without control characters, valid when, timeout ≤ 10m.
  • Reload: {service, signal} or {hook}, not both; the service or hook declared; signal HUP, USR1 or USR2.
  • Person-entered: the rules of Person-entered options.
  • Render: units, integer, unlimited (required with allow_unlimited), true / false, join and format fit the type; yaml / csv only on file and hook deliveries (never for a person_entered scalar); on an env delivery true, false, unlimited and join without ' or \; a numeric unlimited no size within min / max renders as.
  • Values: the default and every group_values value render through every delivery (the implicit UPPER(key) env included), and an env value holds no ', \ or line break (JSON text: no \" escapes either).
  • Secrets: scope: instance only; generate.length within min_len / max_len.

  • Shared folders, checks and gids: the rules and every refusal are listed in contracts §13.15. In short: folder only on instance path options and never with mode, needs or writes_as; runs_as matches the service's compose user:; gids 60000–60999 (the folder groups) are refused wherever a gid comes from; on every service, the compose user: uid is a whole number, a user name or one reference, its gid a whole number or one reference, and each group_add entry a whole number, a group name or one reference, where a reference is exactly $NAME, ${NAME}, ${NAME:-n} or ${NAME-n} naming an instance int option (no mixed text, nesting or + forms); YAML !!binary is refused anywhere.

  • Setup options and jobs (NEW (apps)): the rules of Setup options and jobs, with the Hub's messages (setting <key>: …, jobs: <service> …, service <s>: …).

  • File sharing (Per-person credentials and ids): person_secret / person_id only on a router-less custom template with group_access: true and access_group; their fields as listed (wrong hash, length < 24 or not a multiple of 4, a list or non-file delivery, a missing or colliding mount, revoke_on_leave not true, on_restore not void, no hook on mount.service with credential_change, any scope field, an unknown pool, self_visible not false on person_id, a bad username.pattern, an info placeholder naming an unknown or ineligible option or port are refused); uid_from / gid_from name a person_id option, gid_from needs uid_from and joins_group: template; requires_any names existing instance options, not itself; format: tsv files get no secret and no table; expand_members only on file deliveries of group / groups options; credential_change is a valid when; the volume key portcullis-hub-secrets is refused (as a key, a volume source and in volumes_from); ${PORTCULLIS_LOCAL_NETWORKS} only in exactly that form; ${PORTCULLIS_FOLDER_GID_<KEY>} only in exactly that form, in environment: of the service a folder option <KEY> targets.

The validator also warns when a service reads a secrets file but runs neither as root nor as user: "10001".

items.title: Complete example
items.text:
A native-OIDC app with path settings, generated secrets and a Keycloak client:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=../schema/manifest.schema.json
name: Jellyfin
description: Free and open-source media server -- movies, TV, music, live TV
icon: "\U0001F4FA"
category: media
tags: [media, movies, tv, music, streaming, opensource]
links:
  website: https://jellyfin.org/
  source: https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin

auth:
  method: native-oidc
  sso: true
  group_access: true
  group_admin: true
  access_group: users_jellyfin
  admin_group: admin_jellyfin
  notes: >
    SSO-Auth plugin with group enforcement. Users must be in access_group
    to log in. Members of admin_group get Jellyfin admin.

settings:
  sections: [Libraries]
  options:
    - key: movies_path
      label: Movies folder
      description: Host path to your movies library
      section: Libraries
      type: path
      mode: ro
      needs: read
      writes_as: {uid: 0, gid: 0}
      target:
        service: jellyfin
        mount: /data/movies
      applies: restart

env:
  - key: JELLYFIN_ADMIN_PASSWORD
    description: Jellyfin admin password
    generate: random
  - key: JELLYFIN_OIDC_SECRET
    description: Jellyfin OIDC client secret
    generate: random

keycloak_clients:
  - client_id: jellyfin
    secret_env: JELLYFIN_OIDC_SECRET
    redirect_uris:
      - "https://media.{{DOMAIN}}/sso/OID/redirect/keycloak"
    name: Jellyfin

config_files: []

urls:
  - label: Jellyfin
    url: "https://media.{{DOMAIN}}"

ai:
  unsupported: "No official MCP server; community servers are small and not vetted by Portcullis"

A forward-auth app with host ports:

name: Pi-hole
description: Network-wide ad blocking via DNS sinkhole
icon: "\U0001F6AB"
category: networking
tags: [dns, adblock, privacy, filtering]
links:
  website: https://pi-hole.net/
  source: https://github.com/pi-hole/pi-hole

auth:
  method: forward-auth
  sso: false
  group_access: true
  group_admin: false
  access_group: users_pihole
  admin_group: admin_pihole
  notes: No SSO support. Has its own web password. Access gated by group-gate middleware.

ports:
  - key: PIHOLE_DNS_TCP_HOST
    label: DNS (TCP)
    container: 53
    protocol: tcp
    default: 53
    required: true
    service: pihole
  - key: PIHOLE_DNS_UDP_HOST
    label: DNS (UDP)
    container: 53
    protocol: udp
    default: 53
    required: true
    service: pihole

env:
  - key: PIHOLE_WEBPASSWORD
    description: Pi-hole web interface password
    generate: random

keycloak_clients: []
config_files: []

urls:
  - label: Dashboard
    url: "https://pihole.{{DOMAIN}}/admin"

ai:
  unsupported: "No MCP server known, and every member of the access group is a full administrator of the app (no per-person rights to act with)"

The real manifests of every built-in template are rendered in the App Catalog.

items.title: SAML Integration
items.text: This guide shows how to integrate a SAML-capable application with Portcullis, using Nextcloud as a worked example. The same pattern applies to any app that supports SAML 2.0.

items.title: Overview
items.text:
User (YubiKey) --> Traefik --> App
                                |
                                v  SAML SSO
                             Keycloak (IdP)
                                |
                                v  user lookup
                              LLDAP

The user authenticates at the Traefik layer (with a passkey, or a YubiKey or browser certificate). The app then uses SAML to verify the user's identity via Keycloak, which looks up users in LLDAP.

items.title: Step 1: Deploy the App
items.text:
Create a Docker Compose file for the app (or use its template from the catalog). The key Traefik labels are:

services:
  nextcloud:
    image: nextcloud:<version>-apache@sha256:<digest>   # pin tag + digest
    environment:
      NEXTCLOUD_ADMIN_USER: admin
      NEXTCLOUD_ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${NEXTCLOUD_ADMIN_PASSWORD:?generated}   # never ship a default password
      NEXTCLOUD_TRUSTED_DOMAINS: "nextcloud.${PORTCULLIS_DOMAIN}"
    networks:
      - default
      - portcullis-proxy
    labels:
      traefik.enable: "true"
      traefik.http.routers.nextcloud.rule: "Host(`nextcloud.${PORTCULLIS_DOMAIN}`)"
      traefik.http.routers.nextcloud.entrypoints: websecure
      traefik.http.routers.nextcloud.tls.options: authaware@file
      traefik.http.routers.nextcloud.middlewares: security-headers@file
      traefik.http.services.nextcloud.loadbalancer.server.port: "80"

networks:
  portcullis-proxy:
    external: true

Apps join portcullis-proxy (shared with Traefik), never the core portcullis network.

Note: SAML apps handle their own authentication flow with Keycloak, so they do not need the portcullis-auth@docker forward-auth middleware.

items.title: Step 2: Register the App as a SAML Client in Keycloak
2a. Open Keycloak Admin
items.text: Navigate to https://auth.<your-domain>/admin/ and sign in with your passkey as a member of lldap_admin (the realm admins of the portcullis realm). Select the portcullis realm from the dropdown.

items.title: 2b. Create a New SAML Client
items.text:
1. Navigate to Clients and click Create client
  2. Set:
  3. Client type: SAML
  4. Client ID: https://nextcloud.<your-domain>/apps/user_saml/saml/metadata
  5. Click Next
  6. On the next screen:
  7. Name: Nextcloud
  8. Root URL: https://nextcloud.<your-domain>
  9. Valid redirect URIs: https://nextcloud.<your-domain>/*
  10. Click Save

items.title: 2c. Configure SAML Settings
items.text:
In the client settings, go to the Settings tab:

  • Name ID format: username
  • Force name ID format: ON
  • Sign assertions: ON
  • Signature algorithm: RSA_SHA256
  • SAML signature key name: KEY_ID

Go to the Keys tab:

  • Client signature required: OFF (unless the app is configured to sign requests)

items.title: 2d. Add Attribute Mappers
items.text:
Go to Client scopes, click the client's dedicated scope, then Add mapper and select By configuration:

Email mapper:

  • Mapper type: User Property
  • Name: email
  • Property: email
  • SAML Attribute Name: urn:oid:0.9.2342.19200300.100.1.3
  • SAML Attribute NameFormat: URI Reference

Username mapper:

  • Mapper type: User Property
  • Name: username
  • Property: username
  • SAML Attribute Name: urn:oid:0.9.2342.19200300.100.1.1
  • SAML Attribute NameFormat: URI Reference

Display name mapper:

  • Mapper type: User Property
  • Name: displayName
  • Property: firstName
  • SAML Attribute Name: urn:oid:2.16.840.1.113730.3.1.241
  • SAML Attribute NameFormat: URI Reference

items.title: 2e. Note the IdP Metadata URL
items.text:
You will need this when configuring the app:

https://auth.<your-domain>/realms/portcullis/protocol/saml/descriptor

items.title: Step 3: Configure the App for SAML
items.text: This section uses Nextcloud as an example. Adapt the field names for your specific app.

items.title: 3a. Enable the SAML Plugin
items.text:
In Nextcloud, enable the SSO & SAML authentication app:

docker compose exec nextcloud php occ app:enable user_saml

items.title: 3b. Configure SAML Settings
items.text:
In Nextcloud's Administration settings under SSO & SAML authentication:

General:

  • Attribute to map the UID to: urn:oid:0.9.2342.19200300.100.1.1

Identity Provider Data:

  • Identifier of the IdP entity: https://auth.<your-domain>/realms/portcullis
  • URL target of the IdP where the SP will send the Authentication Request: https://auth.<your-domain>/realms/portcullis/protocol/saml
  • URL Location of IdP where the SP will send the SLO Request: https://auth.<your-domain>/realms/portcullis/protocol/saml
  • Public X.509 certificate of the IdP: Download from the SAML descriptor URL (Step 2e), extract the <ds:X509Certificate> value, and paste it

Service Provider Data:

  • Identifier of the SP entity: https://nextcloud.<your-domain>/apps/user_saml/saml/metadata

Attribute mapping:

  • Attribute to map the displayname to: urn:oid:2.16.840.1.113730.3.1.241
  • Attribute to map the email address to: urn:oid:0.9.2342.19200300.100.1.3

items.title: 3c. Test SAML Login
items.text:
1. Open a private/incognito window
  2. Go to https://nextcloud.<your-domain>
  3. You should see a "Login with SSO" button or be redirected automatically
  4. Keycloak authenticates with your passkey (or your YubiKey or browser certificate, if that method is on)
  5. You are logged into the app

items.title: Step 4: Optional -- LDAP User Backend
items.text:
For richer user integration (groups, quotas, etc.), you can also configure the app's LDAP backend to read from LLDAP directly:

Setting Value Host lldap (Docker service name) Port 3890 User DN uid=admin,ou=people,<your-base-dn> Password Your LLDAP admin password Base DN Your LLDAP_BASE_DN value User object class person Username attribute uid Email attribute mail Group object class groupOfUniqueNames

This way, users and groups from LLDAP appear directly in the app, while SAML handles the authentication flow.

items.title: General SAML Pattern
items.text:
The same steps apply to any SAML-capable application:

  1. Deploy the app behind Traefik (no forward-auth middleware needed)
  2. Create a SAML client in Keycloak with the app's entity ID and ACS URL
  3. Configure attribute mappers for email, username, and display name
  4. Point the app's SAML settings at Keycloak's IdP metadata
  5. Test the SSO flow

items.title: "Invalid signature" on SAML response
items.text:
• Ensure the IdP certificate in the app matches the one from Keycloak's SAML descriptor
  • Check that "Sign assertions" is ON in the Keycloak client config

items.title: User not found after SAML login
items.text:
• Verify the UID attribute mapping matches between Keycloak and the app
  • Check that the user exists in LLDAP and has synced to Keycloak (Keycloak admin panel, Users, search for the username)

items.title: SAML loop / redirect issues
items.text:
• Ensure the app's trusted domains configuration includes your full domain
  • Check that the entity ID in Keycloak matches exactly what the app sends
  • Verify the ACS URL is correct in Keycloak's Valid Redirect URIs

items.title: Mixed content / proxy issues
items.text:
For apps behind a reverse proxy, you typically need to configure the app to know it is behind HTTPS. For Nextcloud, add to config.php:

'overwriteprotocol' => 'https',
'overwrite.cli.url' => 'https://nextcloud.<your-domain>',
'trusted_proxies' => ['172.31.250.2'],   // PORTCULLIS_TRAEFIK_IP only

Trust only Traefik's fixed address (PORTCULLIS_TRAEFIK_IP, default 172.31.250.2), never whole private ranges: every app container on portcullis-proxy could otherwise set its own X-Forwarded-For.

Other apps have similar settings (e.g., FORCE_HTTPS, TRUST_PROXY, SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER).

items.title: Third-Party Apps
items.text:
This guide explains how to put existing Docker apps behind Portcullis authentication without creating a Hub template. Use this when you have an app that:

  • Is already running (or you manage its compose file yourself)
  • Doesn't need to appear in the Hub catalog
  • Just needs to be reachable through Portcullis with SSO/group enforcement

items.title: Quick Overview
items.text: Any Docker container can join the portcullis-proxy network and get Traefik routing + authentication by adding the right labels. No manifest, no Hub, no template repo required.

items.title: Option 1: Forward Auth (app has no SSO support)
items.text: Best for apps that have no OIDC/SAML support — Portcullis handles authentication entirely.

items.title: compose.yml
items.text:
services:
  myapp:
    image: myorg/myapp:latest
    networks:
      - default
      - portcullis-proxy
    labels:
      traefik.enable: "true"
      traefik.http.routers.myapp.rule: Host(`myapp.${PORTCULLIS_DOMAIN}`)
      traefik.http.routers.myapp.entrypoints: websecure
      traefik.http.routers.myapp.tls.options: authaware@file
      traefik.http.routers.myapp.middlewares: client-headers@file,portcullis-auth@docker,portcullis-groups@docker,security-headers@file
      traefik.http.services.myapp.loadbalancer.server.port: "8080"
    restart: unless-stopped

networks:
  portcullis-proxy:
    external: true

items.title: What this does
items.text:
1. User visits https://myapp.yourdomain.com
  2. portcullis-auth@docker (oauth2-proxy) checks for a session cookie
  3. No cookie → redirect to Keycloak → user authenticates with YubiKey
  4. portcullis-groups@docker (group-gate) checks the user's groups
  5. If authorized → request forwarded to your app

items.title: Group enforcement
items.text:
Add your app's subdomain (on the main domain) to group-gate/group-gate-map.conf in the core checkout:

myapp=users_myapp

Then create the group in LLDAP and add users to it. group-gate re-reads the map file on every request, so no restart is needed. If you skip this step, any authenticated Portcullis user can access the app (group-gate logs ALLOW-UNMAPPED).

Use a hostname no Hub app uses

The map file takes <sub>=<group> entries and group-gate expands each <sub> to <sub>.<PORTCULLIS_DOMAIN>; the Hub's policy file (version 6) keys everything by full hostname. If a Hub-enabled instance routes the same hostname, the Hub's groups entry overrides the map file. Hosts Portcullis can't serve — neither <label>.<PORTCULLIS_DOMAIN> nor an added domain <d> / <label>.<d> — are always denied by group-gate. An app on an added domain needs the Hub (it publishes those hosts); the map file only covers the main domain. Core subdomains (auth, traefik, hub, directory, enroll, people, metrics, mcp) cannot be reused.

client-headers@file must come before portcullis-groups@docker, so group-gate sees the YubiKey or browser certificate and can enforce revocation. For admin-only paths, use a separate PathPrefix router; per-path groups (path_groups) are only published by the Hub for templates.

items.title: Passing user identity
items.text:
The authenticated user's LLDAP username is available to your app in the X-Forwarded-User header (set by the group-gate middleware), the email in X-Forwarded-Email and the groups in X-Auth-Request-Groups. Identify users by the username: LLDAP users can edit their own email. Many apps support "trusted header" authentication.

Trust the header only from Traefik

Every container on portcullis-proxy can connect to your app directly. Configure the app to accept identity headers only from PORTCULLIS_TRAEFIK_IP (default 172.31.250.2), never from the whole subnet. See Header Auth Pattern → Header Security.

App Framework Config Grafana GF_AUTH_PROXY_ENABLED=true, GF_AUTH_PROXY_HEADER_NAME=X-Forwarded-User, GF_AUTH_PROXY_HEADER_PROPERTY=username, GF_AUTH_PROXY_WHITELIST=172.31.250.2 Kanboard REVERSE_PROXY_AUTH=true, REVERSE_PROXY_USER_HEADER=HTTP_X_FORWARDED_USER, TRUSTED_PROXY_NETWORKS=172.31.250.2/32 Firefly III AUTHENTICATION_GUARD=remote_user_guard Generic Read X-Forwarded-User header in your app

items.title: Option 2: Native OIDC (app supports OpenID Connect)
items.text: Best for apps that have built-in OIDC/OAuth2 support. The app handles its own login flow with Keycloak.

items.title: Step 1: Register a Keycloak client
items.text:
# Get admin token
TOKEN=$(curl -s http://localhost:8080/realms/master/protocol/openid-connect/token \
  -d "client_id=admin-cli" \
  -d "username=admin" \
  -d "password=$KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD" \
  -d "grant_type=password" | jq -r '.access_token')

# Register client
curl -s http://localhost:8080/admin/realms/portcullis/clients \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "clientId": "myapp",
    "enabled": true,
    "protocol": "openid-connect",
    "publicClient": false,
    "secret": "your-client-secret-here",
    "redirectUris": ["https://myapp.yourdomain.com/callback"],
    "standardFlowEnabled": true,
    "directAccessGrantsEnabled": false,
    "defaultClientScopes": ["openid", "profile", "email", "acr", "groups"]
  }'

items.title: Step 2: Configure your app
items.text:
Point your app's OIDC settings to:

Setting Value Issuer / Authority https://auth.yourdomain.com/realms/portcullis Discovery URL https://auth.yourdomain.com/realms/portcullis/.well-known/openid-configuration Client ID myapp Client Secret your-client-secret-here Scopes openid email profile groups Redirect URI https://myapp.yourdomain.com/callback

items.title: Step 3: compose.yml
items.text:
Native OIDC apps don't need portcullis-auth@docker — they handle auth themselves:

services:
  myapp:
    image: myorg/myapp:latest
    environment:
      OIDC_ISSUER: https://auth.${PORTCULLIS_DOMAIN}/realms/portcullis
      OIDC_CLIENT_ID: myapp
      OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET: your-client-secret-here
    networks:
      - default
      - portcullis-proxy
    labels:
      traefik.enable: "true"
      traefik.http.routers.myapp.rule: Host(`myapp.${PORTCULLIS_DOMAIN}`)
      traefik.http.routers.myapp.entrypoints: websecure
      traefik.http.routers.myapp.tls.options: authaware@file
      traefik.http.routers.myapp.middlewares: client-headers@file,security-headers@file
      traefik.http.services.myapp.loadbalancer.server.port: "8080"
    restart: unless-stopped

networks:
  portcullis-proxy:
    external: true

No portcullis-auth@docker middleware

Native OIDC apps handle their own auth flow. Don't add portcullis-auth@docker or portcullis-groups@docker — the app redirects to Keycloak itself.

items.title: Staging certificates
items.text:
If you're using Let's Encrypt staging (ACME_STAGING=true), your app needs to trust the staging CA. Mount the CA bundle:

services:
  myapp:
    volumes:
      - /path/to/portcullis/certs/ca-bundle.crt:/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt:ro
    environment:
      # For Node.js apps:
      NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS: /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt
      # For Go apps:
      SSL_CERT_FILE: /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt

items.title: Option 3: Public (no authentication)
items.text:
For apps that should be publicly accessible:

services:
  myapp:
    image: myorg/myapp:latest
    networks:
      - default
      - portcullis-proxy
    labels:
      traefik.enable: "true"
      traefik.http.routers.myapp.rule: Host(`myapp.${PORTCULLIS_DOMAIN}`)
      traefik.http.routers.myapp.entrypoints: websecure
      traefik.http.routers.myapp.tls.options: public@file
      traefik.http.routers.myapp.middlewares: security-headers@file
      traefik.http.services.myapp.loadbalancer.server.port: "8080"
    restart: unless-stopped

networks:
  portcullis-proxy:
    external: true

Note: tls.options: public@file (no certificate request) and no auth middleware.

items.title: Running Alongside Portcullis
items.text:
Start your app with its own project name to keep it isolated:

docker compose -p myapp -f /path/to/your/compose.yml up -d

Your app gets its own containers, network, and lifecycle — completely independent of the Portcullis core stack.

items.title: Comparison: Template vs Third-Party
items.text:
Feature Hub Template Third-Party Appears in Hub catalog Yes No One-click enable/disable Yes Manual compose up/down Auto-generated secrets Yes Manual Per-app settings UI Yes Edit compose/env directly Status/logs in Hub Yes docker compose logs Keycloak client auto-registration Yes Manual registration Group-gate mapping Via manifest (access_group, admin_paths) Edit group-gate/group-gate-map.conf Auth badges in UI Yes N/A

For apps you manage frequently or share with others, consider creating a proper template. For one-off apps or quick experiments, the third-party approach is simpler.

items.title: AI Support
items.text:
People can use their Portcullis apps from Claude, Claude Code or another MCP client, and from an AI page, as themselves: the AI gets exactly the person's rights in each app, signs in with the person's passkey, and every request is checked and logged by core's mcp-gate. This page is the administrator's guide. What people see is in Connect your AI; the interfaces are in contracts §15.

AI support is off on a new install. Nothing reaches an app through MCP until you switch the master switch on and switch AI support on for that app.

items.title: How it fits together
items.text:
graph LR
    C[Claude, Claude Code,<br/>other MCP clients] -->|OAuth 2.1 + PKCE| KC[Keycloak<br/>auth.<domain>]
    C -->|Bearer token| T[Traefik]
    P[AI page<br/>LibreChat] -->|each person's token| T
    T --> G[mcp-gate]
    G -->|person's credential<br/>or identity headers| CO[App companions]
    CO --> A[Apps]
    G -->|X-Portcullis-MCP-Secret| H[Hub :8890<br/>Portcullis MCP]
    H -->|gate files| G

Each MCP endpoint is its own OAuth resource with its own scope:

Endpoint Who What https://<app host>/mcp (an app's companion) the app's users (its settings population) the app, as the person https://mcp.<domain>/mcp (All my apps) every signed-in person every companion they can use plus their Portcullis account tools, one connection https://people.<domain>/mcp (Portcullis) every signed-in person their own account and apps; delegated people management for delegates https://hub.<domain>/mcp (Portcullis (admin)) lldap_admin members, only through clients you enable it for the Hub: instances, settings, users and groups, backups, the doctor

A token is minted for exactly one of them: a token whose audience names two resources is refused at both, so an MCP client asks for one resource's scope per token (checked by core's e2e-ai job on Keycloak 26.8.1).

A companion is the MCP server the AI talks to for one app: the app's built-in MCP server or the upstream project's (or a vetted community project's) published image, pinned by digest. Portcullis never writes MCP servers for apps; templates declare their companions in the ai: block, and each app's catalog page has an AI support section.

items.title: Before you start: reachability
items.text:
• Claude desktop, claude.ai and Claude mobile connect from Anthropic's servers (160.79.104.0/21), not from the person's device. For them, auth.<domain> and every app host people connect to must be reachable from the internet. Settings → AI says so. Claude Code and other local clients connect from the person's machine, so a LAN-only install works for them.
  • No certificates. No MCP client can present the person's YubiKey or browser certificate, so certificate methods never count for AI, and an app whose sign-in template needs a certificate in every alternative can't get AI support (the switch is refused with "needs a YubiKey or browser certificate on every sign-in"). A sign-in change that would make it so switches AI support off on that app first, and the preview lists it.
  • Rate limits are per person, not per IP: every hosted Claude user comes from Anthropic's range. Core's rate-limit@file (per source IP) still stays in front of every MCP router and is shared by everyone whose client runs in Anthropic's cloud.

items.title: Settings → AI
items.text:
Setting Default What it does AI support (master switch) off Off: the gate answers every AI request 503 "AI support is off on this Portcullis", the apps' AI switches are greyed out and people's "Connect your AI" cards are hidden; the AI clients and scopes are kept. Switching it on or off restarts every enabled app whose AI support is switched on AI clients offered all three, admin MCP off Each offered client is a Keycloak client people's assistants sign in with: portcullis-ai-claude (claude.ai, Claude desktop, mobile), portcullis-ai-claude-code (loopback localhost / 127.0.0.1 port 33418), portcullis-ai-generic (other MCP clients, same loopback URIs). All are public clients with PKCE S256, consent and a passkey sign-in. Unticking one deletes it, and everyone's connections through it end. The Portcullis admin MCP column is off for every client until you tick it, client by client Portcullis MCP both on For administrators (hub.<domain>/mcp) and for people (people.<domain>/mcp) Connection length unused 7 days, at most 30 Keycloak's offline-session idle (1–30 days) and maximum (1–90 days, ≥ idle) for the AI clients. After that the person signs in again in their assistant Rate limits 120 requests/min per person and app (burst 30), 600/min per person across apps, 60 tool calls/min per person and app, 10 confirmations started per person per hour, 10 app credentials created per person per minute, 4 parallel app calls per "All my apps" request Over a limit: 429 with Retry-After Allowed origins empty Browser origins (https://<host>[:port]) allowed to call; empty: a request with an Origin header is refused. Desktop and command-line clients send none

Access tokens last 5 minutes. Refresh tokens don't rotate: Keycloak 26.8 has no per-client switch, and rotating realm-wide breaks every forward-auth session. What ends a connection is the connection length above, the person's Disconnect on the People page, and every removal the Hub makes (which signs the person out of Keycloak). A stolen AI refresh token stays usable until one of those happens.

A Hub without the gate (no readable HUB_MCP_GATE_RECIPIENT_FILE or gate secret) shows "This core has no mcp-gate": the gate file says AI support is off and every AI request is refused. The settings are kept.

Unhealthy AI clients. If the Hub can't set up an AI client in Keycloak (an untagged client with that id exists, or Keycloak refuses the scopes), the client is left out of the gate file and off the People cards. Settings → AI doesn't show this yet: GET /api/ai/settings has no health field. Check the Hub's log when a client is missing from people's cards.

items.title: Switching an app on
items.text:
Each instance page has an AI tab (deep link #apps/<id>/ai):

  • The companion's facts: its MCP URL, whether it is built into the app or a companion container, official or community, the identity mode, the number of people who can use it (the app's settings population), active app credentials, and the template's "asks to confirm" and "never allowed" tool patterns.
  • AI support and the mode: read and write or read only, where the template offers both. Read-only hides and refuses the template's write tools at the gate, and, where the app supports it, the companion is started read-only too (PORTCULLIS_AI_READONLY_<NAME>, read-only credential scopes). Nextcloud supports neither: there the gate alone enforces read-only (see Residuals).
  • Switching on or off, or changing the mode, restarts a running app (its router labels change); the tab says so before you save. On a disabled app the switch only saves the state.
  • Status: on, off, failed (with the last error), unavailable (switched on but refused now: master off, a template that needs a certificate), revoking (off, a revoke_all is owed — at the next start, or after a template update, see the Doctor) and revoke pending (on, but kept off until the app's next start revokes its earlier credentials).
  • Refused while the master switch is off, the instance is being deleted or restored, the template says ai.unsupported, the sign-in needs a YubiKey or browser certificate, the companion alias would be longer than one DNS label, another container already answers to the alias, or a template update's revocation is still owed.
  • Revoke AI credentials now (not for identity-header companions, which hold none): one person's, or everyone's (revoke_all). People's assistants get new credentials on their next request while AI support is on.
  • Recent AI activity: the newest 20 lines of the gate's access log for the app (never arguments or results).

Switching on first revokes every app credential the companion's earlier life left (revoke_all): a failure is a 502 and nothing changes. A failure after the state is saved is an operation error (op ai) and saving the same again re-applies every step.

An AI page instance (the ai-chat template) has no companion; its AI support tab chooses its model providers.

items.title: Identity modes
items.text:
How the person's identity reaches the app is the template's choice, shown on the tab:

Mode How Leaving app_token The Hub mints a per-person app credential (portcullis-ai-<random>) in the app on the person's first request, through the template's mint hook; it is encrypted to the gate and injected on every call. Someone who never signed in to the app gets "Open in your browser once, then try again" The credential is marked revoking at once (the gate stops using it within seconds) and revoked in the app through the revoke hook, retried until it succeeds identity_headers The gate sends the person's username, email, groups and attribute headers plus a caller secret only the companion knows; the app trusts identity headers only from its companion, on a private trust network Nothing to revoke: the gate refuses the person from their next request app_oauth The app is its own MCP OAuth server and signs people in through Portcullis (Keycloak, passkey). The gate is not in the path: Portcullis doesn't log, confirm, rate-limit or filter these AI actions; the app's own rules apply The Hub runs the template's revoke hook for the person (below)

items.title: Who can use it, and leaving
items.text:
The people who can use a companion are the app's settings population: the access group's members (minus expired memberships), or every signed-in person when the app has no group access. The gate checks this on every request, so a person removed from the group is refused from their next request, not at token expiry. Expiries in expiring are refused from their time on.

When someone leaves:

  • their app_token credentials are revoked (above);
  • their upstream MCP sessions are closed;
  • once they can use no AI resource at all (deleted, or in no population), the Hub deletes their consents and offline sessions for every AI client;
  • a person's own Disconnect on the People page does the same for one client. Keycloak then refuses that client's refresh tokens (offline and online) at once, but access tokens already issued stay valid for up to 5 minutes. The gate's per-request population check still refuses a person who left.

app_oauth apps (Home Assistant). The Hub records who could use the app while its AI support was on (<data>/ai/oauth-seen.json): each person's LLDAP uuid and every Keycloak user id seen for them. A person who leaves:

  • with a verified record (uuid and at least one Keycloak id) gets the template's revoke with their Keycloak id (sub), which ends the AI tokens of exactly that app account;
  • with an unverifiable record (no uuid, the uuid changed, the id lookup failed three passes, or their record couldn't be written) makes the companion's revoke_all run, which ends every person's AI-client tokens in that app (people reconnect), and the person is listed on the AI tab and in the Doctor as left before their account could be matched. Their web, Companion-app and long-lived tokens remain: deactivate or delete them in the app (Home Assistant: Settings > People), then Dismiss them.

Switching an app_oauth companion off runs revoke_all only. A disabled instance, a policy or sign-in change are not leaving.

items.title: Confirmations
items.text:
Destructive actions need the person, in their browser, signing in again with a method the governing template accepts (the hub core page's template for admin tools, the people one for people tools, the app's for a companion; Fresh sign-in):

  • What needs one: companion tools matching the template's confirm patterns, tools the companion marks destructive, and the destructive (D) tools of the Portcullis MCP — deleting, restoring over, revoking, running code, and every call that widens access (adding someone to an administrator or permission group, a weaker policy, public access on, …).
  • The AI gets a link (https://people.<domain>/confirm/<id>, or https://hub.<domain>/confirm/<id> for admin tools) or a URL elicitation its client opens. The page shows what the Hub renders from the stored request — the action, its target, consequences and the exact arguments — never text the model wrote. Values taken from the request are quoted, and every invisible or reordering character (bidi controls, zero-width characters, unusual spaces) shows as \u…, so nothing on the page can be hidden. A request whose user, group or field names aren't valid is refused before any confirmation is created.
