DNS hardening (contract §12): internal/dnsplan (the record sets, the plan diff, the CAA merge rule — other CAs' entries kept, ours replaced, TestMergeKeepsOtherIssuers —, CAA values formatted differently from ours and the CA's judgement, TestWouldIssueFormatting, the RFC 8659 climb incl. an added child of the main domain, a CNAME blocking the address set, TestCNAMEBlocksAddressApply, a failed lookup reading unknown, never ok, TestBuildLookupFailureUnknown), internal/dnssec (the chain check's states on fakedns zones signed with miekg/dns: secure, unsigned, ds_missing, ds_mismatch, bogus by SERVFAIL then CD, an insecure parent), the account switch order (register → CAA → seen at both resolvers → order, TestWaitCAABothResolvers), DELETE and DNS_CAA=false removing only our CAA entries, the unknown CA skipping the set, per-record providers (cloudflare / porkbun) never dropping below our entries during a switch, the Cloudflare signer and Route 53 status reader against httptest fakes, DigitalOcean CAA through godo, and the one-shot tool (domains dns plan|apply|check|dnssec-enable: stdin only, unknown keys refused, credentials refused by check, the exit codes, traefik-account-uri printing only the URI).
  • mcp-gate (mcp-gate/): go mod verify, go vet, gofmt, go test -race ./.... The shared test vector of contract §15.4 (internal/config/testdata/mcp-gate.json and mcp-credentials.json, byte-identical to the Hub's internal/aigate/testdata/; gate file v2) is decoded strictly and re-encoded byte for byte; TestConfigV2Strict refuses version 1, acr_loa / min_loa, a rule leaf outside methods, groups of 9, depth 5, more than 48 leaves and a companion whose rule needs a certificate. internal/signin runs the shared sign-in vectors (internal/signin/testdata/signin_vectors.json, a byte copy of the Hub's internal/signin/testdata/vectors.json): rule shapes, meeting a rule, alternatives, the reader rejects. The step after the tests ("mcp-gate shared vectors match the Hub") compares all three files with the same-named Hub branch, else main, the same way (exact branch, at the listed commit). The tests cover the token rules (signature, issuer, audience, scope, client, the sign-in rule over the token's amr — a certificate, inv, an unknown or switched-off method never counts (TestTokenNeverCountsCertificates), checked after the population and met or refused on the people and admin resources too (TestPopulationBeforeSignInRule) —, population, Origin; a rule that doesn't decode names its path, never its value), resource metadata, protocol versions, tool policy, confirmations and continuations, rate limits, the access log (refusing unloggable calls), the aggregate (names, collisions, per-upstream clients and sign-in rules — TestAggregatePerUpstreamRule, entries keyed on the token's method set), the Portcullis proxy, and the impersonated refusal: a token with an act or pc_imp claim is refused (TestImpersonatedTokenRefused). The gate writes a request's access-log line after the response has gone out. Before reading the log, the end-to-end tests therefore wait until every request they sent (except the open GET stream) has finished being handled, then flush the log's queue. A test never reads a line that is still on its way. The compose wiring check also asserts the gate's networks (exactly portcullis-mcp with the Hub and Keycloak, and portcullis-proxy at its fixed IP), its secret mounts, mcp_gate_data (read-only in the Hub) and that no router targets the Hub's port 8890. A second check (sign-in part 2) pins group_gate_data to exactly group-gate (read-write at /data, 10003:10003 + group 10001) and the Hub (read-write at /group-gate-data), group-gate's two CA files (read-only under /etc/group-gate/ca/) and both CAs' CRL lists, the Hub's HUB_CLIENT_CERT_TTL / HUB_CERT_EXPIRY_WARN_DAYS, Keycloak's PORTCULLIS_SIGNIN_URL, no self-service middleware, and enroll-invite (PathPrefix(/invite/)) as the only router on enroll.<domain>; tests/test_cli.sh checks the same wiring in the files, the realm's two x509 executions and events settings, keycloak configure pushing each x509 config by its alias, and that no text names the retired enroll.<domain> self-service pages.

items.title: build-and-test (whole stack)
items.text:
It boots the stack with a CI override (no ACME; self-signed server cert from the internal PKI) and verifies:

  • Rebuild and recreate. After an upgrade that rebuilds a locally built service (portcullis-enroll), the running container uses the new image, and unchanged services (mcp-gate, postgres) keep their containers.

  • Vault

    • server-mode init and unseal, and the permissions on secrets/
    • after a restart it auto-unseals and the CA is unchanged
    • the enroll AppRole can only sign, list, read and revoke certificates and rotate the CRLs, on both CAs
  • PKI
    • both chain files are created and valid: certs/ca-chain.crt is exactly root + YubiKey CA + browser CA, certs/ca-chain-yubikey.crt exactly the YubiKey CA (no root, no browser CA)
    • Vault issues YubiKey certificates
  • Keycloak
    • the OIDC discovery and SAML descriptor endpoints
    • the WebAuthn policy
    • the portcullis-forward-auth client
    • portcullis-forward-auth requires PKCE S256: an authorization request without a code challenge gets no code, the X.509 login with one does (oauth2-proxy's alpha.yaml must keep code_challenge_method: S256)
    • the invite post-broker flow admits only clients with the portcullis-invite-client scope (only portcullis-forward-auth, never a realm default), and a second keycloak configure keeps an extra-domain callback on portcullis-forward-auth while dropping a wildcard
    • LLDAP users show up through the federation
    • the email-unverified scope has exactly one mapper (email), also after a second keycloak configure; a throwaway direct-grant client with that scope instead of email gets email but no email_verified in the ID token, access token and userinfo, while the built-in email scope sends email_verified: false
  • YubiKey certificates at the handshake
    • the Hub isn't running yet, so the step writes policy file v6 into hub_data (the starting methods, Standard the default, every gated core page on Standard; later steps add their keys to it): without a file group-gate denies everything
    • requests with no cert, or a cert from another CA, are rejected
    • cert info, including the serial, reaches the backend
    • requests arrive from Traefik's static IP
    • the group-gated test router (no forward-auth: the test sends the session headers itself, with an unsigned stand-in access token per method — group-gate reads only its amr / preferred_username) answers the step-up page to a cert without a session, the present-certificate page to an mtls session without the cert, and lets an mtls session with testuser's own unrevoked cert through
  • X.509 login
    • a login via Traefik with a real cert (pc_method=yubikey_cert) succeeds; the Hub isn't running yet, so the step writes a minimal signin-keycloak.json (the starting methods) into hub_data first, or the sign-in extension would refuse everyone
    • the same cert as a forged header sent straight to Keycloak (from the portcullis and portcullis-auth networks and from 127.0.0.1:8080) must not yield an authorization code
  • Header spoofing. Client-supplied cert headers and their aliases are dropped, and group-gate's path rules see X-Forwarded-Uri.
  • Socket proxies. A real docker compose project runs through socket-proxy-hub, and the denied sections (build, swarm, plugins, secrets, system, ...) fail. Traefik's proxy is read-only. Both proxies answer 403 to Podman's own API (/libpod/info, /libpod/play/kube, /v5.0.0/libpod/containers/json) and to /build.
  • Domains service (Pebble e2e). The image is built with GO_TAGS=testprovider (adds provider fake with records in memory + a DNS server on :8053). CI runs Pebble (-dnsserver domains:8053) and configures the service to use fake, Pebble's minica root, and DOMAINS_RESOLVERS=127.0.0.1:8053. It checks:
    • adding a domain, the records check, ACME DNS-01 order, serving the certificate
    • DELETE stops serving it
    • the served document contains only tls.certificates (no routers, services, middlewares)
    • every served certificate's SANs are exactly {<d>, *.<d>} for an added domain
    • Traefik picks up the certificate by SNI within ~25 s without restarting (StartedAt unchanged)
    • core hosts still serve the main-domain certificate, never a certificate from the HTTP provider
    • Traefik's API lists no @http object (routers, services, middlewares, serverstransports)
    • mutual TLS: the endpoint refuses requests without Traefik's certificate
    • a kept domain survives backup/restore
    • DNS hardening (DNS_CAA_ISSUER=pebble.test in the CI override, as Pebble isn't Let's Encrypt): GET /acme/account names Pebble's directory, the issuer pebble.test and an account URI; the plan of the added domain (/domains/<d>/dns?refresh=1) has can_write, its caa set ok, would_issue and the pin naming the service's own account, its address set ok, and the domain object has caa_ok: true; GET /main/dns is the read-only main-domain plan (can_write: false); domains report --main --json (what status reads) has the main plan and exactly the added domain
    • the one-shot dns-tool (docker compose run --rm -T dns-tool, credentials on stdin): apply --wait 60s with the fake provider in the tool's own zone ends with can_write, would_issue and every address / caa item ok; check without credentials, against the domains service's fake DNS, judges the added domain's pin ok (exit 0, can_write: false); check with credentials is refused
    • Pebble doesn't enforce CAA, so CI checks that the records are written and the steps run in order, not a CA's refusal; that is checked by hand on the test server, with Let's Encrypt staging

The production image is built without testprovider (no fake provider).

  • Live Keycloak access role test (opt-in). When PORTCULLIS_KEYCLOAK_LIVE_URL (e.g. http://keycloak:8080) and PORTCULLIS_KEYCLOAK_LIVE_WIPE=portcullis are set, the Hub runs TestLiveClientAccess: it wipes realm portcullis, rebuilds it from the export, creates an LDAP group and a test client with the access role enforced, and drives the flow to verify the role is checked and fails closed. This is the live proof of contract §8. It requires a running Keycloak and is off by default.

  • Hub

    • its LLDAP service account is set up first (the same lldap_service_account that portcullis up runs later in the job): the admin routes check the actor in LLDAP
    • runs as non-root
    • talks to Docker only via its proxy
    • answers 403 without the proxy secret
    • on a fresh install publishes policy file v6 with the four starting methods, Standard the default and Strong on hub / people (GET /api/signin agrees), which group-gate applies to an app without its own pick: a step-up for no session, through for a synced passkey, a security key or a bound certificate
    • an admin's PUT /api/signin/default to Strong reaches group-gate (a synced session gets the step-up or needs-stronger page, a bound certificate still opens the app), and back to Standard
    • the revocation test's precondition is live: testuser's bound mtls session opens the test router before the revocation, so only the revocation can turn 200 into 403
  • signin reset-core on the real Hub. First passkey_synced is switched off through the Hub's API (PUT /api/signin/methods/passkey_synced), so the reset has something to undo. Without --yes and a terminal it exits exactly 2; --yes prints method passkey_synced: off -> on (never "nothing to change"), the Hub runs and answers /healthz again with passkey_synced on and GET /api/signin shows hub and people moved from Strong (the fresh install's) to standard, the files the reset wrote — state.yaml (rewritten atomically, so a new inode owned by the writer), audit.jsonl, .hub.lock — are 10001:10001 (a root run would leave state.yaml root's), and the audit log's last signin.reset_core entry is by cli, ok, naming the change.
  • enroll serves only setup links. https://enroll.<d>/ and every path but /invite/… answer Traefik's 404. On the container itself (step "Find enroll; its retired pages and APIs are gone") :8443/healthz answers 200 and /, /users, /certs, /enroll/<u>, /api/users, /self, /api/self/renew answer 404 (POST /api/sign 404 / 405).
  • enroll's YubiKey certificate API (POST enroll:8444/internal/yubikey-certificates, contract §9.4, the admin CSR path that replaced /api/sign): with the bearer, testuser's CSR is signed on pki_int through enroll's AppRole (201, a PEM certificate issued by the YubiKey CA, chaining to certs/ca-chain.crt); no bearer or a wrong one is 401; the same CSR for admin is refused.
  • Sign-in flows and setup links.
    • first the realm's passwordless passkey policy is drifted (conveyance none, attachment cross-platform), and keycloak configure must restore it
    • the browser flow is exactly the sign-in extension's tree (contract §8.1: cookie · invite redirector · {portcullis-x509 (x509-config) · portcullis-x509 (x509-browser-config) · passkey with one conditional sub-flow per kind · portcullis-password-form}, then portcullis-template), every reference config has a known amr and maxAge 36000; it carries the [sync <hash>] marker and a second keycloak configure rebuilds nothing
    • the two x509 configs on the live realm, as keycloak configure pushed them: x509-config (yubikey_cert, amr mtls, the YubiKey CA, pki_int's CRLs) then x509-browser-config (browser_cert, file, the browser CA, pki_file's CRLs), both aborting on a stale CRL; the realm's events config keeps LOGIN, LOGIN_ERROR and IMPERSONATE
    • webauthn-register-passwordless enabled, the two-factor webauthn-register disabled; the realm has acr.loa.map {}, brute force (10 / 60 s / 900 s, not permanent) and direct passkey attestation
    • the invite post-broker flow: admit / deny sub-flows, then amr inv and portcullis-template
    • the LDAP federation has cachePolicy NO_CACHE (tests/test_shell_libs.sh also checks the realm export and that keycloak configure's patch sets it idempotently)
    • the invite identity provider is enabled, hidden, links existing users only (idp-detect-existing-broker-user, idp-auto-link), back-channel http://enroll:8445, PKCE; the service account portcullis-enroll has exactly view-users + manage-users
    • ./portcullis invite: link format, a new link revokes the older one, viewing doesn't consume it, a cross-site redeem is refused, portcullis-hub is refused, admin is allowed from the server
    • the Hub's invite API (enroll:8444, contract §9.4): 201 for a user, 409 for admin / portcullis-hub, 404 for an unknown user, 401 with a wrong secret; the Hub's copy of the secret matches; the JWKS serves an ES256 key
  • Stock impersonation is off. Keycloak's own POST …/users/{id}/impersonation answers non-2xx and names the feature.
  • acr scope has amr and impersonation. The live acr scope has exactly one amr mapper and one portcullis-impersonation mapper (access token, ID token, userinfo), the notice required action is enabled, and a second keycloak configure adds no second mapper.
  • Client-sent impersonation headers. X-Forwarded-Impersonator / X-Forwarded-Impersonation sent by the client never reach an app on the gated test router, and on people.<domain> GET /api/me/impersonation with forged headers answers {"active": null}.
  • ./portcullis up and the Hub's LLDAP account. portcullis-hub is in lldap_admin, the 0640 / group 10001 password file logs in, a password changed in LLDAP is reset from the file on the next up, and the Hub sees /run/portcullis/lldap and /run/portcullis/invite.
  • Revocation end to end, once through ./portcullis cert revoke and once through Vault's CRL alone.
  • enroll's certificates API (enroll:8444/internal/certificates, contract §9.4): 401 without Authorization, with an empty or wrong bearer or another scheme; with the bearer 200 and exactly {"certificates": [...]}, each entry exactly user (lowercase), serial, kind (yubikey / browser), not_before and not_after (RFC 3339 UTC), revoked (boolean); the test YubiKey certificate revoked above is listed as revoked: true under Vault's serial; Traefik's server certificate (*.portcullis.local) is not listed; no PEM in the answer. enroll's Go tests cover the fail-closed side: a serial whose read fails, whose certificate is missing, or whose revocation_time is missing or unreadable answers 503 for the whole list.
  • Session store (step "Test the session store"). sessions is healthy as 999:1000, read-only, all capabilities dropped, on portcullis-sessions only; secrets/sessions is 0700 and valkey.conf 0640 group 1000 without either password in clear. The ACL, through valkey-cli in the container (the password by environment name, never on a command line): an unauthenticated PING gets NOAUTH, a wrong password WRONGPASS; each proxy's user reads and writes only its own keys (_oauth2_proxy-* / __Host-portcullis_ext-*), the other's are NOPERM; keys, scan, flushall, config get / set, acl list, client list, info, shutdown, script flush are NOPERM; a Lua script reads its own key but neither the other proxy's key nor flushall. Then a real sign-in through forward-auth with a fresh YubiKey certificate for testuser (/oauth2/start?pc_method=yubikey_cert, curl's cookie jar as the browser) ends at /oauth2/auth with 202; the jar holds exactly one _oauth2_proxy (no _oauth2_proxy_0…), under 512 bytes, whose value decodes to an oauth2-proxy ticket v2.<id>.<secret> with id _oauth2_proxy-<32 hex>, and the store holds that key (not readable by forward-auth-ext). /oauth2/sign_out deletes it, and the old cookie then gets 401.
  • CLI. ./portcullis status.
  • Backup round-trip. It runs, in order:
    • ./portcullis backup with nothing stopped, then backup verify --local. A deliberately damaged backup must fail verification.
    • status --textfile.
    • backup --offsite twice to a local restic repository. The second run must be incremental, and retention must collapse same-day snapshots under keep-daily.
    • backup verify (off-host). A wrong BACKUP_PASSWORD must fail, and neither the root token nor the .env secrets may appear in the encrypted repository.
    • Restore into a fresh stack. Containers, volumes, .env, secrets/, certs/ and local backups are all deleted, as on a new host. Then restore --yes --from-offsite must bring back an active Vault, the Keycloak realm, the forward-auth client and the LLDAP user.

The step "Test the VPN service" (.github/ci/build-and-test-vpn-service.sh) runs ./portcullis vpn init on Docker and checks:

  • wg is added to COMPOSE_PROFILES, runs healthy as 10006 with group 10007 only, no capability, device, privilege or socket; wg_data is 2750 10006:10001, status.json 0640 group 10001, the people role is on, and secrets/wg/people.key is 0640 group 10006; the Hub reads wg_data and writes vpn_doc;
  • a whoami on both entrypoints: forged forwarding headers (23 of them) never reach the backend, X-Forwarded-For holds exactly one address (the real peer) and X-Real-Ip is the peer; group-gate never logs a forged value;
  • a PROXY header from a container on portcullis-vpn can't reach vpnsecure at all, and one from another portcullis-vpn-edge address is ignored; no edge port answers while no provider is wired;
  • vpn add-device and tests/e2e/vpn-client through the tunnel: the backend sees exactly the device's tunnel address and Traefik's own forwarding headers.

wg then stays on for the rest of the job (up, upgrade, backup and restore).

The step "Test the public guard (public exceptions) through Traefik" routes a test host through portcullis-public-guard@docker only and checks: no version-3 entry → 403; published prefix / static paths → 200; other paths, encoded / or #, dot-segment escapes → 403; Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, a credential header, credential cookies and query keys in PHP-mangled spellings → 403. The guard's unit tests are in tests/test_group_gate.py (PublicGuardTest, PhpVarNameTest).

items.title: e2e (browser)
items.text:
tests/e2e/e2e_login.py runs Playwright Chromium (pinned in tests/e2e/requirements.txt) with a CDP virtual WebAuthn authenticator against the full chain: Traefik → oauth2-proxy → Keycloak (LLDAP users, WebAuthn, X.509) → group-gate. A whoami test app has three hosts: app. (group users_e2e, /admin → admin_e2e, the default template Standard), hwk. (template any[security_key]) and mtls. (template any[yubikey_cert]). With no Hub in this job, the workflow writes policy file v6 and signin-keycloak.json itself; the latter's trust list is the CI fixture tests/e2e/fixtures/virtual-authenticators.json: Chromium's virtual CTAP2 authenticator (AAGUID 01020304-0506-0708-0102-030405060708, packed attestation with a self-signed "Batch Certificate", backup-eligible 0) as a security_key with that certificate as its root, so the virtual key registers as a security key (Keycloak's realm asks for direct attestation). The jobs that run the Hub (e2e-instances, e2e-signin, e2e-settings, e2e-folders, e2e-filesharing, e2e-ai) start it with HUB_DEV=1 and HUB_SIGNIN_EXTRA_AUTHENTICATORS=/run/portcullis/signin/extra-authenticators.json through their CI-only compose override, which mounts the same fixture read-only there (e2e-signin mounts a copy's directory instead, which its test rewrites) (contract §8.1 "Extra entries", development only), so their virtual keys are security keys too (Strong on hub / people). Every setup-link sign-in in them walks the step-up page with the shared passkey_flow helper of e2e_login.py; every caller states how many step-up pages it expects (one after a setup link, none for a later sign-in), and one more fails at once.

Scenarios:

No user has a password and nothing is pre-assigned in Keycloak: the job creates one-time setup links with ./portcullis invite <user> --to <landing> --json (for e2e, e2e-other, e2e-bypass and the bootstrap admin) and the test starts from them. Any password field fails the test.

  1. An unauthenticated request is redirected to a passkey-only Keycloak sign-in page: it offers the passkey (#authenticateWebAuthnButton), no password field, and isn't Keycloak's error page.
  2. The setup link → Register my key → passkey registration → group-gate's step-up page on hwk. (a setup-link session, amr inv, meets no template) asking for exactly security_key → Continue → one assertion of the new key → the app. Exactly one registration and one assertion; a needs-stronger page fails the test.
  3. The setup link works once.
  4. The session reaches the app.
  5. Apps get the username as X-Forwarded-User, and spoofed identity headers are dropped. A forged unsigned X-Forwarded-Access-Token / Authorization (amr hwk, mtls, the user's own name) never reaches the app, and on mtls. the real session still gets group-gate's step-up to yubikey_cert (a forged amr mtls reaching group-gate would show present-certificate instead).
  6. path_groups: /admin needs admin_e2e. /%61dmin, //admin, /x/../admin and /ADMIN are denied, while /administrator is allowed.
  7. A second login in a fresh browser with the same key is one passkey assertion.
  8. Group denial for a user not in users_e2e (also onboarded by setup link).
  9. The bootstrap admin's link lands on the portal (https://<domain>/) with the Hub link, after one step-up asking for any passkey (pc_method=passkey).
  10. An unused setup link, redeemed and then steered to another client's authorize endpoint with kc_idp_hint=portcullis-invite (client e2e-invite-bypass, created by the job), is denied by the invite post-broker flow: no code for the client, no passkey registered.
  11. A YubiKey-certificate login via Keycloak satisfies the YubiKey-certificate template.
  12. A YubiKey-certificate session without the certificate on the request is refused (certificate binding). The cert-only session opens a default-template app, and enroll's /self and /api/self/renew answer 404 for it (the cert-only renewal is e2e-signin's yubikey_cert_renew: this job runs no Hub).
  13. A revoked YubiKey certificate is rejected.
  14. A certificate from a foreign CA is rejected in the TLS handshake.

login_theme_brand: on the first Keycloak sign-in page the portcullis theme loads css/portcullis.css, the header's ::before shows portcullis-mark.svg, and the page's link[rel=icon] answers 200 with the pinned favicon.ico bytes.

tests/e2e/e2e_invite.py <setup-link> <landing-url> runs the setup-link checks (registration, no password, --expect-amr hwk in CI: the token's passkey method is exactly that one; the re-invite counts one step-up click and one passkey click; the step-up after the link with one more touch, a passkey method in the token's amr, single use, one-touch second login, the invite identity provider refuses browsers without a link) against any running install, e.g. a live server with a throwaway user (E2E_IGNORE_HTTPS_ERRORS=1 for ACME staging). With --reinvite-cmd "<command printing portcullis invite <same user> --json>" it also registers a second, new authenticator through a second link and checks that both keys sign in — or, with --replaced (--replace-keys), that the old one no longer does. With a spare key the step-up after the second link counts two assertion events for one touch: the account holds two passkeys, and Chromium silently probes a multi-entry allowCredentials list first (CDP reports that probe as an assertion too). The e2e job runs both variants after the browser tests (users e2e-spare, e2e-lost). Dialogs are answered like a user pressing OK (the default value).

After the browser tests, the job enables the monitoring profile and checks:

  • all monitoring services become healthy, and every Prometheus target is up
  • the Vault health probe and the enroll, forward-auth and forward-auth-ext (/ready: the session store answers) and LLDAP probes succeed
  • group-gate, CRL, backup (textfile), CA-expiry, Traefik and Vault metrics are present
  • the alert rules are loaded, and neither VaultSealedOrDown nor CrlStale is pending or firing
  • Grafana at metrics.<domain> redirects unauthenticated users to sign in, and rejects a forged identity header that doesn't come from Traefik's IP

On failure, screenshots, HTML, traces and service logs are uploaded as artifacts. The test needs a live stack and is not collected by pytest.

items.title: e2e-instances (app instances, extra domains)
items.text:
The whole stack plus the Hub, the domains service against Pebble with the fake DNS provider, and the added domain team-b.test (added on the domains API with the fake provider, which the Hub refuses; the Hub picks it up from the service's list). The Hub's only template source is the CI template tests/e2e/apps/echo (traefik/whoami behind Portcullis sign-in, plus a hold service that ignores SIGTERM so a backup can be made slow), seeded into hub_data as a local source. Through the Hub's API the job creates echo-a and echo-c on team-b.test and echo-b on the main domain (echo-c on a template the job creates, e2e-cert = any[yubikey_cert], picked with PUT /api/instances/echo-c/settings {sign_in_template}), checks the published policy file (v6, host keys, groups per instance, hosts for echo-c only, extra_domains), the rendered labels (portcullis-auth-ext and the /oauth2/ router to forward-auth-ext on extra-domain hosts only), the callbacks on portcullis-forward-auth and the SNI certificate. Every create carries a label ("Team A", …); a create without one is 400, and so is a host on a domain that isn't added. On echo-b the job checks the env overrides (contracts §11.9): a variable of the admin's own (PUT /api/instances/echo-b/env/CI_MARKER) is stored and listed as a custom row, a Hub variable (PORTCULLIS_INSTANCE) and a setting's variable (ECHO_STOP_GRACE) are refused with 400, the reset (DELETE) answers row: null, and the removed whole-file route /api/templates/env/<id> answers 404 / 405. Then tests/e2e/e2e_instances.py:

  • cross-domain SSO: signed in on the main domain, echo-a opens with no further WebAuthn assertion, through the host's own callback, PKCE S256 and a host-only __Host-portcullis_ext cookie; a stale ext cookie signs in again without a loop; echo-c steps up to the YubiKey certificate exactly once (pc_method=yubikey_cert on the host's own /oauth2/start; a returning user's passkey session, the YubiKey certificate available);
  • two instances, two groups: each user reaches only their instance;
  • a backup longer than 60 s through hub.<domain>: 202, a concurrent request 409, the op record ends ok (Traefik keeps its default timeouts);
  • domains_dns_panel: in Settings → Domains, the DNS button of team-b.test opens its DNS panel; every caa row's status is ok and the CAA line says "would issue: yes" (the e2e-instances domains override sets DNS_CAA_ISSUER=pebble.test).

Finally, on the real daemon: backup (the helper image pulled by digest, helpers removed), the typed-id delete (refusals first, then containers, volume and routing gone, the backup listed), restore into a new id (file and volume-root owners and modes kept, the new volume labelled for its project, the instance enables), and stop_enable_mid_pull: the CI template tests/e2e/apps/slowpull (GitLab CE's ~1.5 GB image, never cached on the runner) is enabled through the API, the test waits for step images to be running and POSTs the Stop (202), then waits for the record to end stopped. Assertions: no containers or volumes left, no Keycloak client slowpull, no groups users_slowpull / admin_slowpull, the instance disabled, and enable.stop in the audit. Poll helpers: Python e2e scripts use the shared module tests/e2e/e2e_ops.py; CI shell steps source tests/e2e/hubop.sh (shellchecked by the unit-tests job). Both poll each operation's own record every 2 s: the 202's poll, /api/instances/<id>/op?op_id=<op_id>, which the Hub keeps after a newer op (such as its own queued restart) has replaced the instance's current record. A poll that isn't of that form, or a record of another op, fails at once. On failure both print the record's error, hint, output and steps. Stop is sent with the enable's op_id. Folder and doctor ops poll their own records (/api/folders/<id>/op, /api/doctor/op), which have no history.

items.title: e2e-signin (sign-in methods)
items.text:
The whole stack plus the Hub and the Keycloak image (each built from its same-named branch) with one local template source: the CI templates tests/e2e/apps/echo (forward-auth) and tests/e2e/apps/oidc-echo (a native-OIDC client the Hub registers; traefik/whoami only answers the redirect URI — the test stops the browser there and redeems the code itself). The Hub's trust-list fixture is a copy of tests/e2e/fixtures/virtual-authenticators.json in /tmp/signin-fixture, whose directory the CI override mounts read-only at /run/portcullis/signin, so the test can rewrite the file in place. Through the Hub's API the job enables Basic and YubiKey + certificate, checks that browser_cert is off by default, switches it on, creates e2e-cert = any[yubikey_cert], e2e-file = any[browser_cert] and e2e-anycert = any[yubikey_cert, browser_cert], and the instances echo-std (the default, Standard), echo-basic (Basic), echo-cert (e2e-cert, protected@file), echo-file (e2e-file) and echo-anycert (e2e-anycert, both protected-any@file), oidc-strong (Strong), oidc-all (YubiKey + certificate) and oidc-cert (e2e-cert), and checks what it published: the picks in policy file v6, hub / people on Strong, and signin-keycloak.json clients (oidc-strong / oidc-all with their templates and names), the fixture's AAGUID, password off, browser_cert on. People (created with the Hub's LLDAP service account): root and sam (lldap_admin), alice, bob (a Vault certificate only), pat (a Hub-generated password only, kept in a 0600 file, never printed), rita and carol; root gets a certificate too. Setup links come from ./portcullis invite inside the test. The venv also gets cryptography (group-gate's pinned, hashed wheels) for the .p12, the CSRs and the CA checks; keys, certificates and .p12 passwords live only in a 0700 temp directory and in memory, and every password is ::add-mask::ed.

tests/e2e/e2e_signin.py uses two kinds of CDP virtual authenticator: backup eligibility 0 (Chromium's packed attestation, listed in the fixture: a security key) and backup eligibility 1 (a synced passkey, contract §8.1 "Passkey kinds"). An init script records the allowCredentials of every navigator.credentials.get, so "only that kind's credentials" is checked on what the browser was asked, not on Chromium's silent probe. Keycloak state is read from its admin API (credential types, brute-force status, sessions) and its log. Before the test, the job drifts the realm's passwordless passkey policy (conveyance none, attachment cross-platform) and keycloak configure must restore it (passkey_kinds_identified below needs the restored policy). In order:

  1. Password off: the cold sign-in offers the passkey only — no "Try another way", no password field —, also for a step-up with pc_method=password (the authorize request is checked to carry it).
  2. Reclassification, part 1: the fixture rewritten to {} (a directory change through the Hub — a throwaway group — makes it publish: signin-keycloak.json loses the virtual key's entry — the real FIDO MDS's entries stay — and gets a higher mds.serial); rita's setup-link key registers as webauthn-passwordless (passkey_synced, logged by the extension); the fixture is put back at once (written atomically: temp file + rename in the mounted directory). pc_fresh absent for her setup-link session: an authorization through portcullis-fresh-auth (PKCE S256, SSO reused, no touch of the key) has no pc_fresh.
  3. Security key on Strong: root's setup link → step-up pc_method=security_key → hub.<d> 200, amr hwk, credential type portcullis-security-key.
  4. Synced passkey refused on Strong: sam's synced key (webauthn-passwordless, amr spk): once the Hub's inventory lists people.sam = [passkey_synced], a later sign-in with it (one touch, amr without inv: a setup-link session counts as not known in people) gets #needs-stronger on hub.<d> (no step-up).
  5. Native-OIDC template enforced: sam on oidc-strong gets Keycloak's portcullis-needs-stronger.ftl ("OIDC echo · OIDC Strong needs a stronger sign-in") in core's portcullis theme, no code. The screenshot and HTML are uploaded on every run (artifact e2e-signin-needs-stronger).
  6. pc_method for one kind: sam's spare security key (a second setup link, landing on hub.<d>): the step-up asks security_key and the browser is asked for that key only, never the synced one.
  7. pc_method reaches Keycloak, amr accumulates: sam's synced session (from 4) on hub.<d>, with people.sam = [passkey_synced, security_key]: step-up pc_method=security_key; Keycloak shows the passkey prompt only (no "Try another way", no password field) and asks for the security key only; the token's amr then has spk and hwk.
  8. Cross-user certificate: alice signs up through a setup link (one step-up); her session is then exactly one small _oauth2_proxy ticket cookie, no _oauth2_proxy_0… (oauth2-proxy #3486: before the session store, this step-up looped). Her passkey session presenting bob's certificate, refused by Keycloak's X.509 user check or the extension's USER_CONFLICT (the log has the extension's line naming alice or a LOGIN_ERROR for bob's certificate with no user) — on echo-cert's yubikey_cert step-up (no code reaches oauth2-proxy) and on oidc-cert, a native-OIDC client on e2e-cert = any[yubikey_cert] where a switch to bob would meet the template: without pc_method Keycloak's needs-stronger page (the certificate isn't alice's, so the template step doesn't ask for it), with pc_method=yubikey_cert the refusal; no code either way. Bob has no Keycloak session, and the forward-auth session is never bob's.
  9. An all template met step by step: root with his certificate on oidc-all (all[yubikey_cert, security_key]): the certificate signs in, Keycloak asks for his security key itself (only it), then issues; the ID token's amr has mtls and hwk.
  10. pc_fresh present: root's fresh passkey sign-in on portcullis-fresh-auth (prompt=login, max_age=0) has pc_fresh = security_key; an SSO reuse right after has none. The hub core template governs admin confirmations: sam calls delete_group on a throwaway group through the Hub's MCP listener (:8890/mcp/admin, the gate secret read from secrets/mcp-gate/hub-secret, never printed); his fresh sign-in on portcullis-fresh-auth with redirect https://hub.<d>/ (the proof posted to /api/me/confirmations/<id> as the page does) with the synced passkey is refused (403 "a fresh sign-in is required"), with the security key approved; ai.confirm names template strong both times. The confirmation is never consumed.
  11. Password on: pat signs in with his password ("Try another way" → Password) on echo-basic (Basic; amr pwd); once the inventory lists people.pat = [password], people.<d> (Strong) answers #needs-stronger.
  12. Admin's password refused: admin with LLDAP's admin password, 11 times (above the realm's failure factor 10): "Password sign-in isn't available for this account" each time, Keycloak's brute-force status for admin shows 0 failures and not disabled, and admin's passkey still signs in.
  13. Password off again: as in 1.
  14. Reclassification, part 2: rita's credential type becomes portcullis-security-key, and the log's PasskeyReclassified user rita … passkey_synced -> security_key line (docker compose logs -t) is at most 360 s after the fixture's return (a new mtime → a higher mds.serial; the extension's task runs every 5 min, plus slack).
  15. Sign-in page, part 2 (browser_cert on since the job's setup):
    • browser_cert_on: the switch is on in GET /api/signin and signin-keycloak.json; echo-file / echo-anycert carry protected-any@file, echo-cert protected@file.
    • browser_cert_create_download: alice signs in on people.<d>/signin with her virtual security key, does a fresh sign-in (the popup flow, redirect https://people.<d>/signin), then POST https://people.<d>/api/me/signin/browser-certificates {days: 30} through Traefik: 200 with Cache-Control: no-store and Pragma: no-cache; the password is 4 × 5 Crockford characters; pkcs12.load_key_and_certificates(p12, password) gives an EC P-256 key and a leaf with CN alice, issued (and signed) by the browser CA, not_after ≈ now + 30 days; the .p12's chain holds the browser CA and the root (never the YubiKey CA); the filename and the row's serial match. The cert.create audit entries hold neither the password nor any base64 run. The policy file's people then lists browser_cert for alice.
    • browser_cert_fresh_refused_weak: sam's synced-passkey fresh sign-in (the people core template is Strong) gets 403 "a fresh sign-in is required"; nothing is created.
    • browser_cert_max_active: two more creates succeed and the fourth gets 409 (at most 3 active).
    • tls_protected_yubikey_ca_only: echo-cert (protected@file, the option mtls apps get): openssl s_client's "Acceptable client certificate CA names" is exactly the YubiKey CA — no root, no browser CA.
    • tls_mtls_refuses_browser_cert: curl to echo-cert with alice's browser leaf followed by the .p12's whole chain (pki_file + root, as a browser sends it) is refused in the handshake (curl exit 35 or 56, nothing else), while the same files complete it on echo-anycert; a Playwright context presenting the .p12 itself is refused too (its synthetic 503 "client-certificate error" page, Chromium's net::ERR_BAD_SSL_CLIENT_AUTH_CERT, or net::ERR_HTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR when the TLS 1.3 refusal reaches Playwright's TLS proxy after it already answered the browser with h2 — that one only with a real answer for the same .p12 from echo-anycert in the same context; any other error fails); root's YubiKey certificate completes the handshake.
    • tls_protected_any: echo-anycert's CA names are the root and both CAs; the browser certificate (with its chain) completes the handshake, no certificate fails it.
    • browser_cert_signin_file: a new context with the .p12 as its client_certificates and no authenticator: alice signs in with the certificate only and echo-file (any[browser_cert]) opens; the token's amr has file and never mtls; Keycloak's LOGIN events have pc_methods browser_cert (never yubikey_cert) and its log names no mtls / yubikey_cert for her.
    • browser_cert_not_yubikey: that session on oidc-cert (any[yubikey_cert]) gets Keycloak's needs-stronger page; with pc_method=yubikey_cert it signs nobody in (no code). A forward-auth any[yubikey_cert] host is protected@file, so there the handshake refuses the browser certificate (above).
    • browser_cert_cannot_renew: the browser certificate presented on POST /api/me/signin/yubikey-certificate/renew with a CSR for its key gets 403 "present your current YubiKey certificate"; nothing is issued.
    • browser_cert_off_counts_nothing: echo-file off e2e-file, e2e-file disabled, browser_cert switched off (both published files without it; echo-anycert on protected@file, since the switch drops browser_cert from every compiled rule and e2e-anycert becomes any[yubikey_cert]; echo-file, on the default Standard meanwhile, on authaware@file): on echo-file the same valid .p12 alone leaves the browser on Keycloak's passkey prompt with no LOGIN event, and alice's earlier file session gets 403. Everything is switched back in a finally (echo-file / echo-anycert back on protected-any@file).
    • yubikey_cert_still_mtls: a pki_int certificate CI issues for alice through Vault signs her in without an authenticator: amr mtls, never file; echo-cert opens.
    • yubikey_cert_renew (the cert-only renewal, moved here from e2e: enroll's /self is gone and the e2e job runs no Hub): that session renews on the Sign-in page — POST https://people.<d>/api/me/signin/yubikey-certificate/renew with a CSR for the same key → 200 no-store, CN alice, the YubiKey CA, the same key, a new serial.
    • forged_cert_headers: Traefik deletes client-sent X-Forwarded-Tls-Client-Cert / -Info: alice's mtls session without the certificate but with both headers forged (her real YubiKey certificate) stays on #present-certificate on people.<d>/, and a renewal from her passkey session with them forged gets 403; the same header sent straight to the Hub's people listener (:8889, no Traefik) renews (200), so the 403 is Traefik deleting it.
    • browser_cert_revoked: DELETE /api/me/signin/certificates/<serial> (through Traefik, with that certificate) → 204; within 70 s echo-file answers 403 (revoked) and GET /api/me/signin shows it revoked; a YubiKey certificate's serial on that route is 404; she revokes her third one too.
    • signin_page_reachable_weak: password on, pat (a password only — bob has a YubiKey certificate, so people.<d> would offer him a step-up) signs in with a wrong password once, then his own: /signin and /api/me/signin answer 200; /api/directory gets #needs-stronger; raw, unnormalised paths sent with http.client (the path written as is: /signin/../api/directory, /api/me/signin/../../directory, /static/../api/directory → 403 #needs-stronger; encoded dots, slashes and backslashes → refused, 400 / 403 / 404, never the Hub). Password off again after.
    • sign_in_help_actions: group hr with carol, PUT /api/directory/permissions/sign_in_help {group: "hr"}; carol's view of alice's Sign-in tab may send a setup link, remove passkeys and revoke, not set a password or issue; she sends alice a setup link (200, masked), removes her passkeys (200, gone from Keycloak) and revokes her second browser certificate (204); she gets 403 for alice's password and for every action on root, portcullis-hub and herself (also revoking root's certificate); as an admin, issuing and revoking root's certificate get 409 "… managed from the server". The audit has user.invite, user.remove_passkeys and cert.revoke with as sign_in_help.
    • browser_cert_none_left: all three revoked, none active, and the policy file's people no longer lists browser_cert for alice.
    • history_entries: alice's /api/me/signin/history (no unknown source) has her setup-link sign_in (no methods, detail "Setup link used"), a sign_in with methods [browser_cert] and a non-empty browser, a step_up, an opened for echo-file with browser_cert, at least three help entries by carol and at least three certificate entries, and no .p12 password; pat's has a failed entry (his wrong password); carol may read alice's history.
    • cert_and_password_kinds_identified: Keycloak's LOGIN pc_methods name yubikey_cert and browser_cert for alice's certificate sign-ins and password for pat's; /api/me/signin lists alice's yubikey_cert and pat's password (and nothing else for pat).
    • enroll_site_gone: https://enroll.<d>/, /self, /api/self/renew, /api/sign, /api/users, /users and /certs get Traefik's own 404 (no router), while /invite/<bad token> reaches enroll's invite page ("This setup link is invalid, expired or already used", 404).

  16. TLS follows the switches (last; it restarts apps): with both certificate methods on, echo-std and echo-basic are on authaware@file and openssl s_client -servername <host> shows "Acceptable client certificate CA names". Standard saved as any[family:passkey], the instances off the certificate templates, hub / people on standard, Strong, YubiKey + certificate, e2e-cert, e2e-file and e2e-anycert disabled → echo-std on public@file with no CA names; echo-basic (Basic still names family:certificate) stays on authaware@file while browser_cert alone is on — checked on six samples over 30 s once the Hub has applied yubikey_cert off (both published files without it, the Hub's own tier for echo-basic authaware@file, no echo-basic op running) — and moves only when both yubikey_cert and browser_cert are switched off. auth.<d> and hub.<d> keep their CA names (core routers stay on authaware). Then everything is put back (in a finally, also when a step failed) and compared with the snapshot taken before (methods, templates and rules, default, core pages, instance picks), and both apps are back on authaware@file with CA names.

  17. Signing in as someone else (the job's .env sets IMPERSONATION_MAX_MINUTES=2, for every case). Each case starts with root's fresh sign-in with his security key, then POSTs the start route on the Hub listener; every case stops its own impersonation within 2 minutes, except imp_expiry and the 125 s case of imp_next_bound, which run last among them, in parallel browser contexts. sam is the second administrator.

    • imp_start: root's YubiKey-certificate session; his fresh security-key sign-in leaves only hwk in the session, so he steps up to yubikey_cert before the start. Reason "checking quota", then next: root's browser lands on the portal as alice; the token has preferred_username alice, act.sub root, pc_imp.id = the id and root's amr (mtls, hwk); root has no Keycloak session left and alice has one, with the impersonator.
    • imp_banner_everywhere: You are signed in as alice (by root) · reason “checking quota” · … min left with a Stop control on the portal, on people.<d>'s My apps and /signin (after impersonation.js ran), on a group-gate needs-stronger page and on the extension's page.
    • imp_call5: an app on e2e-cert opens only while root's YubiKey certificate is presented; with alice's certificate it shows the impersonation needs page with no X-Stepup-URL. An app on Strong opens although alice's own methods don't meet Strong.
    • imp_people_read_only: PUT /api/me/signin/password, POST /api/me/signin/browser-certificates and DELETE /api/me/ai/connections/x get 403 "not while you are signed in as someone else: Stop first"; GET /api/me/apps is 200.
    • imp_signin_page_read_only: the impersonating browser's /signin says "Changes are off while root is signed in as you." and offers no action (no [data-msi-act] element).
    • imp_ai_refused: the CI AI client's authorize in this browser shows #impersonating and issues no code; a token minted for alice before the start still works through mcpclient.
    • imp_refused_concurrent: root's second start → 409 "Stop it first"; sam on alice → 409 "root is signed in as alice right now".
    • imp_stop: Stop on the portal → the Stop page POSTs, the browser goes through /oauth2/sign_out, then to the sign-in page, or, since the browser presents root's YubiKey certificate, to the portal as root with no act / pc_imp; within 20 s alice has no impersonated Keycloak session; the old _oauth2_proxy cookie replayed on the app never gets 200; oidc-strong's refresh token is then invalid_grant; the audit has impersonation.start with the reason and impersonation.end "stopped" with the apps opened; alice's history has the impersonation entry by root with the reason and the apps.
    • imp_stop_elsewhere: sam's stop_impersonation (Hub MCP) ends it; root's browser gets group-gate's ended page within 5 s.
    • imp_notice_next_signin: after imp_stop, alice signs in herself in a new context: the notice reads "root signed in as you on … UTC for … min: checking quota.", Continue reaches her app, and her next sign-in shows no notice.
    • imp_refused_proofs: sam's synced-passkey proof, root's browser-certificate proof and bob's proof → 403; reason "ab" → 400. (The password case is the Hub's unit test: root has no password.)
    • imp_refused_targets: root himself, sam (an administrator), portcullis-hub and admin → 409; a sign_in_help holder as the caller → 403; the switch off → 409, and a running impersonation ends.
    • imp_next_bound: next opened in bob's signed-in context → 403 page and bob's session intact; opened again in root's context after a successful use → 403; a fresh start's next opened after 125 s → 403. Each time alice gets no session.
    • imp_expiry: after 2 min 10 s a request gets group-gate's ended page, the extension's ended page or Keycloak's sign-in page (never anything as alice), within a further 20 s Keycloak has no impersonated session, and the audit has "expired" by portcullis.
    • imp_stock_endpoint_off: Keycloak's own admin impersonation endpoint answers non-2xx.

    After these, before 16, passkey_kinds_identified: the realm's passwordless policy is the restored one, and a security key (rita, after invite --replace-keys), a synced passkey (bob) and a device-bound one (pat; the fixture kind passkey_device) are each identified by kind: credential type, log kind and AAGUID, the /api/me/signin row, the amr and LOGIN pc_methods.

Also in e2e_signin.py:

  • stepup_returns_to_page: sam's synced session opens https://hub.<d>/?from=stepup#x (Strong); the step-up page's Continue has rd = https://hub.<d>/?from=stepup, and after the security-key touch the browser is back on that page.
  • passkey_rename: sam renames his security key through PUT /api/me/signin/passkeys/<id>/label "CI key" → 204, and Keycloak's credential has userLabel "CI key"; his synced passkey renamed "ci KEY" → 409; root's credential id → 404; the audit has signin.passkey.label with a detail ending → CI key.

tests/e2e/e2e_signin.py's and e2e_filesharing.py's fresh sign-ins on people.<domain> use the redirect https://people.<d>/signin.

The throwaway ci-kick-<n> groups are deleted at the end (best effort). ./portcullis signin reset-core is covered by build-and-test (above). The setup link landing on the step-up page is e2e scenario 2. Failure artifacts: screenshots, HTML and service logs; no Playwright traces (a DOM snapshot would carry a typed password), the password pages are captured before anything is typed, and no whoami page is captured (it echoes session cookies and bearer tokens). Setup links are masked in the log (::add-mask::) and redacted from failure messages; the screenshots / HTML of the setup pages show the consumed links (nothing reusable).

items.title: e2e-settings (app settings panel)
items.text:
The whole stack plus the Hub (built from the same-named Hub branch, like e2e-instances) with one local template source: the templates repo's immich, grafana, nextcloud and firefox-sync (from the same-named templates branch, else main) and two CI fixtures, tests/e2e/apps/settings-echo (traefik/whoami with a per-person option delivered as the header X-Forwarded-Attr-Tier) and settings-file (per-person options in a data file people.json, restart on membership changes, and a hook that stores every input it gets). A Traefik alias override puts auth.<domain> and the app hosts on portcullis-proxy, so Immich and Nextcloud reach Keycloak as they would through public DNS. Users are created in LLDAP; groups, memberships, enables and settings go through the Hub's API, the way an admin makes them. Then tests/e2e/e2e_settings.py runs 19 checks in a real browser with virtual passkeys:

  • Sign-in: alice, bob and carol follow their setup links, register a passkey and reach the portal.
  • Claims (Immich): alice (in office_milan, row 10 GiB) has quotaSizeInBytes 10 GiB in /api/users/me and in Immich's UI; bob (in admin_immich, the template's preset row) is an Immich admin with the 100 GiB default.
  • Headers: bob is a Grafana org Admin on his first and later requests, alice a Viewer; settings-echo receives alice's gold and bob's bronze tier, and never another host's header.
  • Data file: people.json inside the settings-file container lists only the people with access.
  • Person-entered values (Firefox Sync): alice enters her Mozilla account uid on people.<domain> (200); bob's identical uid is refused with 409 and the answer doesn't name alice; carol, outside the access group, gets
  • After the debounce, allowlist.json in firefox-sync-init lists only alice's uid, the init ran once, and on the real Postgres her uid gets a tokenserver row while an unlisted one is refused.
  • Membership changes: one batch through the Hub (alice leaves office_milan and joins admin_immich, bob leaves admin_grafana, three people join users_settings-file). Both removals end the person's Keycloak session (the Hub signs removed members out), so alice and bob must sign in again, and any other sign-in prompt fails the test. Then: alice's next Immich sign-in has the 100 GiB default and admin rights (a role changed on an existing account), her tier is bronze, bob is a Grafana Viewer, people.json lists four people, settings-file restarted exactly once for the three joins (counted from a live docker events stream), and the hook got the full state with trigger membership_change.
  • My apps: carol's /api/me/apps lists only settings-file with her values and no other username; /api/instances/immich/settings on people.<domain> is 404.
  • Leave and rejoin: alice leaves users_firefox-sync: the file no longer lists her, her tokenserver rows are deleted and nobody can sync (an empty allowlist lets nobody in); she rejoins and syncs again.
  • Custom fields with _: a field cost_center (LLDAP attribute cost-center) set on alice shows in the overview, fills a rule group cost_center = "CC-42", reaches settings-echo as X-Forwarded-Attr-Cost-Center and Keycloak's example access token for Immich's client as attr_cost_center.
  • Hooks (Nextcloud): the first install applied the default quota through the start hook (occ config:app:get files default_quota is 10 GB).

Timing bounds come from the Hub: a membership delivery arrives within one 60 s debounce window plus the evaluator's minute and slack. Secrets reach the test only through the environment or curl -H @<(…), never on argv. Failure artifacts hold the settings panels (secrets are write-only), the policy and attributes files, the data files (never *.secrets.json), container logs, screenshots and traces. The traces start after the setup-link sign-in; the setup pages' screenshots still show the (consumed) setup links, and traces carry session cookies of the throwaway stack.

items.title: e2e-folders (shared folders and the doctor)
items.text:
Built like e2e-settings (the same-named templates and Hub branches, else main; the Traefik alias override; the Hub's data seeded with one local source): the templates repo's jellyfin (the step fails if it has no folder block) and the CI fixture tests/e2e/apps/folder-writer (alpine as user: "2001:2001" with umask 022, a read-only root filesystem and no capabilities; its option shared has folder: {access: write, runs_as: {uid: 2001, gid: 2001}}; it writes a new file into /shared at every start and has a lan_only TCP port WRITER_PORT, default 18765). Before the stack starts, the job installs acl, checks that /srv is ext4 and takes ACLs, and builds /srv/e2e-media: 6 directories 0750 and 50 files 0640, all 1000:1000.

tests/e2e/e2e_folders.py (Python standard library only, no browser) drives the Hub's admin API, sudo find / getfacl and docker through 14 scenarios, every count exact:

Scenario Checks tree 50 files and 6 directories as built, no ACLs enable jellyfin and folder-writer enable; the writer can't write yet and created no file check Check path's summary is exactly exists · ext4 · ACLs and xattrs supported · 50 files · owners 1000:1000 (all) create folder media gets gid 60000, not adopted preview the preview's lines (gid allocated, "50 files and 6 folders change group 1000 → 60000", group 1000 keeps its access through an ACL on 56 entries, both apps stopped for under a minute); nothing changed on disk apply the operation succeeds: 56 entries, a snapshot, 2 uses added host verify every entry has gid 60000 and its old owner; directories 2770 with group:1000:r-x in the access ACL and a default ACL of group::rwx, mask::rwx, other::--- and no entry for group 1000; files 0660 with group:1000:r-- writer file the writer's new file is 2001:60000, mode 660 despite umask 022 jellyfin its process has gid 60000, lists the library, and can't write (read-only file system) no drift a disk check newer than the request finds no folder_owner finding drift after a chgrp 1000 of the writer's file, exactly one folder_owner Warning offering reapply_folder and undo_folder undo the preview says 56 entries go back, 0 changed since; after the undo every original entry has its exact original owner, group and mode and no ACL, and the folder has nothing left to undo exposure WRITER_PORT on 0.0.0.0 is one lan_only_exposed Warning; Rebind… to 127.0.0.1 leaves docker port showing only 127.0.0.1:18765, and the finding is gone proxy the Hub's socket proxy is unchanged from main, the Hub has no Docker socket, and no fixer helper container is left

A scenario that builds on a failed one fails too. On failure the job uploads e2e-folders-artifacts: logs, API answers, the tree and getfacl -R, the Hub's folder data, snapshots and the doctor cache.

items.title: e2e-filesharing (file-share passwords, SMB3 hardening, revocation)
items.text:
tests/e2e/e2e_filesharing.py (Playwright, smbclient 4.19.5) provisions a stack with Samba and Time Machine instances, tests per-person credential creation (a fresh sign-in the app's template accepts — a passkey, or a password under a password-only template —, the password shown once), SMB3 connections with encryption required, revocation latencies (hub-made removal, LLDAP-direct removal, writer demoted to reader), instance and core restores voiding credentials, that no hash appears in any backup or log, and the F58 capability ruling (smbd signals work without CAP_KILL). Scenarios:

  • Setup: connect_address, ports on 127.0.0.1, size_limit 500GiB / office_milan 10GiB, folder slot via assignment, readers / writers before enable, testparm hardening.
  • Sign-in via setup links (alice, bob, carol); fresh auth popup flow (COOP, the authorize parameters, the password once, replay refused).
  • SMB3 sessions: Time Machine and Samba list shares, carol writes as 21002:60000, encryption required, SMB2/NTLMv1/guest/wrong password refused, outside-LAN client refused.
  • Revocation: hub-made ≤ 10 s, LLDAP-direct ≤ 75 s, writer demoted ≤ 4 s (session gone, login refused). Measured at 0.8–0.9 s, 3.4–51.8 s, and about 3.6 s.
  • Restore: instance restore → credential voided, card says "reset by a restore", re-create works. Core restore → no hash in 45 backup files, hub_secrets emptied, credentials voided, uid pool +1000, Samba restarted from Hub.
  • Governing template: dave (users_samba, a Hub-set password only), with password on, signs in on portcullis-fresh-auth with his password (prompt=login, max_age=0) and the proof is posted to the people listener: refused (403) while the default (Samba takes no pick) is Standard, accepted once the default is a password-only template (credential.create audited with template=e2e-pw); his share then works. The default, the template and the password switch are restored in a finally.
  • No hash visible: docker inspect, container logs, hub_data, audit, ops, archives, state.yaml.

Built like e2e-settings (same-named Hub and templates branches, else main). Ubuntu 24.04 runners, smbclient pinned at 2:4.19.5+dfsg-4ubuntu9*. On failure: policy/attributes files, data files, container logs, screenshots, no traces (DOM snapshots would carry the password).

items.title: e2e-ai (AI support through mcp-gate)
items.text:
The first run of the whole chain: an MCP client on the runner host → Traefik → mcp-gate → the Gitea companion (the official gitea-mcp, from the templates repo) → Gitea, with Keycloak's OAuth (PKCE and resource, the Hub's portcullis-ai-claude-code client and its mcp:* scopes) and the Hub (AI settings, the companion switch, the gate files, lazy mint and revoke hooks). The Hub's template source is the same-named templates branch (else main) with gitea, grafana and the CI echo fixture; the CI fixtures declare ai.unsupported. Setup goes through the Hub's admin API as the CI admin root: instances gitea-b and a throwaway echo-del, gitea, gitea-b and grafana enabled, alice / bob / carol in their groups, the master switch on with Claude Code offered (admin flag on), Gitea's companion in read_write, Grafana's (identity headers) read-only.

tests/e2e/mcpclient is a stand-in for Claude Code on the official MCP Go SDK (pinned in its go.mod):

  • mcpclient login --client-id <id> --callback-port 33418 --resource <url> [--scope "<scopes>"] --token-file <f> [--ca-file <pem>] [--timeout 5m] prints the authorize URL (Playwright opens it, signs in with a CDP virtual authenticator and consents), serves the loopback callback and writes the token to the file (0600; tokens are never printed or put on argv);
  • mcpclient call --url <url> --token-file <f> --method tools/list|tools/call [--tool <name> --args <json>] [--protocol <version>] [--elicitation url [--elicit-answer accept|decline|cancel]] [--ca-file <pem>] prints one JSON document (the result, the negotiated protocol and any elicitation/create requests, or the HTTP status and WWW-Authenticate). --elicitation url declares URL-mode elicitation only and turns off the SDK's automatic retry, so a 2026-07-28 input_required is printed as sent.

tests/e2e/e2e_ai.py scenarios:

  1. gitea_as_alice: a token for https://gitea.<d>/mcp, tools/list, and a repository listing that shows only alice's repositories.
  2. leaver_refused_and_revoked: alice removed from users_gitea → 403, and her portcullis-ai-* Gitea token deleted.
  3. audience_separation: her Gitea token at gitea-b, mcp.<d>, hub.<d> and people.<d> → 401; one token for two resources (both audiences asserted; Keycloak not minting it fails the scenario) → refused at both.
  4. no_token_crossing: the MCP token on Gitea's and the people pages → a sign-in redirect or 401, never a page; browser cookies on /mcp → 401. This proves the apps refuse the MCP token; that the gate never forwards it rests on mcp-gate's unit tests.
  5. destructive_confirmation: root's delete_instance on hub.<d>/mcp → the confirmation link; bob can't open it; root types the id and touches a fresh passkey → approved; the retry runs, a second one needs a new confirmation; audited via: ai with the client and the confirmation id.
  6. aggregate_lists: on mcp.<d> carol sees gitea__*, grafana__* and portcullis__my_apps and calls Grafana through the gate (identity headers); bob sees no grafana__*; root sees no admin tool.
  7. ai_off: the master switch off → every resource 503. While the apps restart, a companion host answers 404 (its router is gone with the app), which fails closed too.
  8. companion_confirmation: alice's label_write delete_repo_label → a people.<d> confirmation (typed check: the instance label); bob 404; approved → runs once with the canonical arguments; changed arguments → a new one; the access log's confirmation_id.
  9. url_elicitation_2026: with URL elicitation declared, a 2026-07-28 call gets input_required (a Hub D tool and a companion tool); a 2025-11-25 session gets the gate's elicitation/create (mode url) and the Hub's text.
  10. gitea_isolation: the gitea-internal and companion alias resolution, no portcullis-hook-* token left after mint and revoke, the switch-on's revoke_all succeeded.
  11. companion_alias_guard: ./portcullis status shows no name takeover for the real Gitea and Grafana companions; a container outside the instance's project answering to portcullis-mcp-gitea--gitea is flagged, and the real one with it as sharing the name.

Not covered: an approved 2026-07-28 round trip through requestState, the gate's continuation of a confirmed call the companion then asks input for, and token refresh. Built like e2e-settings (same-named Hub and templates branches, else main). Tokens live only in a temp directory outside the artifacts. On failure: logs, screenshots and traces.

e2e-instances runs on ubuntu-latest: the echo fixture's hold service has its own pinned busybox image, so the Hub's helper image isn't in use when the job removes it (Docker's containerd image store refuses to remove an image in use).

Cross-repo branches. ci.yml also runs on workflow_dispatch. On a branch whose name exists in porelli/portcullis-hub (not main, not a tag), .github/actions/hub-image builds the Hub from that branch instead of pulling edge. Likewise, on a branch whose name exists in porelli/portcullis-keycloak (not main, not a tag), .github/actions/keycloak-image builds the Keycloak image from it (KEYCLOAK_IMAGE=portcullis-keycloak:ci, KEYCLOAK_LOCAL=1); otherwise it pulls the published edge and names its digest in the step summary. Every job that runs Keycloak uses it, and the cached image lists leave both images out (unpinned). The Hub's build.yml likewise tests against the same-named branch of the templates and core repos, else main.

Running some jobs only. workflow_dispatch has an input jobs (default all): all, or job names separated by commas and/or spaces — unit-tests, build-and-test, e2e, e2e-instances, e2e-signin, e2e-settings, e2e-folders, e2e-filesharing, e2e-ai. The names match exactly (e2e doesn't run e2e-ai); the other jobs are skipped. Every job needs the first job, jobs-input, which fails the run on an unknown name (or all together with names); any subset of the other jobs runs. Push, pull request and workflow_call always run every job (release.yml passes no jobs; the called workflow's default is all).

gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <branch> -R porelli/portcullis -f jobs=build-and-test
gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <branch> -R porelli/portcullis -f jobs="e2e-signin e2e-settings"

Timeouts. Every job has timeout-minutes (about 1.5× its longest green run, at least 20: 20 for most, e2e-signin 40, e2e-settings 30), and so do the slow steps: image loads and local builds 15, the Hub / Keycloak image 20, Playwright installs 10, artifact uploads 10, backup / restore steps 15. A step that runs out fails instead of hanging. The build-push action's build-summary / build-record uploads are off (DOCKER_BUILD_SUMMARY, DOCKER_BUILD_RECORD_UPLOAD false): nothing reads them, and a failing artifact service once kept a finished e2e-settings job retrying them for over 30 minutes.

items.title: e2e-podman (rootless Podman)
items.text:
The whole stack under rootless Podman on ubuntu-26.04, with the runner user as the operator (Rootless Podman). No artifact carries .env, secrets/ or a backup.

  • Docker phase (while Docker still runs): init --runtime docker with the CI override, one LLDAP person created, ./portcullis backup copied aside (mode 0700), the sha256 of certs/ca-chain.crt recorded, then down and everything removed (volumes, .env, secrets/, certs/).
  • Setup. The local, Hub and Keycloak images are built and moved into Podman (docker save | podman load). Docker is stopped and disabled, and the job checks its socket no longer answers. Then podman, passt and uidmap are installed, the runner gets 65536 subuids and subgids, ip_unprivileged_port_start is set to 80, lingering is on and the user podman.socket and podman-restart.service are enabled, and ACME_STAGING=true ./portcullis init --runtime podman runs with the CI override. The Hub's local template sources hold echo, folder-writer and scrutiny; /srv/e2e-pod is operator-owned with one root-owned child.
  • Checks, each failing with FAIL: <what>:
    • status --json has no problems, runtime.name is podman and runtime.port_start is at most 80
    • every pinned network's subnet and range round-trip as in .env, and Traefik, Keycloak, the Hub and mcp-gate sit at their pinned addresses
    • every core container has a memory and a pids limit
    • the socket checks of build-and-test, the Podman API denials included
    • Traefik's Docker provider lists the hub@docker and people@docker routers
    • secrets/hub/core.env is the operator's on the host and 0:10001 inside the namespace (podman unshare stat)
    • the mTLS sign-in and the portal, as in build-and-test
    • forward-auth reaches auth.<domain> through host-gateway
    • tests/e2e/e2e_podman.py: /api/runtime says podman, verified, with the runner's uid as container 0's host id; an echo instance goes through create, enable, disable, backup and restore; the fixer applies on the operator-owned /srv/e2e-pod and refuses the root-owned child with is owned by a host account outside Portcullis' id range and its path; creating scrutiny answers 409 naming SYS_RAWIO
    • Rebuild and recreate. After an up that rebuilds enroll, the running container uses the new image, and unchanged services aren't recreated
    • The VPN service (.github/ci/e2e-podman-vpn-service-on-rootless-podman.sh): vpn init rootless, wg as 10006 without capabilities, vpn add-device for an LLDAP person, a tests/e2e/vpn-client handshake over the published UDP port and a GET of people.<domain> through the edge and vpnsecure (forward-auth's redirect). The host prep writes the operator's containers.conf pool line, and the job checks a new network lands in 10.89.0.0/16
    • reboot: after systemctl restart user@<uid>.service (every container dies with the user manager), podman-restart.service brings the stack back and status is clean within 180 s
    • Docker → Podman round trip: after a wipe, init --runtime podman and ./portcullis restore --yes of the Docker phase's backup: .env keeps CONTAINER_RUNTIME=podman and the rootless socket, status is clean, certs/ca-chain.crt has the recorded sha256, the Docker phase's LLDAP person exists, and the secrets are the operator's on the host
  • On failure it uploads the container logs only.

items.title: e2e-vpn (VPN-only access)
items.text:
The whole stack with the VPN service (COMPOSE_PROFILES=wg, ./portcullis vpn init, ACME_STAGING=true, 45 min), the Hub (same-named Hub branch) with one local template source: the CI template echo (instance echo-vpn, VPN-only) and the templates repo's headscale (same-named templates branch, else main; the job fails without its vpn: block), wired as a provider with a 15 s refresh. A CoreDNS stub is the built-in resolver's upstream. Clients have no privileges: tests/e2e/vpn-client (a Go WireGuard client on the same wireguard-go / gVisor / miekg/dns pins, through a netstack tunnel, one JSON line per call) for the built-in VPN, and userspace tailscaled containers for the tailnet. tests/e2e/e2e_vpn.py (Playwright for setup links, the /vpn/ fresh sign-in and Headscale's OIDC registration) runs these cases, each failing with FAIL: <what>:

Case Checks websecure_vpn_required echo-vpn on websecure answers only /vpn-required builtin_signin_demanded alice's built-in device without a session: redirected to sign in builtin_opens alice's device with alice's session opens echo-vpn builtin_not_yours bob's device (made with the host CLI) with alice's session: "this device isn't yours" builtin_dns the built-in resolver: echo-vpn.<d> A 10.213.0.1, AAAA no data, no AD tailnet_register a tailscaled node registered as alice through Keycloak tailnet_opens, tailnet_dns through the Headscale gateway with alice's session; MagicDNS points echo-vpn.<d> at the gateway via_builtin Through only the built-in VPN: the tailnet device 403, the built-in one opens tailnet_local_denied a node of a local (non-OIDC) Headscale user never opens gateway_claims_builtin, gateway_wrong_source, gateway_wrong_port a gateway claiming a built-in address is closed (outside_ranges); a valid header from another address is closed (wrong_gateway); nothing listens on other edge ports valid_until_expired the Hub stopped and vpn.json past its valid_until: open connections closed, no new ones builtin_revoked bob's device revoked: an open connection closed, the handshake fails within 5 s tailnet_node_deleted alice's node deleted in Headscale: an open connection closed, denied within refresh + 10 s gateway_stopped, identity_hook_broken, wg_stopped only that path fails; once stale the tailnet is denied and the built-in VPN isn't; with wg down echo-vpn is unreachable on both paths, never on the internet server_mode vpn mode server --force: on websecure only the public set answers; vpn mode apps with wg stopped restores everything

Keys, configurations and cookies live only in a 0700 temp directory; setup links are masked and there are no Playwright traces. The artifacts are logs and wg's status, never vpn.json's keys, .env, secrets/ or configurations.

items.title: Caching
items.text:
Core CI caches what it safely can. Caches are written only on pushes to main.

  • Infra and monitoring images: cached by the local composite action .github/actions/cached-images.
    • The cache key is a hash of each job's pinned image list. Refs without a digest are refused.
    • After docker load, every name set by the tarball is removed. Each ref is then re-pulled by its pinned digest (with retry and backoff), so the engine reuses a loaded image only if its content-addressed ID matches the registry's config digest.
  • enroll and group-gate images: buildx layer cache (type=gha).
  • Go: module and build cache through setup-go, with go mod verify.
  • Python: pip and Playwright browsers, cached on the pinned requirements file (group-gate/requirements.txt has --require-hashes).

The revocation check waits up to 180s, because Vault rebuilds delta CRLs at most once a minute.

items.title: Releases (release.yml)
items.text:
Runs on v* tags:

  1. preflight checks three things:
    • The tag is vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH and CHANGELOG.md has its ## [X.Y.Z] section.
    • The HUB_IMAGE default in docker-compose.yml is ghcr.io/porelli/portcullis-hub:A.B.C@sha256:…, where vA.B.C is a published (non-draft, non-prerelease) Hub release and the tag still resolves to that digest.
    • The KEYCLOAK_IMAGE default is ghcr.io/porelli/portcullis-keycloak:D.E.F@sha256:… in the same way (a published portcullis-keycloak release whose tag still resolves to that digest).
  2. ci runs the full ci.yml on the tagged commit.
  3. release builds a reproducible portcullis-X.Y.Z.tar.gz (the checkout without .git, plus VERSION) and its .sha256. It then creates the GitHub release with the changelog section, the pinned Hub and Keycloak images and generated notes.

See Upgrading & Releases.

items.title: Dependabot
items.text:
.github/dependabot.yml proposes weekly, grouped updates for:

  • the compose images
  • the enroll Dockerfile and Go modules
  • the GitHub Actions
  • the e2e Python requirements

Image constants in the CLI and inline images in workflows are not covered by Dependabot. They are still checked by the pin-enforcement step.

items.title: Auto-merge
items.text:
Core, the Hub and the templates share one auto-merge workflow, .github/workflows/dependabot-automerge.yml. Its logic lives in .github/automerge/automerge.sh, which is identical in all three repos and tested by .github/automerge/test.sh. The workflow runs after the required workflows finish on a Dependabot PR and never checks out PR code:

  • Patch, minor and digest-only updates are squash-merged once every required workflow passed on the PR's head commit. The PR must be Dependabot's own single, GitHub-signed commit.
  • Majors (or updates of unknown type) get the major-update label and stay open.
  • Pre-releases are closed.
  • Red CI opens an update-failed issue.

A merge that fails although CI passed gets at most one re-attempt. Only GitHub's "Base branch was modified" error is re-attempted. It happens when another PR merged at the same moment. The workflow waits about 10 seconds, then tries the merge once more at the same tested commit. Anything else, such as an HTTP 5xx, is not retried. If the merge still fails, the run fails and its error names the cause and the command to retry by hand:

gh workflow run dependabot-automerge.yml -f pr=<n> -f dry_run=false

Run it from a checkout of the repo, or add -R porelli/<repo>. Check the PR first: a 5xx can still have merged it. Leave out -f dry_run=false to see the decision without acting on it.

The workflow doesn't ask Dependabot to rebase. Dependabot ignores @dependabot rebase comments posted with the workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN (or by any GitHub App) and replies "only users with push access can use that command".

items.title: Running the core tests locally
items.text:
python3 tests/test_group_gate.py   # in a venv with group-gate/requirements.txt
python3 tests/test_e2e_fsops.py
bash tests/test_cli.sh
bash tests/test_shell_libs.sh
(cd enroll && go test ./...)
(cd mcp-gate && go vet ./... && go test -race ./...)
shellcheck -S warning portcullis scripts/lib/*.sh tests/*.sh tests/e2e/*.sh
# compose validity without Docker containers:
PORTCULLIS_ROOT=/tmp/x ./portcullis init --env-only --non-interactive --domain ci.example.org --dns-provider none

items.title: lint.yml: every push and PR, forks included
items.text:
No secrets, no core checkout, read-only token. Safe for fork pull requests, so every contributor gets this feedback:

  • python tests/validate.py: the manifest schema plus repo rules (networks, volumes, middlewares, required vars, mounts, image pinning, header trust, Dependabot coverage, .core-ref). See Manifest Reference → Validation.
  • bash tests/compose-config.sh: docker compose config for every template.
  • shellcheck of the test scripts and template scripts.
  • actionlint (pinned image).
  • python -m unittest discover -s tests: the validator's own tests, including AITests (the ai: block rule for rule with the Hub's ValidateAI: both forms, companions, identity modes, reserved names and variables, trust networks, the ai.chat rules) and RootlessTests (the shared rootless vectors, the committed classification, PORTCULLIS_UNPRIVILEGED_PORT_START refused in templates, the expected refusals and limits).
  • Rootless classification. python tests/validate.py --rootless prints each template's rootless Podman status and reasons at port start 80; it must equal the committed tests/rootless.txt, so a change to the classification shows up in review. "Rootless vectors match the Hub" compares tests/rootless_vectors.json byte for byte with the Hub's internal/templates/testdata/rootless_vectors.json on the same-named Hub branch, else main.
